And the man rose to depart, he and his concubine and his servant, and his father-in-law, the father of the young woman, said to him, Behold now, toward evening the day has declined; lodge here still today, and let your heart be glad, and rise early tomorrow for your journey, and you will go to your tent.

**Judges 19:10**

But the man was not willing to lodge, and he rose and went away and came opposite Jebous, this is Jerusalem, and with him was a pair of saddled pack animals, and his concubine was with him.

**Judges 19:11**

While they were still near Jebous and the day had declined greatly, the servant said to his master, Come now and let us turn aside into this city of the Jebusite and lodge in it.

**Judges 19:12**

And his master said to him, I will certainly not turn aside into a city of foreigners who are not of the sons of Israel, but we will pass on as far as Gabaa.

**Judges 19:13**

And he said to his servant, Come and let us enter one of the places and lodge in Gabaa or in Rama.

**Judges 19:14**

And they passed by and went on, for the sun set near Gabaa, which belongs to Benjamin.

**Judges 19:15**

And they turned aside there to enter to lodge in Gabaa, and they entered and sat in the square of the city, and there was no man bringing them into the house to lodge.

**Judges 19:16**

And behold, an old man came in from his work out of the field at evening, and the man was from the hill-country of Ephraim and he resided in Gabaa, but the men of the place were sons of Benjamin.

**Judges 19:17**

And lifting up his eyes, he saw the traveling man in the square of the city, and the old man said, Where are you going and from where do you come?

**Judges 19:18**

And he said to him, We are passing through from Bethleem of Judah to the flanks of the hill-country of Ephraim; I am from there, and I went to Bethleem of Judah, and I am turning back to my house, and there is no man bringing me into the house.

**Judges 19:19**

And indeed there is straw and fodder for our donkeys, and there is bread and wine for me and for your maidservant and for the servant with your servants; there is no lack of anything.

**Judges 19:20**

And the old man said, Peace to you. Only let all your lack be upon me; only do not lodge in the square.

**Judges 19:21**

And he brought him into his house and fed his pack animals, and they washed their feet and ate and drank.

**Judges 19:22**

And while their hearts were gladdened, behold, the men of the city, sons of lawlessness, surrounded the house and beat on the door and said to the man, the master of the house, the old man, saying, Bring out the man who entered your house, so that we may know him.

**Judges 19:23**

And the man, the master of the house, went out to them and said to them, No, brothers, do not do evil, after this man has entered my house do not do this folly.

**Judges 19:24**

Behold, my virgin daughter and his concubine, I will bring them out now, and humble them and do to them what is good in your eyes, but to this man do not do this word of folly.

**Judges 19:25**

And the men were not willing to listen to him, and the man took hold of his concubine and brought her out to them outside, and they knew her and abused her all night until morning and sent her away when dawn was rising.

**Judges 19:26**

And the woman came toward morning and fell by the door of the gate of the man's house where her master was, until it became light.

**Judges 19:27**

And her master rose in the morning and opened the doors of the house and went out to go on his way, and behold, his concubine wife had fallen by the door, and her hands were on the threshold.

**Judges 19:28**

And he said to her, Rise and let us go. And she did not answer him, but had died. And he lifted her onto the pack animal, and the man rose and went to his place.

**Judges 19:29**

And he entered into his house and took the sword and took hold of his concubine and cut her up according to her bones into twelve parts and sent them into all the tribes of Israel.

**Judges 19:30**

And it came to be, everyone seeing said, Such a thing neither happened nor was seen from the day the sons of Israel came up from Egypt until this day. And he commanded the men to whom he sent them, saying, Thus you shall say to every man of Israel: Has this matter happened from the day the sons of Israel came up from Egypt until this day? Set counsel for yourselves about her and speak.

### Chapter 20

**Judges 20:1**

And all the sons of Israel went out, and all the congregation was assembled as one man from Dan and as far as Bersabee and the land of Gilead, to the Lord at Massēpha.

**Judges 20:2**

And the whole assembly of the people, all the tribes of Israel, stood in the gathering of the people of God, four hundred thousand foot men drawing sword.

**Judges 20:3**

And the sons of Benjamin heard that the sons of Israel had gone up to the Lord at Massēpha. And the sons of Israel said, Speak, where did this evil happen?

**Judges 20:4**

And the Levite man, husband of the murdered woman, answered and said, I came to Gabaa of Benjamin, I and my concubine, to lodge.

**Judges 20:5**

And the men from Gabaa rose against me and surrounded the house against me by night, and they wanted to kill me, and they humbled my concubine and abused her, and she died.

**Judges 20:6**

And I took hold of my concubine and cut her up and sent her through every border of the inheritance of Israel, because they committed folly in Israel.

**Judges 20:7**

Behold, all of you are sons of Israel; give to yourselves word and counsel.

**Judges 20:8**

And all the people rose as one man, saying, We will not go, man into his tent, and we will not turn aside, man to his house.

**Judges 20:9**

And now this is the word that we will do to Gabaa: we will go up against it by lot.

**Judges 20:10**

And we will take ten men by the hundred and a hundred by the thousand and a thousand by the ten thousand, to take provisions for the people, for those entering to execute against Gabaa of Benjamin according to all the folly that they did in Israel.

**Judges 20:11**

And all Israel, man from the cities, was gathered as one man, coming together.

**Judges 20:12**

And the tribes of Israel sent men in every tribe of Benjamin, saying, What is this evil that happened among you?

**Judges 20:13**

And now give the men, the ungodly ones in Gabaa, the sons of Belial, and we will put them to death and remove evil from Israel. But the sons of Benjamin were not willing to listen to the voice of their brothers, the sons of Israel.

**Judges 20:14**

And the sons of Benjamin were gathered from their cities to Gabaa to go out to fight with the sons of Israel.

**Judges 20:15**

And the sons of Benjamin were counted on that day from the cities, twenty-five thousand men drawing sword, besides the inhabitants of Gabaa; these were counted, seven hundred chosen young men.

**Judges 20:16**

All these were ambidextrous slingers, throwing stones at a hair and not missing.

**Judges 20:17**

And every man of Israel was counted apart from the sons of Benjamin, four hundred thousand men drawing sword; all these were men of war.

**Judges 20:18**

And they arose and went up to Baethel and inquired of God, and the sons of Israel said, Who will go up for us, leading to fight with Benjamin? And the Lord said, Judah shall go up, leading.

**Judges 20:19**

And the sons of Israel rose and encamped against Gabaa.

**Judges 20:20**

And every man of Israel went out to war with Benjamin, and the men of Israel lined up with them for battle against Gabaa.

**Judges 20:21**

And the sons of Benjamin went out from the city and destroyed from Israel on that day twenty-two thousand men to the ground.

**Judges 20:22**

And the men of Israel strengthened themselves and again lined up for battle in the place where they lined up on the first day.

**Judges 20:23**

And the sons of Israel went up and wept before the Lord until evening and inquired of the Lord, saying, Shall I again draw near to battle with Benjamin my brother? And the Lord said, Go up against him.

**Judges 20:24**

And the sons of Israel approached Benjamin on the second day.

**Judges 20:25**

And Benjamin went out from Gabaa to meet them on the second day and destroyed from the people eighteen thousand men to the ground, all these drawing sword.

**Judges 20:26**

And all the sons of Israel and all the people went up and came to Baethel and wept before the Lord and fasted on that day and offered whole burnt offerings of salvation before the Lord.

**Judges 20:27**

And the sons of Israel inquired of the Lord, and there the ark of the covenant of the Lord was in those days,

**Judges 20:28**

and Phinehas son of Eleazar son of Aaron stood before it in those days, saying, Shall I again go out to war with the sons of Benjamin my brother, or shall I cease? And the Lord said, Go up, because tomorrow I will give him into your hand.

**Judges 20:29**

And the sons of Israel set an ambush around Gabaa.

**Judges 20:30**

And Israel lined up against Benjamin on the third day and arrayed themselves against Gabaa as once and again.

**Judges 20:31**

And the sons of Benjamin went out to meet the people and were drawn away from the city and began to strike from the people as once and again on the roads, one going up to Baethel and one going up to Gabaa in the field, about thirty men in Israel.

**Judges 20:32**

And the sons of Benjamin said, They are stumbling before us as at first. But the sons of Israel said, Let us flee and draw them out from the city to the roads.

**Judges 20:33**

And every man of Israel rose from his place and arrayed themselves at Baalthamar, and the ambush of Israel came out from its place from the west of Gabaa.

**Judges 20:34**

And opposite Gabaa came ten thousand chosen men from all Israel, and the battle became heavy, and they did not know that evil was touching them.

**Judges 20:35**

And the Lord routed Benjamin before Israel, and the sons of Israel destroyed in Benjamin on that day twenty-five thousand one hundred men, all these drawing sword.

**Judges 20:36**

And Benjamin saw that it had been routed. And the men of Israel gave place to Benjamin because they relied on the ambush that they had set against Gabaa.

**Judges 20:37**

And the ambush rushed and spread out toward Gabaa, and the ambush went and struck the whole city with the edge of the sword.

**Judges 20:38**

And the signal between the men of Israel and the ambush was for them to bring up from the city a torch of smoke.

**Judges 20:39**

And the men of Israel turned in the battle, and Benjamin had begun striking down wounded men in Israel, about thirty men, because they said, Surely by defeat they are defeated before us as in the former battle.

**Judges 20:40**

And the torch began to go up from the city, a pillar of smoke, and Benjamin looked behind him, and behold, the whole destruction of the city went up to heaven.

**Judges 20:41**

And the men of Israel turned back, and the man of Benjamin was terrified, and he saw that evil had touched him.

**Judges 20:42**

And they turned before the men of Israel to the way of the wilderness, and the battle overtook him, and those from the cities destroyed him in their midst.

**Judges 20:43**

And they cut down Benjamin, giving him no rest, and trampled him down as far as opposite Gabaa from the east of the sun.

**Judges 20:44**

And there fell from Benjamin eighteen thousand men; with all these were mighty men.

**Judges 20:45**

And they turned aside and fled into the wilderness to the rock Rhemmon, and they gleaned five thousand men on the roads and clung after him as far as Gadaam and struck from them two thousand men.

**Judges 20:46**

And all those falling in Benjamin were twenty-five thousand men drawing sword on that day, with all these mighty men.

**Judges 20:47**

And six hundred men turned aside and fled into the wilderness to the rock Rhemmon and sat at the rock Rhemmon four months.

**Judges 20:48**

And the men of Israel shut in the sons of Benjamin and struck them with the edge of the sword from city onward to beast and to everything found; all the cities they found they sent out in fire.

### Chapter 21

**Judges 21:1**

And a man of Israel swore at Massēpha, saying, No man from us will give his daughter to Benjamin as wife.

**Judges 21:2**

And all the people came to Massēpha and Baethel and sat there until evening before God and lifted up their voice and wept with great weeping.

**Judges 21:3**

And they said, Why, Lord God of Israel, has this happened in Israel, that one tribe should be missing in Israel today?

**Judges 21:4**

And it came to be on the next day, the people rose early and built there an altar and offered whole burnt offerings of salvation.

**Judges 21:5**

And the sons of Israel said, Who is there that did not go up in the assembly from all the tribes of Israel to the Lord? For a great oath had been made against whoever did not go up to the Lord at Massēpha, saying, He shall surely die.

**Judges 21:6**

And the sons of Israel were moved concerning Benjamin their brother and said, One tribe has been taken away from Israel today.

**Judges 21:7**

What shall we do for those left for wives, since we swore by the Lord not to give them from our daughters as wives?

**Judges 21:8**

And they said, Which one from the tribes of Israel is it that did not go up to the Lord at Massēpha? And behold, no man had come from Jabis Gilead to the camp to the assembly.

**Judges 21:9**

And the people were counted, and behold, there was no man there from the inhabitants of Jabis Gilead.

**Judges 21:10**

And the congregation sent there twelve thousand men from the sons of might and commanded them, saying, Go and strike all dwelling in Jabis Gilead with the edge of the sword, and the women and the people.

**Judges 21:11**

And this is the word that you shall do: every male and every woman knowing the bed of a male you shall devote to destruction.

**Judges 21:12**

And they found from the inhabitants of Jabis Gilead four hundred young women, virgins who had not known man by the bed of a male, and they brought them to the camp at Shiloh, which is in the land of Canaan.

**Judges 21:13**

And all the congregation sent and spoke to Benjamin at the rock Rhemmon and called them to peace.

**Judges 21:14**

And Benjamin returned to the sons of Israel at that time, and they gave them the women who had been from the women of Jabis Gilead, and it pleased them thus.

**Judges 21:15**

And the people were moved for Benjamin because the Lord made a break in the tribes of Israel.

**Judges 21:16**

And the elders of the congregation said, What shall we do for the rest for wives, because woman has been wiped out from Benjamin?

**Judges 21:17**

And they said, A preserved inheritance belongs to Benjamin, and a tribe shall certainly not be blotted out from Israel.

**Judges 21:18**

And we are not able to give them wives from our daughters, because the sons of Israel swore, saying, Cursed is the one giving a wife to Benjamin.

**Judges 21:19**

And they said, Behold, a feast to the Lord at Shiloh from days to days, which is north of Baethel toward the rising of the sun, on the road going up from Baethel to Sikima, and south of Lebōna.

**Judges 21:20**

And they commanded the sons of Benjamin, saying, Go and lie in ambush in the vineyards.

**Judges 21:21**

And you shall watch, and behold, when the daughters of those dwelling in Shiloh come out in Shiloh to dance in dances, then you shall come out from the vineyards and each man seize for himself a wife from the daughters of Shiloh and go away to the land of Benjamin.

**Judges 21:22**

And it shall be when their fathers or their brothers come to contend with us, we will say to them, Show mercy to them, because not each man took his wife in the war. For you did not give to them at the proper time; otherwise you would have trespassed.

**Judges 21:23**

And the sons of Benjamin did so and took wives according to their number from the dancers whom they carried off, and they went away and returned to their inheritance and built for themselves cities and dwelt in them.

**Judges 21:24**

And the sons of Israel walked from there at that time, each man to his tribe and to his family, and each man went away from there to his inheritance.

**Judges 21:25**

In those days there was no king in Israel; each man did what was right in his own eyes.

## Ruth

### Chapter 1

**Ruth 1:1**

And it came to be in the judging of the judges, and there was famine in the land, and a man from Bethleem of Judah went to reside in the field of Moab, he and his wife and his sons.

**Ruth 1:2**

And the name of the man was Abimelech, and the name of his wife Noemin, and the names of his two sons Maalōn and Chelaiōn, Ephrathites from Bethleem of Judah, and they came into the field of Moab and were there.

**Ruth 1:3**

And Abimelech, husband of Noemin, died, and she was left, she and her two sons.

**Ruth 1:4**

And they took for themselves Moabite women; the name of the one was Orpha and the name of the second Ruth, and they dwelt there about ten years.

**Ruth 1:5**

And both Maalōn and Chelaiōn also died, and the woman was left without her husband and without her two sons.

**Ruth 1:6**

And she rose, she and her two daughters-in-law, and they returned from the field of Moab, because she heard in the field of Moab that the Lord had visited his people to give them bread.

**Ruth 1:7**

And she went out from the place where she had been there, and her two daughters-in-law with her, and they were going on the road to return to the land of Judah.

**Ruth 1:8**

And Noemin said to her daughters-in-law, Go now, return each to her mother's house. May the Lord deal with you in mercy, as you dealt with the dead and with me.

**Ruth 1:9**

May the Lord give to you, and may each of you find rest in the house of her husband. And she kissed them, and they lifted up their voice and wept.

**Ruth 1:10**

And they said to her, With you we will return to your people.

**Ruth 1:11**

And Noemin said, Return now, my daughters. Why are you going with me? Are there yet sons in my womb, and will they be husbands for you?

**Ruth 1:12**

Return now, my daughters, because I have grown old, not to belong to a husband. For if I said, There is hope for me to belong to a husband and bear sons,

**Ruth 1:13**

would you wait for them until they grow up? Or would you be restrained on account of them from belonging to a husband? No, my daughters, because it has become very bitter for me concerning you, because the hand of the Lord has gone out against me.

**Ruth 1:14**

And they lifted up their voice and wept again, and Orpha kissed her mother-in-law and returned to her people, but Ruth followed her.

**Ruth 1:15**

And Noemin said to Ruth, Behold, your fellow daughter-in-law turned back to her people and to her gods. Turn back now, you also, after your fellow daughter-in-law.

**Ruth 1:16**

And Ruth said, Do not press me to leave you or to turn back from behind you, because wherever you go, I will go, and wherever you lodge, I will lodge. Your people shall be my people, and your God my God.

**Ruth 1:17**

And wherever you die, I will die, and there I will be buried. Thus may the Lord do to me, and thus may he add, because only death will divide between me and you.

**Ruth 1:18**

And Noemin saw that she was strong in going with her, and she ceased speaking to her any more.

**Ruth 1:19**

And both of them went until they came to Bethleem, and all the city sounded over them, and they said, Is this Noemin?

**Ruth 1:20**

And she said to them, Do not call me Noemin; call me Bitter, because the Mighty One has made things very bitter in me.

**Ruth 1:21**

I went away full, and the Lord brought me back empty. And why do you call me Noemin, when the Lord humbled me and the Mighty One afflicted me?

**Ruth 1:22**

And Noemin returned, and Ruth the Moabitess her daughter-in-law with her, returning from the field of Moab. And they came to Bethleem at the beginning of barley harvest.

### Chapter 2

**Ruth 2:1**

And for Noemin there was a known man to her husband, and the man was mighty in strength from the kindred of Abimelech, and his name was Boos.

**Ruth 2:2**

And Ruth the Moabitess said to Noemin, Let me now go to the field and glean among the ears behind whoever I find favor in his eyes. And she said to her, Go, daughter.

**Ruth 2:3**

And she went and gleaned in the field behind the reapers, and it happened by chance upon the portion of the field of Boos, who was from the kindred of Abimelech.

**Ruth 2:4**

And behold, Boos came from Bethleem and said to the reapers, The Lord be with you. And they said to him, May the Lord bless you.

**Ruth 2:5**

And Boos said to his young servant set over the reapers, Whose young woman is this?

**Ruth 2:6**

And the young servant set over the reapers answered and said, She is the Moabite girl who returned with Noemin from the field of Moab.

**Ruth 2:7**

And she said, Let me now glean and gather among the sheaves behind the reapers. And she came and has stood from early morning until evening; she did not rest in the field except a little.

**Ruth 2:8**

And Boos said to Ruth, Have you not heard, daughter? Do not go to another field to glean, and do not go from here. Here stay close with my girls.

**Ruth 2:9**

Let your eyes be on the field where they reap, and go behind them. Behold, I commanded the young men not to touch you, and whenever you thirst, go to the vessels and drink from where the young men draw water.

**Ruth 2:10**

And she fell on her face and bowed to the ground and said to him, Why did I find favor in your eyes, that you should notice me, when I am a foreign woman?

**Ruth 2:11**

And Boos answered and said to her, It was fully reported to me all that you have done with your mother-in-law after the death of your husband, and how you left your father and your mother and the land of your birth and went to a people you did not know yesterday or the day before.

**Ruth 2:12**

May the Lord repay your work, and may your wage be full from the Lord God of Israel, under whose wings you came to trust.

**Ruth 2:13**

And she said, May I find favor in your eyes, lord, because you comforted me and because you spoke to the heart of your servant, and behold, I shall be as one of your maidservants.

**Ruth 2:14**

And Boos said to her, Already it is time to eat; come here and eat of the bread and dip your morsel in the vinegar. And Ruth sat beside the reapers, and Boos heaped parched grain for her, and she ate and was filled and left some.

**Ruth 2:15**

And she rose to glean, and Boos commanded his young men, saying, Indeed let her glean even among the sheaves, and do not shame her.

**Ruth 2:16**

And in carrying, carry for her; indeed in dropping, drop for her from the armfuls and leave them, and she will glean, and you shall not rebuke her.

**Ruth 2:17**

And she gleaned in the field until evening and beat out what she had gleaned, and it came to be about an ephah of barley.

**Ruth 2:18**

And she took it and went into the city, and her mother-in-law saw what she had gleaned. And Ruth brought out and gave to her what she had left from what satisfied her.

**Ruth 2:19**

And her mother-in-law said to her, Where did you glean today, and where did you work? Blessed be the one noticing you. And Ruth reported to her mother-in-law where she worked and said, The name of the man with whom I worked today is Boos.

**Ruth 2:20**

And Noemin said to her daughter-in-law, Blessed is he by the Lord, because he did not forsake his mercy with the living and with the dead. And Noemin said to her, The man is near to us; he is from those redeeming us.

**Ruth 2:21**

And Ruth said to her mother-in-law, Indeed he also said to me, Stay close with my young men until they finish all the harvest that belongs to me.

**Ruth 2:22**

And Noemin said to Ruth her daughter-in-law, It is good, daughter, that you went with his girls, and they will not meet you in another field.

**Ruth 2:23**

And Ruth stayed close to the girls of Boos, gleaning until the barley harvest and the wheat harvest were finished, and she lived with her mother-in-law.

### Chapter 3

**Ruth 3:1**

And Noemin her mother-in-law said to her, Daughter, shall I not seek rest for you, so that it may be well with you?

**Ruth 3:2**

And now, is not Boos our kinsman, with whose girls you were? Behold, he winnows the threshing floor of barley tonight.

**Ruth 3:3**

And you shall wash and anoint yourself and put your garment upon yourself and go up to the threshing floor. Do not make yourself known to the man until he finishes eating and drinking.

**Ruth 3:4**

And it shall be when he lies down, you will know the place where he lies there, and you will come and uncover the things at his feet and lie down, and he will tell you what you shall do.

**Ruth 3:5**

And Ruth said to her, Everything that you say I will do.

**Ruth 3:6**

And she went down to the threshing floor and did according to all that her mother-in-law commanded her.

**Ruth 3:7**

And Boos ate and his heart was made glad, and he came to lie down at the edge of the heap, and she came secretly and uncovered the things at his feet.

**Ruth 3:8**

And it happened at midnight, and the man was startled and disturbed, and behold, a woman lay at his feet.

**Ruth 3:9**

And he said, Who are you? And she said, I am Ruth your servant, and you shall spread your wing over your servant, because you are a redeemer.

**Ruth 3:10**

And he said, Blessed are you by the Lord God, daughter, because you made your latter mercy better than the first, by not going after young men, whether poor or rich.

**Ruth 3:11**

And now, daughter, do not fear. Everything that you say I will do for you, for every tribe of my people knows that you are a woman of strength.

**Ruth 3:12**

And now, truly I am a redeemer, and yet there is a redeemer nearer than I.

**Ruth 3:13**

Lodge here tonight, and it shall be in the morning, if he redeems you, good, let him redeem; but if he does not want to redeem you, I will redeem you, as the Lord lives. Sleep until morning.

**Ruth 3:14**

And she slept at his feet until morning, and she rose before one man could recognize his neighbor. And Boos said, Let it not be known that a woman came to the threshing floor.

**Ruth 3:15**

And he said to her, Bring the mantle that is upon you. And she held it, and he measured six of barley and put it on her, and she went into the city.

**Ruth 3:16**

And Ruth entered to her mother-in-law, and she said, Who are you, daughter? And she told her everything that the man did for her.

**Ruth 3:17**

And she said to her, He gave me these six of barley, because he said to me, Do not enter empty to your mother-in-law.

**Ruth 3:18**

And she said, Sit, daughter, until you know how the matter will fall, for the man will certainly not rest until he completes the matter today.

### Chapter 4

**Ruth 4:1**

And Boos went up to the gate and sat there, and behold, the redeemer was passing by whom Boos had spoken of, and Boos said to him, Turn aside, sit here, hidden one. And he turned aside and sat.

**Ruth 4:2**

And Boos took ten men from the elders of the city and said, Sit here. And they sat.

**Ruth 4:3**

And Boos said to the redeemer, The portion of the field that belongs to our brother Abimelech is being given to Noemin who returned from the field of Moab.

**Ruth 4:4**

And I said, I will uncover your ear, saying, Buy it before those sitting here and before the elders of my people. If you redeem, redeem; but if you do not redeem, tell me, and I will know, because there is none besides you to redeem, and I am after you. And he said, I am; I will redeem.

**Ruth 4:5**

And Boos said, On the day of your acquiring the field from the hand of Noemin, and from Ruth the Moabitess, wife of the dead man, it is necessary for you also to acquire her for yourself, so as to raise up the name of the dead over his inheritance.

**Ruth 4:6**

And the redeemer said, I will not be able to redeem for myself, lest I ruin my own inheritance. Redeem my redemption-right for yourself, because I will not be able to redeem.

**Ruth 4:7**

And this was the custom formerly in Israel concerning redemption and concerning exchange, to establish every word: a man would loosen his sandal and give it to his neighbor redeeming his right, and this was a witness in Israel.

**Ruth 4:8**

And the redeemer said to Boos, Acquire my redemption-right for yourself, and he loosened his sandal and gave it to him.

**Ruth 4:9**

And Boos said to the elders and to all the people, You are witnesses today that I acquired everything of Abimelech and everything belonging to Chelaiōn and to Maalōn from the hand of Noemin.

**Ruth 4:10**

And indeed Ruth the Moabitess, wife of Maalōn, I acquired for myself as wife, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, and the name of the dead shall not be blotted out from among his brothers and from the tribe of his people. You are witnesses today.

**Ruth 4:11**

And all the people at the gate said, Witnesses. And the elders said, May the Lord make your wife entering into your house like Rachel and like Leia, who both built the house of Israel, and may they make strength in Ephratha, and may your name be in Bethleem.

**Ruth 4:12**

And may your house become like the house of Phares, whom Thamar bore to Judah, from the seed that the Lord will give you from this servant girl.

**Ruth 4:13**

And Boos took Ruth, and she became his wife, and he went in to her, and the Lord gave her conception, and she bore a son.

**Ruth 4:14**

And the women said to Noemin, Blessed be the Lord, who did not leave you without a redeemer today, and may your name be called in Israel.

**Ruth 4:15**

And he shall be for you a restoring of soul and to nourish your old age, because your daughter-in-law who loved you bore him, she who is good to you beyond seven sons.

**Ruth 4:16**

And Noemin took the child and placed him in her bosom, and she became nurse to him.

**Ruth 4:17**

And the neighboring women called his name, saying, A son has been born to Noemin, and they called his name Ōbēd; he is father of Jessai, father of David.

**Ruth 4:18**

And these are the generations of Phares: Phares fathered Esrōn,

**Ruth 4:19**

and Esrōn fathered Arran, and Arran fathered Aminadab,

**Ruth 4:20**

and Aminadab fathered Naassōn, and Naassōn fathered Salman,

**Ruth 4:21**

and Salman fathered Boos, and Boos fathered Ōbēd,

**Ruth 4:22**

and Ōbēd fathered Jessai, and Jessai fathered David.

## 1 Samuel

### Chapter 1

**1 Samuel 1:1**

There was a man from Armathaim Siphā, from the hill-country of Ephraim, and his name was Elkana, son of Ieremeēl, son of Eliou, son of Thoke, in Nasib Ephraim.

**1 Samuel 1:2**

And to him were two wives; the name of the one was Anna and the name of the second Phennana, and Phennana had children, but Anna had no child.

**1 Samuel 1:3**

And the man went up from days to days from his city, from Armathaim, to bow down and sacrifice to the Lord God Sabaōth at Shilō, and there were Heli and his two sons, Ophni and Phinees, priests of the Lord.

**1 Samuel 1:4**

And it came to be on the day Elkana sacrificed, that he gave to Phennana his wife and to her sons and her daughters portions,

**1 Samuel 1:5**

but to Anna he gave one portion, because she had no child; yet Elkana loved Anna beyond this one, and the Lord had closed the things of her womb.

**1 Samuel 1:6**

Because the Lord had not given her a child, according to her affliction and according to the discouragement of her affliction, and because of this she was disheartened, because the Lord had shut the things of her womb from giving her a child.

**1 Samuel 1:7**

Thus he did year by year, when she went up to the house of the Lord, and she was disheartened and wept and did not eat.

**1 Samuel 1:8**

And Elkana her husband said to her, Anna. And she said to him, Behold, here I am, lord. And he said to her, What is wrong with you, that you weep, and why do you not eat, and why does your heart strike you? Am I not good to you beyond ten children?

**1 Samuel 1:9**

And Anna rose after they ate in Shilō and stood before the Lord, and Heli the priest was sitting upon the seat by the posts of the temple of the Lord.

**1 Samuel 1:10**

And she was bitter in soul and prayed to the Lord, and weeping she wept.

**1 Samuel 1:11**

And she vowed a vow to the Lord, saying, Adōnai, Lord Elōai Sabaōth, if in looking you look upon the humiliation of your servant and remember me and give to your servant seed of men, then I will give him before you as a given thing until the day of his death, and wine and intoxicating drink he shall not drink, and iron shall not come upon his head.

**1 Samuel 1:12**

And it came to be, while she multiplied in praying before the Lord, Heli the priest watched her mouth.

**1 Samuel 1:13**

And she was speaking in her heart, and her lips were moving, but her voice was not heard, and Heli counted her as a drunken woman.

**1 Samuel 1:14**

And the servant Heli said to her, How long will you be drunk? Put away your wine and go from the presence of the Lord.

**1 Samuel 1:15**

And Anna answered and said, No, lord. I am a woman of hard day, and I have not drunk wine or intoxicating drink, but I pour out my soul before the Lord.

**1 Samuel 1:16**

Do not give your servant as a daughter of pestilence, because out of the abundance of my musing I have stretched on until now.

**1 Samuel 1:17**

And Heli answered and said to her, Go in peace. The God of Israel give you every request of yours that you asked from him.

**1 Samuel 1:18**

And she said, Your servant found favor in your eyes. And the woman went on her way and entered into her lodging and ate with her husband and drank, and her face did not fall any more.

**1 Samuel 1:19**

And they rose early in the morning and bowed down to the Lord and went on their way, and Elkana entered into his house at Armathaim and knew Anna his wife, and the Lord remembered her.

**1 Samuel 1:20**

And she conceived, and it came to be at the turn of the days, that she bore a son and called his name Samouēl, and said, Because from the Lord God Sabaōth I asked him.

**1 Samuel 1:21**

And the man Elkana went up, and all his house, to sacrifice in Shilōm the sacrifice of the days and his vows and all the tithes of his land.

**1 Samuel 1:22**

But Anna did not go up with him, because she said to her husband, Until the child goes up, when I wean him, then he will be seen before the face of the Lord and sit there forever.

**1 Samuel 1:23**

And Elkana her husband said to her, Do what is good in your eyes; sit until you wean him. Only may the Lord establish what went out from your mouth. And the woman sat and nursed her son until she weaned him.

**1 Samuel 1:24**

And she went up with him to Shilōm with a three-year-old calf and breads and an ephah of fine flour and a skin of wine, and she entered into the house of the Lord in Shilōm, and the child was with them.

**1 Samuel 1:25**

And they brought him before the Lord, and his father slaughtered the sacrifice that he made from days to days to the Lord, and he brought the child and slaughtered the calf, and Anna, the mother of the child, brought him to Heli.

**1 Samuel 1:26**

And she said, In me, lord, your soul lives: I am the woman who stood before you in praying to the Lord.

**1 Samuel 1:27**

For this child I prayed, and the Lord gave me my request that I asked from him.

**1 Samuel 1:28**

And I lend him to the Lord all the days that he lives, a use to the Lord.

### Chapter 2

**1 Samuel 2:1**

And she said, My heart was strengthened in the Lord, my horn was lifted up in my God, my mouth was widened against enemies, I rejoiced in your salvation.

**1 Samuel 2:2**

Because there is no holy one like the Lord, and there is none righteous like our God; there is no holy one besides you.

**1 Samuel 2:3**

Do not boast and do not speak lofty things; let no big speaking go out from your mouth, because the Lord is a God of knowings and a God preparing his practices.

**1 Samuel 2:4**

The bow of the mighty weakened, and the weak girded themselves with strength.

**1 Samuel 2:5**

Those full of breads were made less, and the hungry left the land, because the barren one bore seven, and the one many in children became weak.

**1 Samuel 2:6**

The Lord kills and makes alive; he brings down to Hades and brings up.

**1 Samuel 2:7**

The Lord makes poor and makes rich, humbles and lifts up.

**1 Samuel 2:8**

He raises the poor from the earth and lifts the needy from the dung heap, to seat him with rulers of peoples and to allot to them a throne of glory.

**1 Samuel 2:9**

Giving prayer to the one praying, and he blessed the years of the righteous, because not by strength is a man mighty.

**1 Samuel 2:10**

The Lord will make his adversary weak; the Lord is holy. Let not the wise boast in his wisdom, and let not the strong boast in his strength, and let not the rich boast in his wealth, but in this let the boasting one boast: to understand and know the Lord and to do judgment and righteousness in the midst of the earth. The Lord went up into the heavens and thundered; he will judge the ends of the earth and gives strength to our kings and will lift up the horn of his anointed.

**1 Samuel 2:11**

And they left him there before the Lord and went away to Armathaim, and the child was ministering before the face of the Lord before Heli the priest.

**1 Samuel 2:12**

And the sons of Heli the priest were sons of pestilence, not knowing the Lord.

**1 Samuel 2:13**

And the ordinance of the priest from the people, everyone sacrificing, was this: the servant of the priest came while the meat was boiling, and a three-pronged flesh-hook was in his hand,

**1 Samuel 2:14**

and he struck it into the great cauldron or into the bronze pot or into the cooking pot. Everything that came up with the flesh-hook the priest took for himself. According to these things they were doing to all Israel who came to sacrifice to the Lord in Shilōm.

**1 Samuel 2:15**

And before the fat was burned, the servant of the priest came and said to the man sacrificing, Give meat for roasting to the priest, and I will certainly not take boiled meat from you out of the cauldron.

**1 Samuel 2:16**

And the sacrificing man said, Let the fat first be burned as is proper, and take for yourself from everything your soul desires. And he said, No, because you shall give now, and if not, I will take by force.

**1 Samuel 2:17**

And the sin of the young servants before the Lord was very great, because they were despising the sacrifice of the Lord.

**1 Samuel 2:18**

And Samouēl was ministering before the Lord, a child girded with a linen ephod.

**1 Samuel 2:19**

And his mother made for him a small doublet and brought it up to him from days to days when she went up with her husband to sacrifice the sacrifice of the days.

**1 Samuel 2:20**

And Heli blessed Elkana and his wife, saying, May the Lord repay you seed from this woman in place of the loan that you loaned to the Lord. And the man went to his place.

**1 Samuel 2:21**

And the Lord visited Anna, and she bore yet three sons and two daughters, and the child Samouēl was magnified before the Lord.

**1 Samuel 2:22**

And Heli was very old and heard what his sons were doing to the sons of Israel.

**1 Samuel 2:23**

And he said to them, Why are you doing according to this word that I hear from the mouth of all the people of the Lord?

**1 Samuel 2:24**

No, children, because the report that I hear is not good. Do not do so, because the reports that I hear are not good, of the people not serving God.

**1 Samuel 2:25**

If a man sins by sinning against a man, then they will pray concerning him to the Lord, but if someone sins against the Lord, who will pray concerning him? And they were not listening to the voice of their father, because the Lord deliberately desired to destroy them.

**1 Samuel 2:26**

And the child Samouēl was going on and growing and good both with the Lord and with men.

**1 Samuel 2:27**

And a man of God came to Heli and said, Thus says the Lord: In revealing did I reveal myself to the house of your father while they were in the land of Egypt, servants to the house of Pharaoh?

**1 Samuel 2:28**

And I chose the house of your father from all the scepters of Israel for myself, to serve as priest and to go up upon my altar and to burn incense and to lift the ephod, and I gave to the house of your father all the fire-offerings of the sons of Israel for food.

**1 Samuel 2:29**

And why did you look upon my incense and upon my sacrifice with shameless eye, and glorify your sons beyond me, to bless yourselves from the firstfruits of every sacrifice of Israel before me?

**1 Samuel 2:30**

Because of this thus said the Lord God of Israel: I said, Your house and the house of your father will pass before me forever. And now, says the Lord, let it not be to me; rather those glorifying me I will glorify, and the one despising me will be dishonored.

**1 Samuel 2:31**

Behold, days are coming, and I will destroy your seed and the seed of your father's house.

**1 Samuel 2:32**

And there shall not be an old man of yours in my house all the days.

**1 Samuel 2:33**

And a man I will not destroy for you from my altar, to fail his eyes and make his soul melt away, and everyone remaining of your house shall fall by the sword of men.

**1 Samuel 2:34**

And this will be the sign to you that will come upon these your two sons, Ophni and Phinees: in one day both will die.

**1 Samuel 2:35**

And I will raise up for myself a faithful priest, who will do all the things in my heart and the things in my soul, and I will build for him a faithful house, and he will pass before my anointed all the days.

**1 Samuel 2:36**

And it shall be that the one left over in your house will come to bow down to him for an obol of silver, saying, Cast me beside one of your priesthoods that I may eat bread.

### Chapter 3

**1 Samuel 3:1**

And the child Samouēl was ministering to the Lord before Heli the priest, and the word of the Lord was precious in those days; there was no vision making distinction.

**1 Samuel 3:2**

And it came to be on that day, and Heli was sleeping in his place, and his eyes began to grow heavy and he was not able to see.

**1 Samuel 3:3**

And the lamp of God was before being set in order, and Samouēl was sleeping in the temple where the ark of God was.

**1 Samuel 3:4**

And the Lord called, Samouēl, Samouēl. And he said, Behold, here I am.

**1 Samuel 3:5**

And he ran to Heli and said, Behold, here I am, because you called me. And he said, I did not call you; go back, sleep. And he went back and slept.

**1 Samuel 3:6**

And the Lord added and called, Samouēl, Samouēl. And he went to Heli a second time and said, Behold, here I am, because you called me. And he said, I did not call you; go back, sleep.

**1 Samuel 3:7**

And Samouēl was before knowing God and before the word of the Lord was revealed to him.

**1 Samuel 3:8**

And the Lord added to call Samouēl a third time, and he rose and went to Heli and said, Behold, here I am, because you called me. And Heli understood that the Lord had called the child.

**1 Samuel 3:9**

And he said, Go back, sleep, child, and it shall be if he calls you, then you shall say, Speak, Lord, because your servant hears. And Samouēl went and lay down in his place.

**1 Samuel 3:10**

And the Lord came and stood and called him as once and again, and Samouēl said, Speak, because your servant hears.

**1 Samuel 3:11**

And the Lord said to Samouēl, Behold, I am doing my words in Israel, so that whoever hears them, both his ears will ring.

**1 Samuel 3:12**

In that day I will raise upon Heli all that I spoke against his house; I will begin and I will complete.

**1 Samuel 3:13**

And I have announced to him that I am avenging his house forever for the injustices of his sons, because his sons were blaspheming God and he was not warning them, not even so.

**1 Samuel 3:14**

I swore to the house of Heli whether the injustice of the house of Heli will be propitiated by incense and by sacrifices forever.

**1 Samuel 3:15**

And Samouēl slept until morning and rose early in the morning and opened the doors of the house of the Lord, and Samouēl feared to report the vision to Heli.

**1 Samuel 3:16**

And Heli said to Samouēl, Samouēl, child. And he said, Behold, here I am.

**1 Samuel 3:17**

And he said, What is the word spoken to you? Do not hide it from me. Thus may God do to you and thus may he add, if you hide from me a word of all the words spoken to you in your ears.

**1 Samuel 3:18**

And Samouēl reported all the words and did not hide from him, and Heli said, He is the Lord; what is good before him he will do.

**1 Samuel 3:19**

And Samouēl grew great, and the Lord was with him, and not one of all his words fell to the ground.

**1 Samuel 3:20**

And all Israel knew, from Dan and as far as Bersabee, that Samouēl was faithful as prophet to the Lord.

**1 Samuel 3:21**

And the Lord again made himself known in Shilōm, because the Lord was revealed to Samouēl, and Samouēl was entrusted to become prophet to the Lord for all Israel from end of the land to end. And Heli was very old, and his sons were going on and their way was evil before the Lord.

### Chapter 4

**1 Samuel 4:1**

And it came to be in those days, and foreigners were gathered for war against Israel, and Israel went out to meet them for war, and they camped by Abenezēr, and the foreigners camped in Aphek.

**1 Samuel 4:2**

And the foreigners lined up for battle against Israel, and the battle turned, and a man of Israel stumbled before the foreigners, and four thousand men were struck down in battle in the field.

**1 Samuel 4:3**

And the people came into the camp, and the elders of Israel said, Why did the Lord make us stumble today before the foreigners? Let us take the ark of our God from Shilōm, and let it come out in our midst and save us from the hand of our enemies.

**1 Samuel 4:4**

And the people sent to Shilōm, and they took from there the ark of the Lord seated on cherubim, and both sons of Heli were with the ark, Ophni and Phinees.

**1 Samuel 4:5**

And it came to be, when the ark of the Lord came into the camp, all Israel cried out with a great voice, and the earth resounded.

**1 Samuel 4:6**

And the foreigners heard the sound of the cry and said, What is this great cry in the camp of the Hebrews? And they knew that the ark of the Lord had come into the camp.

**1 Samuel 4:7**

And the foreigners were afraid and said, These gods have come to them into the camp. Woe to us, Lord, rescue us today, because such a thing has not happened yesterday or the day before.

**1 Samuel 4:8**

Woe to us. Who will rescue us from the hand of these strong gods? These are the gods who struck Egypt with every plague and in the wilderness.

**1 Samuel 4:9**

Be strong and become men, foreigners, lest you serve the Hebrews as they served us. And become men and fight them.

**1 Samuel 4:10**

And they fought them, and a man of Israel stumbled, and each fled to his tent, and there was a very great blow, and thirty thousand ranks fell from Israel.

**1 Samuel 4:11**

And the ark of God was taken, and both sons of Heli died, Ophni and Phinees.

**1 Samuel 4:12**

And a Jeminite man ran from the battle line and came to Shilōm on that day, and his garments were torn and earth was on his head.

**1 Samuel 4:13**

And he came, and behold, Heli was sitting on the seat by the gate, watching the road, because his heart was beside itself concerning the ark of God. And the man entered into the city to report, and the city cried out.

**1 Samuel 4:14**

And Heli heard the sound of the outcry and said, What is this cry of this sound? And the man hurried and entered and reported to Heli.

**1 Samuel 4:15**

And Heli was ninety years old, and his eyes had become fixed, and he did not see, and Heli said to the men standing around him, What is the voice of this sound?

**1 Samuel 4:16**

And the man hurried and came near to Heli and said to him, I am the one coming from the camp, and I fled from the battle line today. And he said, What is the matter, child?

**1 Samuel 4:17**

And the young servant answered and said, A man of Israel fled from before the foreigners, and there was a great blow among the people, and both your sons have died, and the ark of God has been taken.

**1 Samuel 4:18**

And it came to be, when he mentioned the ark of God, he fell from the seat backward near the gate, and his back was broken and he died, because the man was old and heavy, and he judged Israel twenty years.

**1 Samuel 4:19**

And his daughter-in-law, wife of Phinees, had conceived to give birth, and she heard the news that the ark of God had been taken and that her father-in-law and her husband had died, and she crouched down and gave birth, because her labor pains turned upon her.

**1 Samuel 4:20**

And at the time of her dying the women standing by her said to her, Do not fear, because you have borne a son. But she did not answer, and her heart did not understand.

**1 Samuel 4:21**

And she called the child Ouai Barchabōth because of the ark of God and because of her father-in-law and because of her husband.

**1 Samuel 4:22**

And they said, Glory has departed from Israel in the taking of the ark of the Lord.

### Chapter 5

**1 Samuel 5:1**

And the foreigners took the ark of God and brought it in from Abennezēr to Azotus.

**1 Samuel 5:2**

And the foreigners took the ark of the Lord and brought it into the house of Dagon and set it beside Dagon.

**1 Samuel 5:3**

And the Azotians rose early and entered into the house of Dagon, and behold, Dagon had fallen on his face before the ark of God. And they raised up Dagon and set him in his place, and the hand of the Lord grew heavy upon the Azotians, and he tormented them and struck them in their seats, Azotus and its borders.

**1 Samuel 5:4**

And it came to be when they rose early in the morning, behold, Dagon had fallen on his face before the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and the head of Dagon and both the prints of his hands were removed upon the front threshold, each one, and both palms of his hands had fallen on the threshold; only the back of Dagon was left.

**1 Samuel 5:5**

Because of this the priests of Dagon and everyone entering the house of Dagon do not step upon the step of the house of Dagon in Azotus until this day, because in passing over they pass over it.

**1 Samuel 5:6**

And the hand of the Lord grew heavy upon Azotus and brought upon them and boiled out for them in their ships, and in the midst of its region mice sprang up, and there was a great confusion of death in the city.

**1 Samuel 5:7**

And the men of Azotus saw that it was so and said, The ark of the God of Israel will not remain with us, because his hand is hard upon us and upon Dagon our god.

**1 Samuel 5:8**

And they sent and gathered the satraps of the foreigners to them and said, What shall we do with the ark of the God of Israel? And the Gittites said, Let the ark of God come over to us. And the ark of God came over to Geththa.

**1 Samuel 5:9**

And it came to be after it came over, the hand of the Lord was in the city, a very great disturbance, and he struck the men of the city from small to great and struck them in their seats, and the Gittites made seats for themselves.

**1 Samuel 5:10**

And they sent away the ark of God to Ascalon, and it came to be when the ark of God entered into Ascalon, the Ascalonites cried out, saying, Why did you return to us the ark of the God of Israel, to kill us and our people?

**1 Samuel 5:11**

And they sent and gathered the satraps of the foreigners and said, Send away the ark of the God of Israel, and let it sit in its place, and it shall certainly not kill us and our people, because there was confusion of death in the whole city, very heavy, as the ark of the God of Israel entered there.

**1 Samuel 5:12**

And the living who did not die were struck in their seats, and the cry of the city went up to heaven.

### Chapter 6

**1 Samuel 6:1**

And the ark was in the field of the foreigners seven months, and their land boiled out mice.

**1 Samuel 6:2**

And the foreigners call the priests and their diviners and enchanters, saying, What shall we do with the ark of the Lord? Make known to us in what way we shall send it to its place.

**1 Samuel 6:3**

And they said, If you send away the ark of the covenant of the Lord God of Israel, by no means send it away empty, but in repaying repay it for the torment, and then you will be healed and it will be propitiated for you. Will not his hand depart from you?

**1 Samuel 6:4**

And they say, What is the thing of torment that we shall repay to it? And they said, According to the number of the satraps of the foreigners, five golden seats, because the same fall is on you and on your rulers and on the people.

**1 Samuel 6:5**

And golden mice, likeness of your mice destroying the land, and you shall give glory to the Lord, so that he may lighten his hand from you and from your gods and from your land.

**1 Samuel 6:6**

And why do you harden your hearts as Egypt and Pharaoh hardened their hearts? Was it not when he mocked them that they sent them away and they went?

**1 Samuel 6:7**

And now take and make a new wagon and two first-calving cows apart from their calves, and yoke the cows to the wagon and lead away the calves from behind them into the house.

**1 Samuel 6:8**

And you will take the ark and put it on the wagon, and the gold objects that you repay to it for the torment you shall place in a chest beside it, and you shall send it away and drive it out, and it will go.

**1 Samuel 6:9**

**1 Samuel 6:10**

And the foreigners did so, and they took two first-calving cows and yoked them to the wagon, and they shut up their calves in the house.

**1 Samuel 6:11**

And they set the ark upon the wagon and the chest Ergab and the gold mice.

**1 Samuel 6:12**

And the cows went straight on the road, on the road to Baithsamyis, in one path they went, and they toiled and did not turn aside right or left, and the satraps of the foreigners went after it until the borders of Baithsamyis.

**1 Samuel 6:13**

And those in Baithsamyis were reaping wheat harvest in the valley, and they lifted up their eyes and saw the ark of the Lord and rejoiced to meet it.

**1 Samuel 6:14**

And the wagon came into the field of Ōsēe in Baithsamyis, and they stood there by a great stone, and they split the wood of the wagon and offered the cows as a whole burnt offering to the Lord.

**1 Samuel 6:15**

And the Levites brought up the ark of the Lord and the chest Ergab with it and the gold items upon it and placed them on the great stone, and the men of Baithsamyis offered whole burnt offerings and sacrifices on that day to the Lord.

**1 Samuel 6:16**

And the five satraps of the foreigners saw and returned to Ascalon on that day.

**1 Samuel 6:17**

And these are the golden seats that the foreigners repaid to the Lord for the torment: one for Azotus, one for Gaza, one for Ascalon, one for Geth, one for Akkaron,

**1 Samuel 6:18**

and the golden mice according to the number of all the cities of the foreigners of the five satraps, from fortified city and to village of the Perizzite, and to the great stone on which they placed the ark of the covenant of the Lord, the one in the field of Ōsēe the Baithsamyisite.

**1 Samuel 6:19**

And the sons of Iechoniou were not pleased among the men of Baithsamyis because they saw the ark of the Lord, and he struck among them seventy men and fifty thousand men, and the people mourned because the Lord struck the people with a very great blow.

**1 Samuel 6:20**

And the men from Baithsamyis said, Who will be able to go through before this holy Lord, and to whom will the ark of the Lord go up from us?

**1 Samuel 6:21**

### Chapter 7

**1 Samuel 7:1**

**1 Samuel 7:2**

And it came to be from the day the ark was in Kariathiarim, the days multiplied and became twenty years, and all the house of Israel looked after the Lord.

**1 Samuel 7:3**

And Samouēl said to all the house of Israel, saying, If with your whole heart you are turning to the Lord, remove the foreign gods from your midst and the groves, and prepare your hearts toward the Lord and serve him alone, and he will deliver you from the hand of the foreigners.

**1 Samuel 7:4**

And the sons of Israel removed the Baals and the groves of Astarōth and served the Lord alone.

**1 Samuel 7:5**

And Samouēl said, Gather all Israel to Massēphath, and I will pray concerning you to the Lord.

**1 Samuel 7:6**

**1 Samuel 7:7**

And the foreigners heard that all the sons of Israel had gathered to Massēphath, and the satraps of the foreigners went up against Israel. And the sons of Israel heard and feared from before the foreigners.

**1 Samuel 7:8**

And the sons of Israel said to Samouēl, Do not be silent away from us from crying to the Lord your God, and he will save us from the hand of the foreigners.

**1 Samuel 7:9**

**1 Samuel 7:10**

**1 Samuel 7:14**

**1 Samuel 7:15**

And Samouēl judged Israel all the days of his life.

**1 Samuel 7:16**

**1 Samuel 7:17**

**1 Samuel 8:1**

**1 Samuel 8:13**

**1 Samuel 8:14**

**1 Samuel 8:16**

**1 Samuel 8:17**

And you will cry out in that day because of your king whom you chose for yourselves, and the Lord will not listen to you in those days, because you chose a king for yourselves.

**1 Samuel 8:19**

**1 Samuel 8:20**

**1 Samuel 8:21**

And Samouēl heard all the words of the people and spoke them into the ears of the Lord.

**1 Samuel 8:22**

### Chapter 9

**1 Samuel 9:1**

And there was a man from the sons of Benjamin, and his name was Kis, son of Abiēl, son of Sared, son of Bachir, son of Aphek, son of a Jeminaian man, a mighty man.

**1 Samuel 9:2**

And he had a son, and his name was Saoul, a well-grown good man, and there was not among the sons of Israel a better man than he; from his shoulders and above he was taller than all the people.

**1 Samuel 9:3**

And the donkeys of Kis, father of Saoul, were lost, and Kis said to Saoul his son, Take with yourself one of the young men, rise, and go seek the donkeys.

**1 Samuel 9:4**

And they passed through the hill-country of Ephraim, and they passed through the land of Selcha and did not find them, and they passed through the land of Easakem and it was not there, and they passed through the land of Iakim and did not find them.

**1 Samuel 9:5**

When they came into Siph, Saoul said to his young man who was with him, Come, let us turn back, lest my father leave off about the donkeys and be anxious about us.

**1 Samuel 9:6**

And the young man said to him, Behold now, there is a man of God in this city, and the man is honored; everything whatever he may speak, when it comes, it will stand. And now let us go there, so he may report to us the road on which we have gone.

**1 Samuel 9:7**

And Saoul said to his young man who was with him, And behold, we will go, but what shall we bring to the man of God? Because the breads have failed from our vessels, and there is no more with us to carry in to the man of God. What have we with us?

**1 Samuel 9:8**

And the young man answered Saoul again and said, Behold, a quarter-shekel of silver has been found in my hand, and I will give it to the man of God, and he will tell us our road.

**1 Samuel 9:9**

Formerly in Israel each one used to say these things when going to inquire of God: Come, let us go to the seer, because the people formerly called the prophet the seer.

**1 Samuel 9:10**

And Saoul said to his young man, Good word. Come, let us go. And they went into the city where the man of God was there.

**1 Samuel 9:11**

As they were going up the ascent of the city, they found young girls who had come out to draw water, and they say to them, Is the seer here?

**1 Samuel 9:12**

And the girls answered them and say to them, He is; behold, before your face now. For today he has come into the city, because there is a sacrifice today for the people at the high place.

**1 Samuel 9:13**

As soon as you enter the city, so you will find him in the city before he goes up to the high place to eat. Because the people certainly will not eat until he enters, because he blesses the sacrifice, and after these things the guests eat. And now go up, because today you will find him.

**1 Samuel 9:14**

And they go up to the city. As they were entering into the middle of the city, behold, Samouēl came out to meet them, to go up to the high place.

**1 Samuel 9:15**

And the Lord had uncovered the ear of Samouēl one day before Saoul came to him, saying,

**1 Samuel 9:16**

About this time tomorrow I will send to you a man from the land of Benjamin, and you will anoint him as ruler over my people Israel, and he will save my people from the hand of foreigners, because I have looked upon the humiliation of my people, because their cry has come to me.

**1 Samuel 9:17**

And Samouēl saw Saoul, and the Lord answered him, Behold, the man of whom I spoke to you; this one will rule among my people.

**1 Samuel 9:18**

And Saoul came near to Samouēl in the middle of the city and said, Tell me now, where is the house of the seer?

**1 Samuel 9:19**

And Samouēl answered Saoul and said, I am he. Go up before me to the high place and eat with me today, and I will send you away in the morning, and all the things in your heart I will report to you.

**1 Samuel 9:20**

And concerning your donkeys that were lost three days ago today, do not set your heart on them, because they have been found. And for whom are the beautiful things of Israel? Are they not for you and for your father’s house?

**1 Samuel 9:21**

And Saoul answered and said, Am I not son of a Jeminaian man, from the least scepter of a tribe of Israel, and my tribe the least from the whole scepter of Benjamin? And why have you spoken to me according to this word?

**1 Samuel 9:22**

And Samouēl took Saoul and his young man and brought them into the guest room and set for them a place among the first of those who had been called, about seventy men.

**1 Samuel 9:23**

And Samouēl said to the cook, Give me the portion that I gave to you, which I said to you to set beside you.

**1 Samuel 9:24**

And the cook lifted up the haunch and set it before Saoul, and Samouēl said to Saoul, Behold, what has been left over; set it before you and eat, because it has been kept for you for this appointed witness beside the others. And Saoul ate with Samouēl on that day.

**1 Samuel 9:25**

And he came down from the high place into the city, and they spread a bed for Saoul on the roof.

**1 Samuel 9:26**

And he slept. And it came to be, as dawn was rising, Samouēl called Saoul on the roof, saying, Rise, and I will send you away. And Saoul rose, and both he and Samouēl went out.

**1 Samuel 9:27**

As they were going down to the outskirts of the city, Samouēl said to Saoul, Tell the young man, and let him pass on before us. But you stand like today, and hear the word of God.

### Chapter 10

**1 Samuel 10:1**

And Samouēl took the flask of oil and poured it on his head and kissed him and said to him, Has not the Lord anointed you as ruler over his people, over Israel? And you will rule among the people of the Lord, and you will save him from the hand of his enemies round about. And this is the sign to you that the Lord has anointed you over his inheritance as ruler.

**1 Samuel 10:2**

When you depart from me today, you will find two men by the tombs of Rachel in the border of Benjamin, speaking great things, and they will say to you, The donkeys that you went to seek have been found, and behold, your father has shaken off the matter of the donkeys and is anxious about you, saying, What shall I do concerning my son?

**1 Samuel 10:3**

And you will pass on from there and beyond, and you will come as far as the oak of Thabor, and you will find there three men going up to God at Baithēl, one carrying three kids, one carrying three vessels of breads, and one carrying a skin of wine.

**1 Samuel 10:4**

And they will ask you the things of peace, and they will give you two firstfruits of breads, and you will take them from their hand.

**1 Samuel 10:5**

And after these things you will enter the hill of God, where the station of the foreigners is, there at Nasib the foreigner. And it will be when you enter there into the city, you will meet a chorus of prophets coming down from the high place, and before them harp and tambourine and flute and lyre, and they prophesying.

**1 Samuel 10:6**

And the Spirit of the Lord will rush upon you, and you will prophesy with them, and you will be turned into another man.

**1 Samuel 10:7**

And it will be when these signs come upon you, do everything whatever your hand finds, because God is with you.

**1 Samuel 10:8**

And you will go down before me to Galgala, and behold, I am coming down to you to offer up whole burnt offerings and sacrifices of peace. Seven days you will wait until my coming to you, and I will make known to you what you shall do.

**1 Samuel 10:9**

And it came to be when he turned his shoulder to depart from Samouēl, God turned for him another heart, and all these signs came on that day.

**1 Samuel 10:10**

And he comes from there to the hill, and behold, a chorus of prophets came opposite him, and the Spirit of God leapt upon him, and he prophesied in their midst.

**1 Samuel 10:11**

And it came to be, all who knew him yesterday and the third day saw, and behold, he was in the midst of the prophets, and each person said to his neighbor, What is this that has happened to the son of Kis? Is Saoul also among prophets?

**1 Samuel 10:12**

And one of them answered and said, And who is his father? Because of this it became a proverb, Is Saoul also among prophets?

**1 Samuel 10:13**

And he finished prophesying and comes to the hill.

**1 Samuel 10:14**

And his kinsman said to him and to his young man, Where did you go? And they said, To seek the donkeys, and we saw that they are not there, and we entered to Samouēl.

**1 Samuel 10:15**

And the kinsman said to Saoul, Tell me now, what did Samouēl say to you?

**1 Samuel 10:16**

And Saoul said to his kinsman, He plainly told me that the donkeys have been found. But the word of the kingship he did not tell him.

**1 Samuel 10:17**

And Samouēl summoned all the people to the Lord at Massēpha,

**1 Samuel 10:18**

and he said to the sons of Israel, Thus says the Lord God of Israel, saying, I brought up the sons of Israel from Egypt, and I delivered you from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt and from all the kingdoms afflicting you.

**1 Samuel 10:19**

And you today have counted as nothing your God, who himself is your savior from all your evils and afflictions, and you said, No, but you will appoint a king over us. And now stand before the Lord by your scepters and by your tribes.

**1 Samuel 10:20**

And Samouēl brought near all the scepters of Israel, and the scepter of Benjamin was taken by lot.

**1 Samuel 10:21**

And he brings near the scepter of Benjamin by tribes, and the tribe of Mattari is taken by lot. And they bring near the tribe of Mattari by men, and Saoul son of Kis was taken by lot. And they sought him, and he was not found.

**1 Samuel 10:22**

And Samouēl inquired yet again of the Lord whether the man comes here. And the Lord said, Behold, he is hidden among the baggage.

**1 Samuel 10:23**

And they ran and take him from there, and he stood in the midst of the people, and he was taller than all the people from the shoulder and upward.

**1 Samuel 10:24**

And Samouēl said to all the people, Have you seen whom the Lord has chosen for himself, that there is none like him among all of you? And all the people knew and said, Long live the king.

**1 Samuel 10:25**

And Samouēl told the people the righteous judgment of the king, and he wrote it in a scroll and set it before the Lord. And Samouēl sent away all the people, and each went to his place.

**1 Samuel 10:26**

And Saoul went to his house at Gabaa, and sons of powers whose hearts God had touched went with Saoul.

**1 Samuel 10:27**

And pestilent sons said, How will this one save us? And they dishonored him and did not bring him gifts.

### Chapter 11

**1 Samuel 11:1**

And it came to be as after a month, Naas the Ammanite went up and camped against Iabis Galaad, and all the men of Iabis said to Naas the Ammanite, Make a covenant with us, and we will serve you.

**1 Samuel 11:2**

And Naas the Ammanite said to them, On this condition I will make a covenant with you: that I gouge out every right eye of yours, and I will set reproach on Israel.

**1 Samuel 11:3**

And the men of Iabis say to him, Leave us for seven days, and we will send messengers into every border of Israel. And if there is no one saving us, we will come out to you.

**1 Samuel 11:4**

**1 Samuel 11:5**

And behold, Saoul came after the morning from the field, and Saoul said, Why is the people weeping? And they recount to him the words of the sons of Iabis.

**1 Samuel 11:6**

And the Spirit of the Lord leapt upon Saoul as he heard these words, and his anger was greatly kindled against them.

**1 Samuel 11:7**

And the astonishment of the Lord came upon the people of Israel, and they cried out like one man.

**1 Samuel 11:8**

And he musters them at Abiezek on the high place, every man of Israel six hundred thousand, and men of Iouda seventy thousand.

**1 Samuel 11:9**

And he said to the messengers who came, Thus you will say to the men of Iabis, Tomorrow salvation is for you, when the sun grows warm. And the messengers came into the city and report to the men of Iabis, and they rejoiced.

**1 Samuel 11:10**

And the men of Iabis said to Naas the Ammanite, Tomorrow we will come out to you, and you may do to us what is good in your sight.

**1 Samuel 11:11**

**1 Samuel 11:12**

And the people said to Samouēl, Who is the one who said, Shall Saoul not reign over us? Hand over the men, and we will put them to death.

**1 Samuel 11:13**

And Saoul said, No one will be put to death on this day, because today the Lord has worked salvation in Israel.

**1 Samuel 11:14**

And Samouēl said to the people, saying, Let us go to Galgala, and let us renew the kingship there.

**1 Samuel 11:15**

### Chapter 12

**1 Samuel 12:1**

And Samouēl said to every man of Israel, Behold, I have listened to your voice in everything whatever you said to me, and I made a king reign over you.

**1 Samuel 12:2**

And now behold, the king goes before you, and I have grown old and will sit, and behold, my sons are among you, and behold, I have gone before you from my youth until this day.

**1 Samuel 12:3**

Behold me. Answer against me before the Lord and before his anointed. Whose calf have I taken, or whose donkey have I taken, or whom of you have I oppressed, or whom have I crushed, or from whose hand have I taken a propitiation, even sandals? Answer against me, and I will restore it to you.

**1 Samuel 12:4**

And they said to Samouēl, You have not wronged us, and you have not oppressed us, and you have not crushed us, and you have not taken anything from the hand of anyone.

**1 Samuel 12:5**

And Samouēl said to the people, The Lord is witness among you, and his anointed is witness today in this day, that you have not found anything in my hand. And they said, Witness.

**1 Samuel 12:6**

And Samouēl said to the people, saying, The Lord is witness, the one who made Moses and Aarōn, the one who brought our fathers up from Egypt.

**1 Samuel 12:7**

And now stand, and I will judge you before the Lord, and I will recount to you all the righteousness of the Lord, what things he did among you and among your fathers.

**1 Samuel 12:8**

When Iakōb and his sons entered into Egypt, and Egypt humbled them, our fathers cried out to the Lord, and the Lord sent Moses and Aarōn and brought our fathers out of Egypt and settled them in this place.

**1 Samuel 12:9**

And they forgot the Lord their God, and he sold them into the hands of Sisara, commander of the army of Iabin king of Asōr, and into the hands of foreigners, and into the hands of the king of Mōab, and they fought against them.

**1 Samuel 12:10**

And they cried out to the Lord and said, We have sinned, because we abandoned the Lord and served the Baals and the groves, and now deliver us from the hand of our enemies, and we will serve you.

**1 Samuel 12:11**

And the Lord sent Ierobaal and Barak and Iephthae and Samouēl, and he delivered you from the hand of your enemies round about, and you lived trusting.

**1 Samuel 12:12**

And you saw that Naas king of the sons of Ammon came against you, and you said, No, but a king will reign over us, though the Lord your God is your king.

**1 Samuel 12:13**

And now behold the king whom you chose, and behold, the Lord has given a king over you.

**1 Samuel 12:14**

If you fear the Lord and serve him and hear his voice and do not rebel against the mouth of the Lord, then both you and the king who reigns over you will be going after the Lord.

**1 Samuel 12:15**

But if you do not hear the voice of the Lord and you rebel against the mouth of the Lord, then the hand of the Lord will be upon you and upon your king.

**1 Samuel 12:16**

And now stand and see this great thing, which the Lord will do before your eyes.

**1 Samuel 12:17**

Is it not wheat harvest today? I will call upon the Lord, and he will give voices and rain, and know and see that your evil is great, which you did before the Lord, asking a king for yourselves.

**1 Samuel 12:18**

And Samouēl called upon the Lord, and the Lord gave voices and rain on that day, and all the people greatly feared the Lord and Samouēl.

**1 Samuel 12:19**

And all the people said to Samouēl, Pray concerning your servants to the Lord your God, and let us not die, because we have added to all our sins this evil, asking a king for ourselves.

**1 Samuel 12:20**

And Samouēl said to the people, Do not fear. You have done all this evil; only do not turn aside from behind the Lord, and serve the Lord with your whole heart.

**1 Samuel 12:21**

And do not turn aside after the things that are not, which will accomplish nothing and will not deliver, because they are nothing.

**1 Samuel 12:22**

Because the Lord will not thrust away his people, on account of his great name, because the Lord was pleased to take you to himself for a people.

**1 Samuel 12:23**

And as for me, far be it from me to sin against the Lord by ceasing to pray concerning you, and I will serve the Lord and show you the good and straight way.

**1 Samuel 12:24**

Only fear the Lord and serve him in truth and with your whole heart, because you have seen what things he magnified with you.

**1 Samuel 12:25**

But if you do evil in doing evil, both you and your king will be swept away.

### Chapter 13

**1 Samuel 13:2**

And Saoul chose for himself three thousand men from the men of Israel, and two thousand were with Saoul in Machmas and on the hill of Baithēl, and one thousand were with Iōnathan in Gabee of Benjamin, and the rest of the people he sent away, each to his tent.

**1 Samuel 13:3**

And Iōnathan struck the foreign garrison on the hill, and the foreigners heard, and Saoul blew the trumpet through all the land, saying, The slaves have revolted.

**1 Samuel 13:4**

**1 Samuel 13:5**
