**1 Samuel 13:6**

And each man of Israel saw that he was in a narrow place, that no one could come near him, and the people hid in the caves and in the folds and in the rocks and in the pits and in the cisterns.

**1 Samuel 13:7**

And the ones crossing over crossed the Jordan into the land of Gad and Galaad. And Saoul was still in Galgala, and all the people stood outside themselves after him.

**1 Samuel 13:8**

And he waited seven days for the testimony, as Samouēl said, and Samouēl did not arrive in Galgala, and his people were scattered from him.

**1 Samuel 13:9**

And Saoul said, Bring near, so I may offer whole burnt offerings and peace offerings. And he offered the whole burnt offering.

**1 Samuel 13:10**

And it came to be, as he finished offering the whole burnt offering, Samouēl arrives, and Saoul went out to meet him, to bless him.

**1 Samuel 13:11**

And Samouēl said, What have you done? And Saoul said, Because I saw that the people were scattered from me, and you did not come as you ordered in the testimony of the days, and the foreigners were gathered in Machmas,

**1 Samuel 13:12**

I said, Now the foreigners will come down against me to Galgala, and I have not entreated the face of the Lord. And I forced myself and offered the whole burnt offering.

**1 Samuel 13:13**

And Samouēl said to Saoul, It has been made foolish for you, because you did not keep the commandment that the Lord commanded you. For now the Lord would have prepared your kingdom over Israel forever.

**1 Samuel 13:14**

And now your kingdom will not stand, and the Lord will seek for himself a man according to his heart, and the Lord will appoint him as ruler over his people, because you did not keep what the Lord commanded you.

**1 Samuel 13:15**

And Samouēl rose and went away from Galgala on his road, and the remnant of the people went up after Saoul to meet their fighting people, from Galgala to Gabaa of Benjamin. And Saoul mustered the people found with him, about six hundred men.

**1 Samuel 13:16**

And Saoul and Iōnathan his son and the people found with them were staying in Gabee of Benjamin and were weeping, and the foreigners had camped in Machmas.

**1 Samuel 13:17**

And the destroyer came out from the camp of the foreigners in three companies. The one company looked toward the road of Gophera, toward the land of Sōgal.

**1 Samuel 13:18**

And one company looked toward the road of Baithōrōn, and one company looked toward the road of Gabee that bends down toward the land of Sabin.

**1 Samuel 13:19**

And a smith of iron was not found in all the land of Israel, because the foreigners said, Lest the Hebrews make sword or spear.

**1 Samuel 13:20**

And all Israel used to go down into the land of the foreigners for each one to forge his reaping tool and his implement and each one his axe and his sickle.

**1 Samuel 13:21**

And the harvest was ready for reaping, and the implements were at three shekels for the tooth, and for the axe and for the sickle the charge was the same.

**1 Samuel 13:22**

And it came to be in the days of the war at Machmas, sword and spear were not found in the hand of any of the people with Saoul and with Iōnathan, but they were found for Saoul and for Iōnathan his son.

**1 Samuel 13:23**

And the station of the foreigners came out to the region beyond Machmas.

### Chapter 14

**1 Samuel 14:1**

And it came to be on a day, Iōnathan son of Saoul said to the young man carrying his equipment, Come, and let us cross over to the station of the foreigners that is over there beyond. But to his father he did not report it.

**1 Samuel 14:2**

And Saoul was sitting on the edge of the hill under the pomegranate tree in Magdōn, and about six hundred men were with him.

**1 Samuel 14:3**

And Achia son of Achitōb, brother of Iōchabēd, son of Phinees, son of Heli, priest of God in Sēlōm, was carrying an ephod. And the people did not know that Iōnathan had gone.

**1 Samuel 14:4**

And between the passage where Iōnathan was seeking to cross over to the station of the foreigners, there was a rocky spur on this side and a rocky spur on that side. The name of the one was Bazez, and the name of the other Senna.

**1 Samuel 14:5**

The one road was northward, toward Machmas, and the other southward, toward Gabee.

**1 Samuel 14:6**

And Iōnathan said to the young man carrying his equipment, Come, let us cross over to the station of these uncircumcised ones; perhaps the Lord may act for us, because for the Lord there is no restraint to save by many or by few.

**1 Samuel 14:7**

And the one carrying his equipment said to him, Do everything whatever your heart inclines. Behold, I am with you; as your heart, my heart.

**1 Samuel 14:8**

And Iōnathan said, Behold, we are crossing over to the men, and we will roll ourselves down to them.

**1 Samuel 14:9**

If they say these things to us, Stand there until we report to you, then we will stand in our place and certainly will not go up against them.

**1 Samuel 14:10**

But if they say these things to us, Come up to us, then we will go up, because the Lord has delivered them into our hands. This will be the sign for us.

**1 Samuel 14:11**

And both entered into the station of the foreigners, and the foreigners say, Behold, the Hebrews are coming out from their holes where they had hidden there.

**1 Samuel 14:12**

And the men of the station answered Iōnathan and the one carrying his equipment and say, Come up to us, and we will make a word known to you. And Iōnathan said to the one carrying his equipment, Come up after me, because the Lord has delivered them into the hands of Israel.

**1 Samuel 14:13**

And Iōnathan went up on his hands and on his feet, and the one carrying his equipment after him. And they looked into the face of Iōnathan, and he struck them down, and the one carrying his equipment kept finishing them off behind him.

**1 Samuel 14:14**

And the first blow that Iōnathan and the one carrying his equipment struck was about twenty men, with darts and sling-stones and field-pebbles.

**1 Samuel 14:15**

And there was astonishment in the camp and in the field, and all the people in the station and the destroyers stood outside themselves, and they themselves were not willing to act, and the earth was amazed, and there was astonishment from the Lord.

**1 Samuel 14:16**

And the watchmen of Saoul in Gabee of Benjamin saw, and behold, the camp was troubled here and there.

**1 Samuel 14:17**

And Saoul said to the people with him, Muster now and see who has gone out from you. And they mustered, and behold, Iōnathan and the one carrying his equipment were not found.

**1 Samuel 14:18**

And Saoul said to Achia, Bring the ephod near, because he was carrying the ephod on that day before Israel.

**1 Samuel 14:19**

And it came to be, as Saoul was speaking to the priest, the sound in the camp of the foreigners kept going and increasing. And Saoul said to the priest, Gather in your hands.

**1 Samuel 14:20**

And Saoul cried out, and all the people with him, and they came as far as the battle, and behold, the sword of each man came against his neighbor, a very great confusion.

**1 Samuel 14:21**

And the slaves who were with the foreigners yesterday and the third day, who had gone up into the camp, they also turned to be with Israel, those with Saoul and Iōnathan.

**1 Samuel 14:22**

And all Israel, the ones hiding in the hill-country of Ephraim, heard that the foreigners had fled, and they also joined after them in the battle.

**1 Samuel 14:23**

And the Lord saved Israel on that day, and the battle passed through Baithōn, and all the people with Saoul were about ten thousand men, and the battle was scattered through the whole city in the hill-country of Ephraim.

**1 Samuel 14:24**

And Saoul committed a great ignorance on that day, and he bound the people under oath, saying, Cursed is the man who eats bread until evening, until I take vengeance on my enemy. And none of the people tasted bread.

**1 Samuel 14:25**

And all the land came into a wooded forest, and there was a honeycomb on the face of the field.

**1 Samuel 14:26**

And the people entered into the honey-place, and behold, honey was going along, and there was no one turning his hand to his mouth, because the people feared the oath of the Lord.

**1 Samuel 14:27**

And Iōnathan had not heard when his father put the people under oath, and he stretched out the tip of his staff that was in his hand and dipped it into the comb of the honey and turned his hand to his mouth, and his eyes looked up.

**1 Samuel 14:28**

And one from the people answered and said, Your father bound the people with an oath, saying, Cursed is the man who eats bread today, and the people grew faint.

**1 Samuel 14:29**

And Iōnathan understood and said, My father has troubled the land. See now that my eyes have brightened because I tasted a little of this honey.

**1 Samuel 14:30**

How much more, if the people today had eaten from the spoil of their enemies that they found. For now the blow among the foreigners would have been greater.

**1 Samuel 14:31**

And on that day he struck down the foreigners from Machmas, and the people grew very weary.

**1 Samuel 14:32**

And the people turned aside to the spoil, and the people took flocks and cattle and calves of oxen and slaughtered them on the ground, and the people were eating with the blood.

**1 Samuel 14:33**

And it was reported to Saoul, saying, The people have sinned against the Lord by eating with the blood. And he said, In Geththēm, roll to me a great stone here.

**1 Samuel 14:34**

And Saoul said, Scatter among the people and tell them to bring here, each his calf and each his sheep, and let him slaughter on this and not sin against the Lord by eating with the blood. And all the people brought near, each the thing in his hand, and they slaughtered there.

**1 Samuel 14:35**

And Saoul built there an altar to the Lord. This was what Saoul began to build as an altar to the Lord.

**1 Samuel 14:36**

And Saoul said, Let us go down after the foreigners by night and plunder among them until the day gives light, and let us not leave a man among them. And they said, Do everything good in your sight. And the priest said, Let us come near to God here.

**1 Samuel 14:37**

And Saoul inquired of God, Shall I go down after the foreigners? Will you deliver them into the hands of Israel? And he did not answer him on that day.

**1 Samuel 14:38**

And Saoul said, Bring near here all the corners of Israel, and know and see in what this sin has happened today.

**1 Samuel 14:39**

Because the Lord lives, who saved Israel, that if it is found in Iōnathan my son, he will surely die. And there was not one answering from all the people.

**1 Samuel 14:40**

And he said to all Israel, You will be for one side, and I and Iōnathan my son will be for one side. And the people said to Saoul, Do what is good in your sight.

**1 Samuel 14:41**

And Saoul said, Lord God of Israel, why have you not answered your servant today? If the wrong is in me or in Iōnathan my son, Lord God of Israel, give clear signs; and if thus you say, In your people Israel, give holiness. And Iōnathan and Saoul were taken by lot, and the people went out.

**1 Samuel 14:42**

And Saoul said, Cast lot between me and between Iōnathan my son; whomever the Lord may take by lot, let him die. And the people said to Saoul, This word is not right. But Saoul prevailed over the people, and they cast lot between him and between Iōnathan his son, and Iōnathan was taken by lot.

**1 Samuel 14:43**

And Saoul said to Iōnathan, Tell me what you have done. And Iōnathan told him and said, Tasting, I tasted a little honey on the tip of the staff that was in my hand. Behold, I am dying.

**1 Samuel 14:44**

And Saoul said to him, Thus may God do to me and thus may he add, because you will surely die today.

**1 Samuel 14:45**

And the people said to Saoul, Will the one who worked this great salvation in Israel be put to death today? The Lord lives, if a hair of his head will fall to the ground, because he worked with the people of God on this day. And the people prayed for Iōnathan on that day, and he did not die.

**1 Samuel 14:46**

And Saoul went up from after the foreigners, and the foreigners went away to their place.

**1 Samuel 14:47**

And Saoul took up rule over Israel and fought all his enemies round about, against Mōab and against the sons of Ammon and against the sons of Edom and against Baithōr and against king Souba and against the foreigners. Wherever he turned, he was being saved.

**1 Samuel 14:48**

And he worked might and struck Amalēk and delivered Israel from the hand of those trampling him.

**1 Samuel 14:49**

And the sons of Saoul were Iōnathan and Iessiou and Melchisa, and the names of his two daughters: the name of the firstborn Merob, and the name of the second Melchol.

**1 Samuel 14:50**

And the name of his wife was Achinoom, daughter of Achimaas, and the name of the commander of his army was Abennēr, son of Nēr, son of a kinsman of Saoul.

**1 Samuel 14:51**

And Kis, father of Saoul, and Nēr, father of Abennēr, were sons of Iamin, son of Abiēl.

**1 Samuel 14:52**

And the war against the foreigners was fierce all the days of Saoul, and when Saoul saw every mighty man and every man a son of strength, he gathered them to himself.

### Chapter 15

**1 Samuel 15:1**

And Samouēl said to Saoul, The Lord sent me to anoint you as king over Israel, and now hear the voice of the Lord.

**1 Samuel 15:2**

Thus says the Lord Sabaōth, Now I will avenge what Amalēk did to Israel, how he met him on the road when he was coming up out of Egypt.

**1 Samuel 15:3**

And now go, and you will strike Amalēk and devote all that is his, and you will not preserve anything from him, and you will utterly destroy him and devote him and all his things, and you will not spare from him, and you will kill from man to woman and from infant to one nursing and from calf to sheep and from camel to donkey.

**1 Samuel 15:4**

And Saoul gave orders to the people and musters them in Galgala, four hundred thousand companies, and Iouda thirty thousand companies.

**1 Samuel 15:5**

And Saoul came as far as the cities of Amalēk and lay in ambush in the wadi.

**1 Samuel 15:6**

And Saoul said to the Kainite, Go away and turn aside from the midst of Amalēk, lest I add you with him, because you worked mercy with the sons of Israel when they were coming up out of Egypt. And the Kainite turned aside from the midst of Amalēk.

**1 Samuel 15:7**

And Saoul struck Amalēk from Heuila as far as Sour, in front of Egypt.

**1 Samuel 15:8**

And he captured Agag king of Amalēk alive, and all the people he killed by the mouth of the sword.

**1 Samuel 15:9**

And Saoul and all the people preserved Agag alive and the good things of the flocks and the herds and the foods and the vineyards and all the good things, and they were not willing to destroy them. But every dishonored and worthless thing they destroyed.

**1 Samuel 15:10**

And the word of the Lord came to Samouēl, saying,

**1 Samuel 15:11**

I have been comforted that I made Saoul king, because he turned from behind me and did not keep my words. And Samouēl was troubled, and he cried out to the Lord all the night.

**1 Samuel 15:12**

And Samouēl rose early and went to meet Israel in the morning, and it was reported to Samouēl, saying, Saoul has come to Karmēlos and has raised a hand for himself and turned the chariot and gone down to Galgala toward Saoul. And behold, he had offered whole burnt offerings to the Lord, the first of the spoil that he brought from Amalēk.

**1 Samuel 15:13**

And Samouēl came to Saoul, and he said to him, Blessed are you to the Lord. I have established everything whatever the Lord spoke.

**1 Samuel 15:14**

And Samouēl said, And what is this voice of the flock in my ears, and the voice of cattle that I hear?

**1 Samuel 15:15**

And Saoul said, I brought them from Amalēk, the things that the people preserved, the strongest of the flock and of the herds, so that they may be sacrificed to the Lord your God, and the rest I destroyed.

**1 Samuel 15:16**

And Samouēl said to Saoul, Let it be, and I will report to you what the Lord spoke to me in the night. And he said to him, Speak.

**1 Samuel 15:17**

And Samouēl said to Saoul, Were you not small before him, leader of the scepter of a tribe of Israel? And the Lord anointed you as king over Israel.

**1 Samuel 15:18**

And the Lord sent you on a road and said to you, Go, and utterly destroy Amalēk, the ones sinning against me, and you will fight them until you finish them.

**1 Samuel 15:19**

And why did you not hear the voice of the Lord, but rushed to set yourself on the spoil and did the evil before the Lord?

**1 Samuel 15:20**

And Saoul said to Samouēl, Because I heard the voice of the people, I went on the road on which the Lord sent me, and I brought Agag king of Amalēk, and Amalēk I destroyed utterly.

**1 Samuel 15:21**

And the people took from the spoil flocks and herds, the first of the devoted destruction, to sacrifice before the Lord our God in Galgala.

**1 Samuel 15:22**

And Samouēl said, Is it acceptable to the Lord, whole burnt offerings and sacrifices, as hearing the voice of the Lord? Behold, hearing is better than sacrifice, and listening than the fat of rams.

**1 Samuel 15:23**

Because sin is divination, and pain and grief bring on teraphim, because you counted the word of the Lord as nothing, and the Lord will count you as nothing from being king over Israel.

**1 Samuel 15:24**

And Saoul said to Samouēl, I have sinned, because I transgressed the word of the Lord and your saying, because I feared the people and heard their voice.

**1 Samuel 15:25**

And now take away my sin, and turn back with me, and I will bow down to the Lord your God.

**1 Samuel 15:26**

And Samouēl said to Saoul, I will not turn back with you, because you counted the word of the Lord as nothing, and the Lord will count you as nothing from being king over Israel.

**1 Samuel 15:27**

And Samouēl turned his face to go away, and Saoul seized the wing of his double cloak and tore it.

**1 Samuel 15:28**

And Samouēl said to him, The Lord has torn the kingdom of Israel from your hand today and will give it to your neighbor, the good one beyond you.

**1 Samuel 15:29**

And Israel will be divided into two, and he will not turn back, nor will he repent, because he is not like a human, for him to repent.

**1 Samuel 15:30**

And Saoul said, I have sinned, but glorify me now before the elders of Israel and before my people, and turn back with me, and I will bow down to the Lord your God.

**1 Samuel 15:31**

And Samouēl turned back after Saoul, and he bowed down to the Lord.

**1 Samuel 15:32**

And Samouēl said, Bring near to me Agag king of Amalēk. And Agag came to him trembling, and Agag said, Is death thus bitter?

**1 Samuel 15:33**

And Samouēl said to Agag, As your sword made women childless, so your mother will be made childless among women. And Samouēl slaughtered Agag before the Lord in Galgala.

**1 Samuel 15:34**

And Samouēl went away to Armathaim, and Saoul went up to his house at Gabaa.

**1 Samuel 15:35**

And Samouēl did not add again to see Saoul until the day of his death, because Samouēl was mourning for Saoul, and the Lord repented that he had made Saoul king over Israel.

### Chapter 16

**1 Samuel 16:1**

And the Lord said to Samouēl, How long do you mourn over Saoul, while I have counted him as nothing from reigning over Israel? Fill your horn with oil and come, I will send you to Iessai in Bēthleem, because I have seen among his sons one for me to reign.

**1 Samuel 16:2**

And Samouēl said, How shall I go? Saoul will hear and kill me. And the Lord said, Take a heifer of the cattle in your hand, and you will say, I have come to sacrifice to the Lord.

**1 Samuel 16:3**

And you will call Iessai to the sacrifice, and I will make known to you what you shall do, and you will anoint whomever I tell you.

**1 Samuel 16:4**

And Samouēl did everything whatever the Lord spoke to him, and he came to Bēthleem, and the elders of the city stood outside themselves to meet him and said, Seer, is your coming peace?

**1 Samuel 16:5**

And he said, Peace. I have come to sacrifice to the Lord. Consecrate yourselves and be glad with me today. And he consecrated Iessai and his sons and called them to the sacrifice.

**1 Samuel 16:6**

And it came to be as they were entering, he saw Eliab and said, Then indeed his anointed is before the Lord.

**1 Samuel 16:7**

And the Lord said to Samouēl, Do not look on his appearance, nor on the condition of his stature, because I have counted him as nothing. For God will not see as a human sees, because a human sees into the face, but God sees into the heart.

**1 Samuel 16:8**

And Iessai called Aminadab and brought him before Samouēl, and he said, Neither has the Lord chosen this one.

**1 Samuel 16:9**

And Iessai brought Sama, and he said, Neither in this one has the Lord chosen.

**1 Samuel 16:10**

And Iessai brought his seven sons before Samouēl, and Samouēl said, The Lord has not chosen among these.

**1 Samuel 16:11**

And Samouēl said to Iessai, Have the young men failed? And he said, There is still the small one; behold, he is shepherding among the flock. And Samouēl said to Iessai, Send and take him, because we certainly will not recline until he comes here.

**1 Samuel 16:12**

And he sent and brought him in. And he was ruddy, with beauty of eyes, and good in appearance to the Lord. And the Lord said to Samouēl, Rise and anoint David, because this one is good.

**1 Samuel 16:13**

And Samouēl took the horn of oil and anointed him in the midst of his brothers, and the Spirit of the Lord leapt upon David from that day and beyond. And Samouēl rose and went away to Armathaim.

**1 Samuel 16:14**

And the Spirit of the Lord departed from Saoul, and an evil spirit from the Lord was choking him.

**1 Samuel 16:15**

And the servants of Saoul said to him, Behold now, an evil spirit from the Lord is choking you.

**1 Samuel 16:16**

Let your servants before you speak now, and let them seek for our lord a man knowing how to play on a lyre, and it will be when an evil spirit is upon you, he will play with his lyre, and it will be good for you and will give you rest.

**1 Samuel 16:17**

And Saoul said to his servants, Find for me now a man playing rightly, and bring him to me.

**1 Samuel 16:18**

And one of his young men answered and said, Behold, I have seen a son belonging to Iessai the Bēthleemite, and he knows song, and the man is prudent and a warrior and wise in word and good in appearance, and the Lord is with him.

**1 Samuel 16:19**

And Saoul sent messengers to Iessai, saying, Send to me your son David, the one with your flock.

**1 Samuel 16:20**

And Iessai took a gomor of breads and a skin of wine and one kid of the goats and sent them by the hand of David his son to Saoul.

**1 Samuel 16:21**

And David entered to Saoul and stood before him, and he loved him greatly, and he became for him the one carrying his equipment.

**1 Samuel 16:22**

And Saoul sent to Iessai, saying, Let David now stand before me, because he has found favor in my eyes.

**1 Samuel 16:23**

And it came to be, when the evil spirit was upon Saoul, David would take the lyre and play with his hand, and Saoul would breathe freely, and it became good for him, and the evil spirit departed from him.

### Chapter 17

**1 Samuel 17:1**

And the foreigners gather their camps for war, and they are gathered at Sokchōth of Ioudaia, and they camp between Sokchōth and between Azēka in Epheremem.

**1 Samuel 17:2**

And Saoul and the men of Israel gather and camp in the valley, and they arrange themselves for war opposite the foreigners.

**1 Samuel 17:3**

And the foreigners stood on the mountain here, and Israel stood on the mountain there, and the valley was between them.

**1 Samuel 17:4**

And a mighty man came out from the battle-line of the foreigners, Goliath was his name, from Geth; his height was four cubits and a span.

**1 Samuel 17:5**

And a helmet was on his head, and he was clothed in a chain breastplate, and the weight of his breastplate was five thousand shekels of bronze and iron.

**1 Samuel 17:6**

And bronze greaves were over his legs, and a bronze shield was between his shoulders.

**1 Samuel 17:7**

And the shaft of his spear was like the beam of weavers, and his spearhead was six hundred shekels of iron, and the one carrying his weapons went before him.

**1 Samuel 17:8**

And he stood and cried out to the battle-line of Israel and said to them, Why do you come out to array yourselves for battle against us? Am I not a foreigner, and you Hebrews of Saoul? Choose for yourselves a man, and let him come down to me.

**1 Samuel 17:9**

And if he is able to fight with me and if he strikes me, we will be your slaves. But if I prevail and strike him, you will be our slaves and serve us.

**1 Samuel 17:10**

And the foreigner said, Behold, I have reproached the battle-line of Israel today in this day. Give me a man, and let the two of us fight alone.

**1 Samuel 17:11**

And Saoul and all Israel heard these words of the foreigner, and they stood outside themselves and feared greatly.

**1 Samuel 17:32**

And David said to Saoul, Let not the heart of my lord fall upon him. Your servant will go and fight with this foreigner.

**1 Samuel 17:33**

And Saoul said to David, You certainly will not be able to go to the foreigner to fight with him, because you are a young boy, and he is a warrior from his youth.

**1 Samuel 17:34**

And David said to Saoul, Your servant was shepherding for his father among the flock, and whenever the lion or the bear came and took a sheep from the herd,

**1 Samuel 17:35**

I would go out after it and strike it and snatch it from its mouth. And if it rose up against me, I seized its throat and struck and killed it.

**1 Samuel 17:36**

And your servant used to strike both the bear and the lion, and this uncircumcised foreigner will be like one of them. Will I not go and strike him and remove today reproach from Israel? Because who is this uncircumcised one, who has reproached the battle-line of the living God?

**1 Samuel 17:37**

The Lord who delivered me from the hand of the lion and from the hand of the bear, he will deliver me from the hand of this uncircumcised foreigner. And Saoul said to David, Go, and the Lord will be with you.

**1 Samuel 17:38**

And Saoul clothed David with a cloak and put a bronze helmet around his head.

**1 Samuel 17:39**

And David girded on his sword over his cloak and labored to walk once and twice, and David said to Saoul, I certainly will not be able to go in these things, because I have not tried them. And they take them off from him.

**1 Samuel 17:40**

And he took his staff in his hand and chose for himself five smooth stones from the wadi and put them in the shepherd’s pouch that belonged to him for gathering, and his sling was in his hand, and he came near to the foreign man.

**1 Samuel 17:42**

And Goliad saw David and dishonored him, because he was a youth, and he was ruddy, with beauty of eyes.

**1 Samuel 17:43**

And the foreigner said to David, Am I like a dog, that you come against me with staff and stones? And David said, No, but worse than a dog’s hand. And the foreigner cursed David by his gods.

**1 Samuel 17:44**

And the foreigner said to David, Come to me, and I will give your flesh to the birds of the sky and to the beasts of the earth.

**1 Samuel 17:45**

And David said to the foreigner, You come to me with sword and spear and shield, but I go to you in the name of the Lord Sabaōth, God of the battle-line of Israel, whom you have reproached today.

**1 Samuel 17:46**

And the Lord will shut you up into my hand today, and I will kill you and remove your head from you, and I will give your limbs and the limbs of the camp of the foreigners in this day to the birds of the sky and to the beasts of the earth, and all the earth will know that there is a God in Israel.

**1 Samuel 17:47**

And all this assembly will know that the Lord does not save with sword and spear, because the battle is the Lord’s, and the Lord will deliver you into our hands.

**1 Samuel 17:48**

And the foreigner rose and went to meet David.

**1 Samuel 17:49**

And David stretched out his hand into the pouch and took from there one stone and slung it and struck the foreigner on his forehead, and the stone went through the helmet into his forehead, and he fell on his face to the ground.

**1 Samuel 17:51**

And David ran and stood over him and took his sword and killed him and removed his head. And the foreigners saw that their mighty one had died, and they fled.

**1 Samuel 17:52**

And the men of Israel and Iouda rose and shouted and chased after them as far as the entrance of Geth and as far as the gate of Askalōn, and wounded men of the foreigners fell on the road of the gates and as far as Geth and as far as Akkarōn.

**1 Samuel 17:53**

And the men of Israel returned, turning aside from after the foreigners, and they trampled their camps.

**1 Samuel 17:54**

And David took the head of the foreigner and brought it into Ierousalēm, and his equipment he placed in his tent.

### Chapter 18

**1 Samuel 18:6**

And the dancing women came out to meet David from all the cities of Israel with tambourines and with rejoicing and with cymbals.

**1 Samuel 18:7**

And the women went out and were saying, Saoul struck in his thousands, and David in his tens of thousands.

**1 Samuel 18:8**

And the saying appeared evil in the eyes of Saoul because of this word, and he said, To David they gave the tens of thousands, and to me they gave the thousands.

**1 Samuel 18:9**

And Saoul was looking askance at David from that day and beyond.

**1 Samuel 18:12**

And Saoul feared from before David.

**1 Samuel 18:13**

And he removed him from himself and appointed him for himself commander of a thousand, and he went out and came in before the people.

**1 Samuel 18:14**

And David was understanding in all his ways, and the Lord was with him.

**1 Samuel 18:15**

And Saoul saw that he was understanding exceedingly, and he stood in awe from before him.

**1 Samuel 18:16**

And all Israel and Iouda loved David, because he was going out and coming in before the people.

**1 Samuel 18:20**

And Melchol daughter of Saoul loved David, and it was reported to Saoul, and it was made straight in his eyes.

**1 Samuel 18:21**

And Saoul said, I will give her to him, and she will be to him for a stumbling, and the hand of the foreigners will be against Saoul.

**1 Samuel 18:22**

And Saoul commanded his servants, saying, Speak secretly to David, saying, Behold, the king delights in you, and all his servants love you, and you become son-in-law to the king.

**1 Samuel 18:23**

And the servants of Saoul spoke these words into the ears of David, and David said, Is it a light thing in your eyes to become son-in-law to a king? And I am a humble man and not honored.

**1 Samuel 18:24**

And the servants of Saoul reported to him according to these words that David spoke.

**1 Samuel 18:25**

And Saoul said, Thus you will say to David: The king does not desire in a marriage gift, except one hundred foreskins of foreigners, to avenge on the enemies of the king. And Saoul thought to cast him into the hands of the foreigners.

**1 Samuel 18:26**

And the servants of Saoul report these words to David, and the word was made straight in the eyes of David, to become son-in-law to the king.

**1 Samuel 18:27**

And David rose and went, he and his men, and struck among the foreigners one hundred men, and he brought their foreskins to the king, and he became son-in-law to the king, and he gives to him Melchol his daughter to be his wife.

**1 Samuel 18:28**

And Saoul saw that the Lord was with David, and all Israel loved him.

**1 Samuel 18:29**

And Saoul added still more to stand in awe from before David.

### Chapter 19

**1 Samuel 19:1**

And Saoul spoke to Iōnathan his son and to all his servants to put David to death, but Iōnathan son of Saoul preferred David greatly.

**1 Samuel 19:2**

And Iōnathan reported to David, saying, Saoul seeks to put you to death. Therefore guard yourself tomorrow morning and hide and sit concealed.

**1 Samuel 19:3**

And I will go out and stand beside my father in the field where you are there, and I will speak concerning you to my father, and I will see what there may be, and I will report to you.

**1 Samuel 19:4**

And Iōnathan spoke good things concerning David to Saoul his father and said to him, Let not the king sin against your servant David, because he has not sinned against you, and his deeds are very good.

**1 Samuel 19:5**

And he put his life in his hand and struck the foreigner, and the Lord worked a great salvation, and all Israel saw and rejoiced. And why do you sin against innocent blood, to put David to death for nothing?

**1 Samuel 19:6**

And Saoul listened to the voice of Iōnathan, and Saoul swore, saying, As the Lord lives, he will not die.

**1 Samuel 19:7**

And Iōnathan called David and reported to him all these words, and Iōnathan brought David in to Saoul, and he was before him as yesterday and the third day.

**1 Samuel 19:8**

And the war was added to be against Saoul, and David prevailed and fought the foreigners and struck among them a very great blow, and they fled from before him.

**1 Samuel 19:9**

And it came to be, an evil spirit of God was on Saoul, and he was in the house sitting, and a spear was in his hand, and David was playing with his hands.

**1 Samuel 19:10**

And Saoul sought to strike the spear into David, but David withdrew from before Saoul, and he struck the spear into the wall, and David departed and escaped.

**1 Samuel 19:11**

And it came to be on that night, Saoul sent messengers to the house of David to guard him so as to kill him in the morning. And Melchol his wife reported to David, saying, If you do not save your life this night, tomorrow you will be put to death.

**1 Samuel 19:12**

And Melchol let David down through the window, and he went away and fled and was saved.

**1 Samuel 19:13**

And Melchol took the tomb-images and placed them on the bed, and she put a goat’s liver at his head and covered them with a garment.

**1 Samuel 19:14**

And Saoul sent messengers to take David, and they say that he is sick.

**1 Samuel 19:15**

And Saoul sent for David, saying, Bring him to me on the bed, so as to put him to death.

**1 Samuel 19:16**

And the messengers come, and behold, the tomb-images were on the bed and a goat’s liver at his head.

**1 Samuel 19:17**

And Saoul said to Melchol, Why did you thus deceive me and send away my enemy, and he escaped? And Melchol said to Saoul, He said, Send me away, or else I will kill you.

**1 Samuel 19:18**

And David fled and was saved and comes to Samouēl at Armathaim and reports to him all that Saoul did to him. And David and Samouēl went and sat in Nauath at Rama.

**1 Samuel 19:19**

And it was reported to Saoul, saying, Behold, David is in Nauath at Rama.

**1 Samuel 19:20**

And Saoul sent messengers to take David, and they saw the assembly of the prophets, and Samouēl stood appointed over them. And the Spirit of God came upon the messengers of Saoul, and they prophesy.

**1 Samuel 19:21**

And it was reported to Saoul, and he sent other messengers, and they also prophesied. And Saoul added to send third messengers, and they also prophesied.

**1 Samuel 19:22**

And the anger of Saoul burned, and he also went to Armathaim, and he comes as far as the well of the threshing floor in Sephi and asked and said, Where are Samouēl and David? And they said, Behold, in Nauath at Rama.

**1 Samuel 19:23**

And he went from there to Nauath at Rama, and the Spirit of God also came upon him, and he went on prophesying until he came into Nauath at Rama.

**1 Samuel 19:24**

And he stripped off his garments and prophesied before them and fell naked all that day and all that night. Because of this they said, Is Saoul also among prophets?

### Chapter 20

**1 Samuel 20:1**

And David fled from Nauath at Rama and comes before Iōnathan and said, What have I done, and what is my wrongdoing, and in what have I sinned before your father, that he seeks my life?

**1 Samuel 20:2**

And Iōnathan said to him, Far from you. You certainly will not die. Behold, my father will not do a great word or a small one without uncovering my ear, and why should my father hide this word from me? It is not so.

**1 Samuel 20:3**

And David answered Iōnathan and said, Knowing, your father knows that I have found favor in your eyes, and he said, Let not Iōnathan know this, lest he not be willing. But as the Lord lives and as your life lives, as I said, there is only the fullness between me and death.

**1 Samuel 20:4**

And Iōnathan said to David, Whatever your soul desires, I will do for you.

**1 Samuel 20:5**

And David said to Iōnathan, Behold now, new moon is tomorrow, and sitting I will not sit with the king to eat, and you will send me away, and I will hide in the field until evening.

**1 Samuel 20:6**

If your father inspecting should inspect for me, then you will say, David earnestly asked leave from me to run to Bēthleem his city, because there is there a sacrifice of days for all the tribe.

**1 Samuel 20:7**

If he says thus, Good, there is peace for your servant. But if he answers harshly, know that evil is completed by him.

**1 Samuel 20:8**

And you will do mercy with your servant, because you brought your servant into a covenant of the Lord with yourself. And if there is wrongdoing in your servant, you put me to death, and why do you thus bring me to your father?

**1 Samuel 20:9**

And Iōnathan said, Far from you. For if in knowing I know that evil has been completed by my father to come upon you, will I not report it to you even into your cities?

**1 Samuel 20:10**

And David said to Iōnathan, Who will report to me if your father answers you harshly?

**1 Samuel 20:11**

And Iōnathan said to David, Go and remain in the field. And both went out into the field.

**1 Samuel 20:12**

And Iōnathan said to David, The Lord God of Israel knows that I will search out my father about this time tomorrow and the third day, and behold, if there is good concerning David and I do not send to you into the field,

**1 Samuel 20:13**

thus may God do to Iōnathan and thus may he add, if I bring the evils upon you and do not uncover your ear and send you away, and you go in peace. And the Lord will be with you as he was with my father.

**1 Samuel 20:14**

And if I am still living, you will indeed do mercy with me, and if I surely die,

**1 Samuel 20:15**

you will not remove your mercy from my house forever, and not even when the Lord removes the enemies of David, each one from the face of the earth.

**1 Samuel 20:16**

May the name of Iōnathan be removed from the house of David, and may the Lord seek out the enemies of David.

**1 Samuel 20:17**

And Iōnathan added still to swear to David, because he loved the soul of the one loving him.

**1 Samuel 20:18**

And Iōnathan said, Tomorrow is new moon, and you will be missed, because your seat will be inspected.

**1 Samuel 20:19**

And you will do it a third time and inspect, and you will come to your place where you hid on the working day, and you will sit beside that Ergab.

**1 Samuel 20:20**

And I will make the third shot with arrows, sending toward Amattari.

**1 Samuel 20:21**

And behold, I will send the young man, saying, Come, find the arrow for me. If in saying I say to the young man, Here is the arrow from you and on this side, take it, come, because there is peace for you and there is no word, as the Lord lives.

**1 Samuel 20:22**

But if I say thus to the young man, Here is the arrow from you and beyond, go, because the Lord has sent you away.

**1 Samuel 20:23**

And the word that we spoke, I and you, behold, the Lord is witness between me and you forever.

**1 Samuel 20:24**

And David hid in the field, and the month arrives, and the king comes to the table to eat.

**1 Samuel 20:25**

And the king sat on his seat, as once and once, on the seat by the wall, and he came before Iōnathan, and Abennēr sat by the side of Saoul, and David’s place was inspected.

**1 Samuel 20:26**

And Saoul did not speak anything on that day, because he said, An incident appears, he is not clean, because he has not been purified.

**1 Samuel 20:27**

And it came to be on the next day of the month, the second day, David’s place was inspected, and Saoul said to Iōnathan his son, Why is the son of Iessai not present, both yesterday and today, at the table?

**1 Samuel 20:28**

And Iōnathan answered Saoul and said to him, David has earnestly requested from me to go to Bēthleem his city,

**1 Samuel 20:29**

and he said, Send me away now, because there is for us a tribal sacrifice in the city, and my brothers have given charge to me, and now if I have found favor in your eyes, I will indeed escape and see my brothers. Because of this he has not come to the king’s table.

**1 Samuel 20:30**

And the anger of Saoul burned very greatly against Iōnathan, and he said to him, Son of fleeing girls, for I know that you share with the son of Iessai to your shame and to the shame of your mother’s nakedness.

**1 Samuel 20:31**

Because all the days that the son of Iessai lives upon the earth, your kingdom will not be established. Now therefore, send and take the young man, because he is a son of death.

**1 Samuel 20:32**

And Iōnathan answered Saoul, Why should he die? What has he done?

**1 Samuel 20:33**

And Saoul lifted the spear against Iōnathan to put him to death, and Iōnathan knew that this evil from his father had been completed, to put David to death.

**1 Samuel 20:34**

And Iōnathan sprang up from the table in anger of wrath and did not eat bread on the second of the month, because he was shattered over David, because his father had brought it to completion against him.

**1 Samuel 20:35**

And it came to be in the morning, Iōnathan went out into the field, as he had appointed, for the testimony with David, and a little young man was with him.

**1 Samuel 20:36**

And he said to the young man, Run, find for me the arrows in which I am shooting. And the young man ran, and he shot the arrow and brought it past him.

**1 Samuel 20:37**

And the young man came as far as the place of the arrow that Iōnathan shot, and Iōnathan cried out behind the young boy and said, Is not the arrow from you and beyond?

**1 Samuel 20:38**

And Iōnathan cried out behind his young man, saying, Hurry, make haste, do not stand. And the young man of Iōnathan gathered the arrows to his lord.

**1 Samuel 20:39**

And the young man knew nothing, except that Iōnathan and David knew the word.

**1 Samuel 20:40**

And Iōnathan gave his equipment to his young man and said to his young man, Go, enter into the city.

**1 Samuel 20:41**

And as the young man entered, David arose from Ergab and fell on his face and bowed down to him three times, and each kissed his neighbor, and each wept to his neighbor until great completion.

**1 Samuel 20:42**

And Iōnathan said, Go in peace, and as we two swore in the name of the Lord, saying, The Lord will be witness between me and you and between my seed and between your seed forever.

### Chapter 21

**1 Samuel 21:1**

And David rose and went away, and Iōnathan entered into the city.

**1 Samuel 21:2**

And David comes to Nomba to Abimelech the priest, and Abimelech stood outside himself to meet him and said to him, Why are you alone, and no one with you?

**1 Samuel 21:3**

And David said to the priest, The king has charged me with a word today and said to me, Let no one know the word concerning which I am sending you and concerning which I have charged you. And I have directed the young men to the place called God’s faith, Phellani, Alemoni.

And now, if there are five loaves under your hand, give into my hand what is found.

And the priest answered David and said, There are no common breads under my hand, but only holy breads are here, if the young men have kept themselves from woman, and he will eat.

**1 Samuel 21:6**

And David answered the priest and said to him, On the contrary, we have been kept from woman yesterday and the third day since my going out on the road. All the young men have become purified, and this road is common, because today it will be sanctified by my equipment.

**1 Samuel 21:7**

And Abimelech the priest gave him the loaves of presentation, because there was no bread there except the breads of the presence, the ones removed from the face of the Lord, to set warm bread on the day he took them.

**1 Samuel 21:8**

And there was there one of the servants of Saoul on that day, held in before the Lord, and his name was Dōēk the Syrian, pasturing the mules of Saoul.

**1 Samuel 21:9**

And David said to Abimelech, Look, is there here under your hand spear or sword? Because I did not take my sword and my equipment in my hand, because the king’s word was in haste.

**1 Samuel 21:10**

And the priest said, Behold, the sword of Goliath the foreigner, whom you struck in the valley of Ela, and it is wrapped in a garment. If you will take it for yourself, take it, because there is no other besides this here. And David said, Behold, there is none like it. Give it to me.

**1 Samuel 21:11**

And he gave it to him. And David rose and fled on that day from before Saoul, and David came to Anchous king of Geth.

**1 Samuel 21:12**

And the servants of Anchous said to him, Is not this David, king of the land? Is it not to this one that the dancers came out, saying, Saoul struck in his thousands, and David in his tens of thousands?

**1 Samuel 21:13**

And David put the words in his heart and feared greatly from before Anchous king of Geth.

**1 Samuel 21:14**

And he altered his face before him and pretended on that day, and was drumming on the doors of the city, and was carried along in his hands, and was falling on the doors of the gate, and his saliva was running down on his beard.

**1 Samuel 21:15**

And Anchous said to his servants, Behold, you see a possessed man. Why did you bring him to me?

**1 Samuel 21:16**

Do I lack possessed men, that you have brought him for acting possessed toward me? This one will not enter into the house.

### Chapter 22

**1 Samuel 22:1**

And David went away from there and was saved and comes into the cave of Odollam, and his brothers and all his father’s house heard and came down there to him.

**1 Samuel 22:2**

And everyone in distress and everyone in debt and everyone bitter in soul gathered to him, and he was leader over them, and there were with him about four hundred men.

**1 Samuel 22:3**

And David went from there to Massēpha of Mōab and said to the king of Mōab, Let now my father and my mother be with you until I know what God will do to me.

**1 Samuel 22:4**

And he entreated the face of the king of Mōab, and they stayed with him all the days David was in the stronghold.

**1 Samuel 22:5**

And Gad the prophet said to David, Do not sit in the stronghold. Go, and you will come into the land of Iouda. And David went and came and sat in the city of Sarich.

**1 Samuel 22:6**

And Saoul heard that David and the men with him had become known. And Saoul was sitting on the hill under the tamarisk tree in Rama, and the spear was in his hand, and all his servants stood by him.

**1 Samuel 22:7**

And Saoul said to his servants standing by him, Hear now, sons of Benjamin. Will the son of Iessai truly give to all of you fields and vineyards and appoint all of you centurions and commanders of thousands,

**1 Samuel 22:8**

that all of you conspire against me, and there is no one uncovering my ear when my son makes a covenant with the son of Iessai, and there is no one among you grieved concerning me and uncovering my ear that my son has stirred up my servant against me as an enemy, as this day?

**1 Samuel 22:9**

And Dōēk the Syrian answered, the one set over the mules of Saoul, and said, I saw the son of Iessai coming to Nomba to Abimelech son of Achitōb the priest.

**1 Samuel 22:10**

And he inquired for him through God and gave him provisions and gave him the sword of Goliath the foreigner.

**1 Samuel 22:11**

And the king sent to call Abimelech son of Achitōb and all the sons of his father, the priests in Nomba, and all came to the king.

**1 Samuel 22:12**

And Saoul said, Hear now, son of Achitōb. And he said, Behold, I am here, speak, lord.

**1 Samuel 22:13**

And Saoul said to him, Why did you conspire against me, you and the son of Iessai, by giving him bread and sword and by inquiring for him through God, to set him against me as an enemy, as this day?

**1 Samuel 22:14**

And he answered the king and said, And who among all your servants is like David, faithful and son-in-law of the king and ruler of all your commands and honored in your house?

**1 Samuel 22:15**

Have I begun today to inquire for him through God? Far be it. Let not the king put a word against his servant and against all the house of my father, because your servant knew nothing in all these things, small or great.

**1 Samuel 22:16**

And king Saoul said, Dying you will die, Abimelech, you and all your father’s house.

**1 Samuel 22:17**

And the king said to the runners standing over him, Bring forward and kill the priests of the Lord, because their hand is with David, and because they knew that he was fleeing and did not uncover my ear. And the servants of the king were not willing to bring their hands upon the priests of the Lord.

**1 Samuel 22:18**

And the king said to Dōēk, Turn yourself and attack the priests. And Dōēk the Syrian turned and killed the priests of the Lord on that day, three hundred and five men, all carrying ephod.

**1 Samuel 22:19**

And he struck Nomba, the city of the priests, by the mouth of the sword, from man to woman, from infant to nursing child, and ox and donkey and sheep.

**1 Samuel 22:20**

And one son of Abimelech son of Achitōb escaped, and his name was Abiathar, and he fled after David.

**1 Samuel 22:21**

And Abiathar reported to David that Saoul had killed all the priests of the Lord.

**1 Samuel 22:22**

And David said to Abiathar, I knew on that day that Dōēk the Syrian would surely report to Saoul. I am guilty for the lives of your father’s house.

**1 Samuel 22:23**

Stay with me. Do not fear, because where I seek my life, I will seek a place for your life, because you are guarded with me.

### Chapter 23

**1 Samuel 23:1**

And it was reported to David, saying, Behold, the foreigners are making war at Keila, and they are plundering and trampling the threshing floors.

**1 Samuel 23:2**

And David inquired through the Lord, saying, Shall I go and strike these foreigners? And the Lord said, Go, and you will strike these foreigners and save Keila.

**1 Samuel 23:3**

And the men of David said to him, Behold, we here in Ioudaia are afraid, and how will it be if we go to Keila? We will enter into the spoils of the foreigners.

**1 Samuel 23:4**

And David added still to inquire through the Lord, and the Lord answered him and said to him, Rise and go down to Keila, because I am delivering the foreigners into your hands.

**1 Samuel 23:5**

And David and the men with him went to Keila and fought among the foreigners, and they fled from before him, and he brought away their cattle and struck among them a great blow, and David saved the inhabitants of Keila.

**1 Samuel 23:6**

And it came to be when Abiathar son of Abimelech fled to David, he himself went down with David into Keila, having ephod in his hand.

**1 Samuel 23:7**

And it was reported to Saoul that David had come to Keila, and Saoul said, God has sold him into my hands, because he has shut himself in by entering a city of doors and bars.

**1 Samuel 23:8**

And Saoul ordered all the people for war, to go down to Keila, to hem in David and his men.

**1 Samuel 23:9**

And David knew that Saoul was not silent about evil against him, and David said to Abiathar the priest, Bring near the ephod of the Lord.

**1 Samuel 23:10**

And David said, Lord God of Israel, your servant has surely heard that Saoul seeks to come against Keila to destroy the city because of me.

**1 Samuel 23:11**

Will it be shut up? And now will Saoul come down, as your servant has heard? Lord God of Israel, report to your servant. And the Lord said, It will be shut up.

**1 Samuel 23:13**

And David rose, and the men with him, about four hundred, and they went out from Keila and were going wherever they went. And it was reported to Saoul that David had escaped from Keila, and he let go of going out.

**1 Samuel 23:14**

And David sat in the wilderness in Maserem in the narrow places, and he sat in the wilderness on the mountain of Ziph in the dry land, and Saoul sought him all the days, but the Lord did not deliver him into his hands.

**1 Samuel 23:15**

And David saw that Saoul was going out to seek David, and David was on the dry mountain in the New Place of Ziph.

**1 Samuel 23:16**

And Iōnathan son of Saoul rose and went to David into the New Place and strengthened his hands in the Lord.

**1 Samuel 23:17**

And he said to him, Do not fear, because the hand of Saoul my father certainly will not find you, and you will reign over Israel, and I will be second to you, and Saoul my father also knows thus.

**1 Samuel 23:18**

And both made a covenant before the Lord, and David sat in the New Place, and Iōnathan went away to his house.

**1 Samuel 23:19**

And the Ziphites went up from the dry land to Saoul on the hill, saying, Is not David hidden with us in Messara in the narrow places, in the New Place on the mountain of Echela, which is on the right of Iessaimoun?

**1 Samuel 23:20**

And now let the king come down with all the desire of his soul for going down. They have shut him into the hands of the king.

**1 Samuel 23:21**

And Saoul said to them, Blessed are you to the Lord, because you grieved for me.

**1 Samuel 23:22**

Go now and prepare still more, and know his place, where his foot will be in haste there, where you said, Lest perhaps he act craftily.

**1 Samuel 23:23**

And see and know, and we will go with you, and if he is on the land, I will search him out in all the thousands of Iouda.

**1 Samuel 23:24**

And the Ziphites rose and went before Saoul, and David and his men were in the wilderness of Maan, toward evening, on the right of Iessaimoun.

**1 Samuel 23:25**

And Saoul and his men went to seek him, and they reported to David, and he went down to the rock in the wilderness of Maan. And Saoul heard and pursued after David into the wilderness of Maan.

**1 Samuel 23:26**

And Saoul and his men were going from one side of this mountain, and David and his men from the side of that mountain, and David was hiding himself to go from before Saoul, and Saoul and his men had camped against David and his men to seize them.

**1 Samuel 23:27**

And a messenger came to Saoul, saying, Hasten and come, because the foreigners have attacked the land.

**1 Samuel 23:28**

And Saoul turned back from pursuing after David and went to meet the foreigners. Because of this that place was called Divided Rock.

### Chapter 24

**1 Samuel 24:1**

And David went up from there and sat in the narrow places of Engaddi.

**1 Samuel 24:2**

And it came to be as Saoul turned back from after the foreigners, that it was reported to him saying that David was in the wilderness of Engaddi.

**1 Samuel 24:3**

And he took with himself three thousand chosen men from all Israel and went to seek David and his men upon the face of Saddaeim.

**1 Samuel 24:4**

**1 Samuel 24:5**

And the men of David said to him, Behold, this day of which the Lord spoke to you, to deliver your enemy into your hands, and you will do to him as good in your eyes. And David rose and removed the wing of Saoul’s double cloak secretly.

**1 Samuel 24:6**

And it came to be after these things that David’s heart struck him because he had removed the wing of his double cloak.

**1 Samuel 24:7**

And David said to his men, Far be it from me before the Lord if I do this thing to my lord, the anointed of the Lord, to bring my hand upon him, because this one is anointed of the Lord.

**1 Samuel 24:8**

And David persuaded his men with words and did not let them rise to put Saoul to death, and Saoul rose and went down on the road.

**1 Samuel 24:9**

And David rose after him from the cave and cried out behind Saoul, saying, Lord king. And Saoul looked behind him, and David bent his face to the ground and bowed down to him.

**1 Samuel 24:10**

And David said to Saoul, Why do you listen to the words of the people saying, Behold, David seeks your life?

**1 Samuel 24:11**

Behold, on this day your eyes have seen that the Lord delivered you today into my hand in the cave, and I was not willing to kill you, and I spared you and said, I will not put my hand upon my lord, because he is anointed of the Lord.

**1 Samuel 24:12**

And behold, the wing of your double cloak is in my hand. I removed the wing and did not kill you. Know and see today that there is no evil in my hand, nor impiety and revolt, and I have not sinned against you, but you bind my life to take it.

**1 Samuel 24:13**

May the Lord judge between me and you, and may the Lord avenge me from you, but my hand will not be upon you.

**1 Samuel 24:14**

As the ancient proverb says, From lawless ones wrongdoing will go out, but my hand will not be upon you.

**1 Samuel 24:15**

And now, after whom do you come out, king of Israel? After whom do you pursue? After a dead dog and after one flea.

**1 Samuel 24:16**

May the Lord become judge and justice between me and you. May the Lord see and judge my judgment and give me justice from your hand.

**1 Samuel 24:17**

And it came to be, when David finished speaking these words to Saoul, Saoul said, Is this your voice, child David? And Saoul lifted up his voice and wept.

**1 Samuel 24:18**

And Saoul said to David, You are more righteous than I, because you repaid me good things, but I repaid you evil things.

**1 Samuel 24:19**

And you reported to me today what good things you did to me, how the Lord shut me up today into your hands and you did not kill me.

**1 Samuel 24:20**

And because if anyone should find his enemy in affliction and send him away on a good road, then the Lord will repay him good things, as you have done today.

**1 Samuel 24:21**

And now, behold, I know that in reigning you will reign, and the kingdom of Israel will stand in your hands.

**1 Samuel 24:22**

And now swear to me by the Lord that you will not destroy my seed after me and will not wipe out my name from the house of my father.

**1 Samuel 24:23**

And David swore to Saoul, and Saoul went away to his place, and David and his men went up to the narrow Messara.

### Chapter 25

**1 Samuel 25:1**

And Samouēl died, and all Israel gathered and mourned for him and buried him in his house at Armathaim. And David rose and went down into the wilderness of Maan.

**1 Samuel 25:2**

And there was a man in Maan, and his flocks were in Karmēl, and the man was very great, and he had three thousand sheep and one thousand goats. And it came to be when he was shearing his flock in Karmēl,

**1 Samuel 25:3**

the name of the man was Nabal, and the name of his wife was Abigaia, and his wife was good in understanding and very beautiful in appearance, but the man was harsh and evil in practices, and the man was doglike.

**1 Samuel 25:4**

And David heard in the wilderness that Nabal the Karmelite was shearing his flock.

**1 Samuel 25:5**

And David sent ten young men and said to the young men, Go up to Karmēl and go to Nabal and ask him in my name about peace.

**1 Samuel 25:6**

And you will say these things at the season: And you are in health, and your house, and all your things in health.

**1 Samuel 25:7**

And now behold, I have heard that they are shearing for you. Now your shepherds who were with us in the wilderness, we did not hinder them, and we did not command anything from them all the days they were in Karmēl.

**1 Samuel 25:8**

Ask your young men, and they will report to you. And let the young men find favor in your eyes, because we have come on a good day. Give now whatever your hand may find to your son David.

**1 Samuel 25:9**

And the young men come and speak these words to Nabal according to all these words in the name of David, and he sprang away.

**1 Samuel 25:10**

**1 Samuel 25:11**

And shall I take my breads and my wine and my victims that I have slaughtered for those shearing my sheep and give them to men whose origin I do not know?

**1 Samuel 25:12**

And David’s young men turned on their way and returned and came and reported to David according to these words.

**1 Samuel 25:13**

And David said to his men, Gird on each his sword. And about four hundred men went up after David, and two hundred sat with the baggage.

**1 Samuel 25:14**

**1 Samuel 25:15**

And the men were very good to us. They did not hinder us, nor did they command anything to us all the days we were with them and while we were in the field.

**1 Samuel 25:16**

They were like a wall around us, both night and day, all the days we were with them shepherding the flock.

**1 Samuel 25:17**

And now know and see what you will do, because evil has been completed against our lord and against his house, and he is a pestilent son, and no one can speak to him.

**1 Samuel 25:18**

And Abigaia hurried and took two hundred loaves and two vessels of wine and five prepared sheep and five ophi of fine flour and one gomor of raisins and two hundred cakes and put them on the donkeys.

**1 Samuel 25:19**

And she said to her young men, Go on before me, and behold, I am coming behind you. But to her husband she did not report it.

**1 Samuel 25:20**

And it came to be, as she was mounted on the donkey and going down under the shelter of the mountain, behold, David and his men were coming down to meet her, and she met them.

**1 Samuel 25:21**

And David said, Perhaps in vain I have guarded all his things in the wilderness, and we did not command taking anything from all his things, and he repaid me evil instead of good.

**1 Samuel 25:22**

Thus may God do to David and thus may he add, if I leave from all the things of Nabal until morning one who urinates against a wall.

**1 Samuel 25:23**

And Abigaia saw David and hurried and sprang down from the donkey and fell before David on her face and bowed down to him on the ground.

**1 Samuel 25:24**

**1 Samuel 25:25**

Let not my lord set his heart on this pestilent man, because as his name, so he is: Nabal is his name, and folly is with him. But I your servant did not see your young men whom you sent.

**1 Samuel 25:26**

And now, my lord, as the Lord lives and as your life lives, just as the Lord kept you back from coming into innocent blood and from saving your hand for yourself, now let your enemies and the ones seeking evil for my lord become like Nabal.

**1 Samuel 25:27**

And now take this blessing that your servant has brought to my lord, and you will give it to the young men standing by my lord.

**1 Samuel 25:28**

Take away the lawless deed of your servant, because in doing the Lord will make for my lord a faithful house, because my lord fights the battles of the Lord, and evil will not be found in you ever.

**1 Samuel 25:29**

And a man will rise up pursuing you and seeking your life, and the life of my lord will be bound in the bundle of life with the Lord your God, and the life of your enemies you will sling out in the middle of the sling.

**1 Samuel 25:30**

And it will be that the Lord will do for my lord all the good things he spoke concerning you, and the Lord will appoint you as leader over Israel.

**1 Samuel 25:31**

And this will not be to you an abomination and a stumbling for my lord, to pour out innocent blood for nothing and for the hand of my lord to save for himself. And the Lord will do good to my lord, and you will remember your servant to do good to her.

**1 Samuel 25:32**

And David said to Abigaia, Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, who sent you today on this day to meet me.

**1 Samuel 25:33**

And blessed be your discernment, and blessed are you, who kept me back today on this day from coming into bloods and from saving my hand for myself.

**1 Samuel 25:34**

Except that the Lord God of Israel lives, who kept me back today from doing evil to you, because if you had not hurried and come to meet me, then I said, Surely there would have been left to Nabal until morning one urinating against a wall.

**1 Samuel 25:35**

And David took from her hand all that she brought to him and said to her, Go up in peace to your house. See, I have heard your voice and honored your face.

**1 Samuel 25:36**

**1 Samuel 25:37**

And it came to be in the morning, as Nabal sobered from the wine, his wife reported these words to him, and his heart died within him, and he became like a stone.

**1 Samuel 25:38**

**1 Samuel 25:39**

And David heard and said, Blessed be the Lord, who judged the judgment of my reproach from the hand of Nabal and preserved his servant from the hand of evils, and the Lord turned back the evil of Nabal on his own head. And David sent and spoke concerning Abigaia, to take her for himself as wife.

**1 Samuel 25:40**

And the servants of David came to Abigaia at Karmēl and spoke to her, saying, David has sent us to you, to take you for himself as wife.

**1 Samuel 25:41**

And she rose and bowed down to the ground on her face and said, Behold, your servant is for a slave-girl to wash the feet of your servants.

**1 Samuel 25:42**

And Abigaia rose and mounted the donkey, and five girls were following her, and she went behind the servants of David and became his wife.

**1 Samuel 25:43**

And David took Achinaam from Iezraēl, and both became his wives.

**1 Samuel 25:44**

And Saoul gave Melchol his daughter, the wife of David, to Phalti son of Lais from Romma.

### Chapter 26

**1 Samuel 26:1**

And the Ziphites come from the dry land to Saoul on the hill, saying, Behold, David is hiding with us on the mountain of Echela, opposite Iessaimoun.

**1 Samuel 26:2**

And Saoul rose and went down into the wilderness of Ziph, and with him were three thousand chosen men from Israel, to seek David in the wilderness of Ziph.

**1 Samuel 26:3**

And Saoul camped on the mountain of Echela opposite Iessaimoun by the road, and David sat in the wilderness, and David saw that Saoul came after him into the wilderness.

**1 Samuel 26:4**

And David sent spies and knew that Saoul came prepared from Keila.

**1 Samuel 26:5**

And David rose secretly and enters into the place where Saoul was sleeping there, and there was Abennēr son of Nēr, his commander, and Saoul was sleeping in the wagon circle, and the people had camped around him.

**1 Samuel 26:6**

And David answered and said to Achimelech the Hittite and to Abessa son of Sarouia, brother of Iōab, saying, Who will go in with me to Saoul into the camp? And Abessa said, I will go in with you.

**1 Samuel 26:7**

**1 Samuel 26:8**

**1 Samuel 26:9**

And David said to Abessa, Do not humble him, because who will bring his hand upon the anointed of the Lord and be held innocent?

**1 Samuel 26:10**

And David said, As the Lord lives, unless the Lord strikes him, or his day comes and he dies, or he goes down into battle and is swept away,

**1 Samuel 26:11**

far be it from me before the Lord to bring my hand upon the anointed of the Lord. And now take the spear from his head and the flask of water, and let us go for ourselves.

**1 Samuel 26:12**

And David took the spear and the flask of water from his head, and they went away by themselves, and there was none seeing and none knowing and none waking; all were sleeping, because astonishment from the Lord had fallen upon them.

**1 Samuel 26:13**

And David crossed over to the other side and stood on the top of the mountain far off, and the road between them was great.

**1 Samuel 26:14**

And David called to the people and spoke to Abennēr, saying, Will you not answer, Abennēr? And Abennēr answered and said, Who are you, the one calling me?

**1 Samuel 26:15**

And David said to Abennēr, Are you not a man, and who is like you in Israel? And why do you not guard your lord the king? Because one from the people entered to destroy your lord the king.

**1 Samuel 26:16**

**1 Samuel 26:17**

And Saoul recognized the voice of David and said, Is this your voice, child David? And David said, Your servant, lord king.

**1 Samuel 26:18**

And he said, Why is my lord pursuing after his servant? Because in what have I sinned, and what wrongdoing has been found in me?

**1 Samuel 26:19**

And now let my lord the king hear the word of his servant. If God stirs you up against me, may he smell your sacrifices. But if sons of men, cursed are these before the Lord, because they cast me out today from being established in the inheritance of the Lord, saying, Go, serve other gods.

**1 Samuel 26:20**

And now let not my blood fall to the ground opposite the face of the Lord, because the king of Israel has come out seeking my life, as the night-raven pursues in the mountains.

**1 Samuel 26:21**

And Saoul said, I have sinned. Return, child David, because I will not do evil to you, because my life was precious in your eyes on this day. I have been made foolish and have been very greatly ignorant.

**1 Samuel 26:22**

And David answered and said, Behold, the spear of the king. Let one of the young men cross over and take it.

**1 Samuel 26:23**

And the Lord will return to each his righteousness and his faithfulness, just as the Lord delivered you today into my hands, and I was not willing to bring my hand upon the anointed of the Lord.

**1 Samuel 26:24**

And behold, just as your life was magnified today on this day in my eyes, so may my life be magnified before the Lord, and may he shelter me and deliver me from all affliction.

**1 Samuel 26:25**

And Saoul said to David, Blessed are you, child; doing you will do, and prevailing you will prevail. And David went on his way, and Saoul returned to his place.

### Chapter 27

**1 Samuel 27:1**

And David said in his heart, saying, Now one day I will be swept away into the hands of Saoul, and there is nothing good for me unless I am saved into the land of the foreigners. And Saoul will let go of seeking me in every border of Israel, and I will be saved from his hand.

**1 Samuel 27:2**

And David rose, and the four hundred men with him, and went to Anchous son of Ammach, king of Geth.

**1 Samuel 27:3**

And it was reported to Saoul that David had fled to Geth, and he no longer added to seek him.

**1 Samuel 27:6**

**1 Samuel 27:7**

**1 Samuel 27:8**

**1 Samuel 27:9**

And he would strike the land and would not keep alive man and woman, and he took flocks and herds and donkeys and camels and clothing, and they returned and came to Anchous.

**1 Samuel 27:10**

And Anchous said to David, Against whom did you attack today? And David said to Anchous, Against the south of Ioudaia and against the south of Iesmega and against the south of the Kenezite.

**1 Samuel 27:11**

And he did not keep alive man and woman to bring into Geth, saying, Lest they report in Geth against us, saying, Thus David does. And this was his rule all the days David sat in the countryside of the foreigners.

**1 Samuel 27:12**

And David was deeply trusted by Anchous, saying, In shaming he has been shamed among his people in Israel, and he will be my servant forever.

### Chapter 28

**1 Samuel 28:1**

And it came to be in those days, the foreigners gathered in their camps to go out to fight against Israel. And Anchous said to David, In knowing you will know that you and your men will go out with me into battle.

**1 Samuel 28:2**

And David said to Anchous, Thus now you will know what your servant will do. And Anchous said to David, Thus I will appoint you chief bodyguard all the days.

**1 Samuel 28:3**

And Samouēl died, and all Israel mourned for him and buried him in Armathaim, in his city. And Saoul removed the ventriloquists and the knowers from the land.

**1 Samuel 28:4**

And the foreigners gather and come and camp in Sōman, and Saoul gathers every man of Israel and they camp in Gelboue.

**1 Samuel 28:5**

And Saoul saw the camp of the foreigners and feared, and his heart stood outside itself greatly.

**1 Samuel 28:6**

And Saoul inquired through the Lord, and the Lord did not answer him in dreams and in manifestations and in prophets.

**1 Samuel 28:7**

And Saoul said to his servants, Seek for me a ventriloquist woman, and I will go to her and inquire by her. And his servants said to him, Behold, there is a ventriloquist woman in Aendōr.

**1 Samuel 28:8**

And Saoul disguised himself and clothed himself with other garments, and he goes, he and two men with him, and they come to the woman by night, and he said to her, Divine for me now by the ventriloquist, and bring up for me whomever I tell you.

**1 Samuel 28:9**

And the woman said to him, Behold now, you know what Saoul did, how he destroyed the ventriloquists and the knowers from the land. And why are you trapping my life to put it to death?

**1 Samuel 28:10**

And Saoul swore to her, saying, As the Lord lives, wrongdoing will not meet you in this matter.

**1 Samuel 28:11**

And the woman said, Whom shall I bring up for you? And he said, Bring up Samouēl for me.

**1 Samuel 28:12**

And the woman saw Samouēl and cried out with a great voice, and the woman said to Saoul, Why did you deceive me? And you are Saoul.

**1 Samuel 28:13**

And the king said to her, Do not fear. Tell me, what have you seen? And she said to him, I have seen gods coming up from the earth.

**1 Samuel 28:14**

And he said to her, What did you recognize? And she said to him, An upright man coming up from the earth, and he had a double cloak wrapped around him. And Saoul knew that this was Samouēl, and he bent on his face to the ground and bowed down to him.

**1 Samuel 28:15**

And Samouēl said, Why have you disturbed me, to bring me up? And Saoul said, I am in great distress, and the foreigners are fighting against me, and God has departed from me and no longer listened to me, both by the hand of prophets and in dreams. And now I have called you to make known to me what I shall do.

**1 Samuel 28:16**

And Samouēl said, Why do you ask me, since the Lord has departed from you and has come to be with your neighbor?

**1 Samuel 28:17**

And the Lord has done for you just as he spoke by my hand, and the Lord will tear your kingdom from your hand and give it to your neighbor, to David.

**1 Samuel 28:18**

Because you did not hear the voice of the Lord and did not carry out the anger of his wrath in Amalēk, because of this thing the Lord has done this to you on this day.

**1 Samuel 28:19**

And the Lord will deliver Israel with you into the hands of the foreigners, and tomorrow you and your sons with you will fall, and the camp of Israel the Lord will give into the hands of the foreigners.

**1 Samuel 28:20**

And Saoul hurried and fell standing to the ground, and he feared greatly from the words of Samouēl, and there was no strength in him still, because he had not eaten bread all that day and all that night.

**1 Samuel 28:21**

And the woman came in to Saoul and saw that he had been greatly shaken, and she said to him, Behold now, your servant listened to your voice and set my life in my hand, and I listened to the words you spoke to me.

**1 Samuel 28:22**

And now listen now to the voice of your servant, and I will set before you a morsel of bread, and eat, and there will be strength in you because you will go on the road.

**1 Samuel 28:23**

And he was not willing to eat, and his servants and the woman pressed him, and he listened to their voice and rose from the ground and sat on the couch.

**1 Samuel 28:24**

And the woman had a grazing heifer in the house, and she hurried and slaughtered it and took flour and kneaded it and baked unleavened bread.

**1 Samuel 28:25**

And she brought it before Saoul and before his servants, and they ate and rose and went away that night.

### Chapter 29

**1 Samuel 29:1**

And the foreigners gather all their camps in Aphek, and Israel camped in Aendōr in Iezraēl.

**1 Samuel 29:2**

And the satraps of the foreigners were passing by in hundreds and thousands, and David and his men were passing by at the rear with Anchous.

**1 Samuel 29:3**

And the satraps of the foreigners said, Who are these passing over?
