**1 Samuel 29:4**

And the generals of the foreigners were grieved over him and say to him, Turn the man back to his place where you stationed him, and let him not come with us into battle, and let him not become a plotter in the camp. And by what will this man be reconciled to his lord? Is it not by the heads of those men?

**1 Samuel 29:5**

Is not this David, to whom they came out in dances, saying, Saoul struck in his thousands, and David in his tens of thousands?

**1 Samuel 29:6**

And Anchous called David and said to him, As the Lord lives, you are upright, and good in my eyes is your going out and your coming in with me in the camp, and I have found no evil against you from the day you came to me until this day, but in the eyes of the satraps you are not good.

**1 Samuel 29:7**

And now turn back and go in peace, and you certainly will not do evil in the eyes of the satraps of the foreigners.

**1 Samuel 29:8**

And David said to Anchous, What have I done to you, and what have you found in your servant from the day I was before you until this day, that I should not come to fight the enemies of my lord the king?

**1 Samuel 29:9**

And Anchous answered David, I know that you are good in my eyes, but the satraps of the foreigners say, He will not come with us into battle.

**1 Samuel 29:10**

And now rise early in the morning, you and the servants of your lord who came with you, and go to the place where I stationed you there, and do not set a pestilent word in your heart, because you are good before me. And rise early on the road, and let it grow light for you, and go.

**1 Samuel 29:11**

And David rose early, he and his men, to depart and keep the land of the foreigners, and the foreigners went up to fight against Israel.

### Chapter 30

**1 Samuel 30:1**

And it came to be when David and his men entered into Sekelak on the third day, Amalēk attacked the south and Sekelak and struck Sekelak and burned it with fire.

**1 Samuel 30:2**

And they did not kill man or woman among the women and all in it from small to great, but they took them captive and went on their way.

**1 Samuel 30:3**

And David and his men came to the city, and behold, it had been burned with fire, and their wives and their sons and their daughters had been taken captive.

**1 Samuel 30:4**

And David and his men lifted up their voice and wept until there was no longer strength in them to weep.

**1 Samuel 30:5**

And both David’s wives had been taken captive, Achinoom the Iezraēlite and Abigaia the wife of Nabal the Karmelite.

**1 Samuel 30:6**

And David was greatly distressed, because the people spoke of stoning him, because the soul of all the people was bitter, each for his sons and for his daughters. And David strengthened himself in the Lord his God.

**1 Samuel 30:7**

And David said to Abiathar the priest son of Achimelech, Bring near the ephod.

**1 Samuel 30:8**

And David inquired through the Lord, saying, Shall I pursue after this raiding band? Shall I overtake them? And he said to him, Pursue, because overtaking you will overtake, and rescuing you will rescue.

**1 Samuel 30:9**

And David went, he and the six hundred men with him, and they come as far as the wadi Bosor, and the excess stood there.

**1 Samuel 30:10**

And David pursued with four hundred men, but two hundred men lagged behind, who sat beyond the wadi Bosor.

**1 Samuel 30:11**

And they find an Egyptian man in the field and take him and lead him to David in the field, and they give him bread, and he ate, and they gave him water to drink.

**1 Samuel 30:12**

And they gave him a piece of a cake, and he ate, and his spirit was restored within him, because he had not eaten bread and had not drunk water three days and three nights.

**1 Samuel 30:13**

And David said to him, Whose are you, and from where are you? And the Egyptian young man said, I am slave of an Amalēkite man, and my lord left me because I became sick, today the third day.

**1 Samuel 30:14**

And we attacked the south of Cholthi and the parts of Ioudaia and the south of Cheloub, and we burned Sekelak with fire.

**1 Samuel 30:15**

And David said to him, Will you lead me down against this raiding band? And he said, Swear to me by God not to put me to death and not to hand me into the hands of my lord, and I will lead you down against this raiding band.

**1 Samuel 30:16**

And he led him down there, and behold, they were spread out over the face of all the land, eating and drinking and feasting over all the great spoil they had taken from the land of the foreigners and from the land of Iouda.

**1 Samuel 30:17**

And David came upon them and struck them from dawn until evening and on the next day, and there was not saved from them a man, except four hundred young men who had mounted on the camels and fled.

**1 Samuel 30:18**

And David took away all that the Amalēkites had taken, and he rescued both his wives.

**1 Samuel 30:19**

And nothing was missing to them from small to great and from the spoil and to sons and daughters and to all that they had taken from them; David returned everything.

**1 Samuel 30:20**

And David took all the flocks and the herds and drove them before the spoils, and to those spoils it was said, These are David’s spoils.

**1 Samuel 30:21**

And David comes to the two hundred men who had become too faint to go after David, and he seated them at the wadi Bosor. And they went out to meet David and to meet the people with him, and David came near to the people, and they asked him the things of peace.

**1 Samuel 30:22**

And every pestilent and evil man of the fighting men who had gone with David answered and said, Because they did not pursue with us, we will not give them from the spoil that we rescued, except each his wife and his children; let them take them and go away.

**1 Samuel 30:23**

And David said, You will not do thus, after the Lord gave to us and guarded us and delivered the raiding band coming against us into our hands.

**1 Samuel 30:24**

And who will listen to you in these words? Because their portion is no less, for according to the portion of the one going down into battle, so will be the portion of the one sitting over the baggage; they will divide alike.

**1 Samuel 30:25**

And it came to be from that day and above, and it became an ordinance and a judgment for Israel until today.

**1 Samuel 30:26**

And David came to Sekelak and sent from the spoils to the elders of Iouda and to his neighbors, saying, Behold, from the spoils of the enemies of the Lord,

**1 Samuel 30:27**

to those in Baithsour and to those in Rama of the south and to those in Ietthor,

**1 Samuel 30:28**

and to those in Aroēr and to those in Ammadi and to those in Saphi and to those in Esthie, and to those in Geth and to those in Kinan and to those in Saphek and to those in Thimath,

**1 Samuel 30:29**

and to those in Karmēl and to those in the cities of Ieramēli and to those in the cities of the Kenezite,

**1 Samuel 30:30**

and to those in Ierimouth and to those in Bērsabee and to those in Noo,

**1 Samuel 30:31**

and to those in Chebrōn and to all the places through which David passed, he and his men.

### Chapter 31

**1 Samuel 31:1**

And the foreigners were fighting against Israel, and the men of Israel fled from before the foreigners and fell wounded on Mount Gelboue.

**1 Samuel 31:2**

And the foreigners closed with Saoul and his sons, and the foreigners struck Iōnathan and Aminadab and Melchisa, sons of Saoul.

**1 Samuel 31:3**

And the battle grew heavy against Saoul, and the men, the archers, found him, and he was wounded in the flanks.

**1 Samuel 31:4**

And Saoul said to the one carrying his equipment, Draw your sword and pierce me with it, lest these uncircumcised ones come and pierce me and mock me. But the one carrying his equipment was not willing, because he feared greatly. And Saoul took the sword and fell upon it.

**1 Samuel 31:5**

And the one carrying his equipment saw that Saoul had died, and he too fell upon his own sword and died with him.

**1 Samuel 31:6**

And Saoul died, and his three sons, and the one carrying his equipment, on that day together.

**1 Samuel 31:7**

And the men of Israel who were beyond the valley and those beyond the Jordan saw that the men of Israel had fled and that Saoul and his sons had died, and they abandoned their cities and fled, and the foreigners come and live in them.

**1 Samuel 31:8**

And it came to be on the next day, the foreigners came to strip the dead, and they find Saoul and his three sons fallen on Mount Gelboue.

**1 Samuel 31:9**

And they turned him and stripped off his equipment and send them throughout the land of the foreigners round about, proclaiming good news to their idols and to their people.

**1 Samuel 31:10**

And they placed his equipment in the temple of Astarte, and his body they fixed in the wall of Baithsan.

**1 Samuel 31:11**

And the inhabitants of Iabis of Galaaditēs heard what the foreigners had done to Saoul.

**1 Samuel 31:12**

And every mighty man rose and went all the night and took the body of Saoul and the body of Iōnathan his son from the wall of Baithsan and bring them into Iabis and burn them there.

**1 Samuel 31:13**

And they took their bones and buried them under the tamarisk tree at Iabis and fasted seven days.

## 2 Samuel

### Chapter 1

**2 Samuel 1:1**

And it came to be after the death of Saoul, David returned from striking Amalēk, and David sat in Sekelak two days.

**2 Samuel 1:2**

And it came to be on the third day, behold, a man came from the camp from the people of Saoul, and his garments were torn and earth was on his head. And it came to be when he entered to David, he fell to the ground and bowed down to him.

**2 Samuel 1:3**

And David said to him, From where do you come? And he said to him, I have escaped from the camp of Israel.

**2 Samuel 1:4**

And David said to him, What is this word? Report to me. And he said, The people fled from the battle, and many of the people have fallen and died, and both Saoul and Iōnathan his son have died.

**2 Samuel 1:5**

And David said to the young man reporting to him, How do you know that Saoul and Iōnathan his son have died?

**2 Samuel 1:6**

And the young man reporting to him said, By chance I happened on Mount Gelboue, and behold, Saoul had leaned upon his spear, and behold, the chariots and the horse-commanders had joined close to him.

**2 Samuel 1:7**

And he looked behind him and saw me and called me, and I said, Behold, here I am.

**2 Samuel 1:8**

And he said to me, Who are you? And I said, I am an Amalēkite.

**2 Samuel 1:9**

And he said to me, Stand now over me and put me to death, because terrible darkness seized me, because all my life is still in me.

**2 Samuel 1:10**

And I stood over him and put him to death, because I knew that he would not live after his fall. And I took the kingship-band that was on his head and the bracelet that was on his arm and have brought them here to my lord.

**2 Samuel 1:11**

And David seized his garments and tore them, and all the men with him tore their garments.

**2 Samuel 1:12**

And they mourned and wept and fasted until evening over Saoul and over Iōnathan his son and over the people of Iouda and over the house of Israel, because they were struck by the sword.

**2 Samuel 1:13**

And David said to the young man reporting to him, From where are you? And he said, I am son of a sojourning Amalēkite man.

**2 Samuel 1:14**

And David said to him, How were you not afraid to bring your hand to destroy the anointed of the Lord?

**2 Samuel 1:15**

And David called one of his young men and said, Come near, strike him. And he struck him, and he died.

**2 Samuel 1:16**

And David said to him, Your blood is on your head, because your mouth answered against you, saying, I myself killed the anointed of the Lord.

**2 Samuel 1:17**

And David lamented this lament over Saoul and over Iōnathan his son.

**2 Samuel 1:18**

And he said to teach the sons of Iouda; behold, it is written in the Book of the Upright.

**2 Samuel 1:19**

Set up, O Israel, over your dead, upon your high places the wounded. How the mighty have fallen.

**2 Samuel 1:20**

Do not report it in Geth, and do not proclaim good news in the streets of Askalōn, lest the daughters of the foreigners rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised exult.

**2 Samuel 1:21**

Mountains of Gelboue, let no dew come down on you and no rain on you, nor fields of firstfruits, because there the shield of the mighty was defiled, the shield of Saoul not anointed with oil.

**2 Samuel 1:22**

From the blood of the wounded, from the fat of the mighty, the bow of Iōnathan did not turn back empty, and the sword of Saoul did not return empty.

**2 Samuel 1:23**

Saoul and Iōnathan, the beloved and beautiful, not separated, lovely in their life and in their death they were not divided; swifter than eagles, they were made stronger than lions.

**2 Samuel 1:24**

Daughters of Israel, weep over Saoul, the one clothing you in scarlet with your ornament, the one bringing golden ornament upon your garments.

**2 Samuel 1:25**

How the mighty have fallen in the midst of battle. Iōnathan, wounded on your high places.

**2 Samuel 1:26**

I am in pain for you, my brother Iōnathan. You were made very beautiful to me; your love to me was made wonderful beyond the love of women.

**2 Samuel 1:27**

How the mighty have fallen, and the weapons of war have perished.

### Chapter 2

**2 Samuel 2:1**

And it came to be after these things, David inquired of the Lord, saying, Shall I go up into one of the cities of Iouda? And the Lord said to him, Go up. And David said, Where shall I go up? And he said, To Chebrōn.

**2 Samuel 2:2**

And David went up there to Chebrōn, and both his wives, Achinoom the Iezraēlite and Abigaia the wife of Nabal the Karmelite.

**2 Samuel 2:3**

And the men with him, each and his household, and they lived in the cities of Chebrōn.

**2 Samuel 2:4**

And men of Iouda come and anoint David there to reign over the house of Iouda. And they reported to David, saying that the men of Iabis of Galaaditēs buried Saoul.

**2 Samuel 2:5**

And David sent messengers to the leaders of Iabis of Galaaditēs and said to them, Blessed are you to the Lord, because you did this mercy for your lord, for Saoul the anointed of the Lord, and buried him and Iōnathan his son.

**2 Samuel 2:6**

And now may the Lord do mercy and truth with you, and indeed I will do these good things with you, because you did this word.

**2 Samuel 2:7**

**2 Samuel 2:11**

**2 Samuel 2:12**

**2 Samuel 2:13**

**2 Samuel 2:14**

And Abennēr said to Iōab, Let the young men rise now and play before us. And Iōab said, Let them rise.

**2 Samuel 2:15**

And they rose and passed over by number, twelve of the sons of Benjamin belonging to Iebosthe son of Saoul, and twelve of the servants of David.

**2 Samuel 2:16**

And each seized the head of his neighbor by the hand, and his knife into the side of his neighbor, and they fall together. And the name of that place was called Portion of the Plotters, which is in Gabaōn.

**2 Samuel 2:17**

And the battle became very hard on that day, and Abennēr and the men of Israel stumbled before the servants of David.

**2 Samuel 2:18**

And there were there three sons of Sarouia: Iōab and Abessa and Asaēl, and Asaēl was swift in his feet like one gazelle in the field.

**2 Samuel 2:19**

And Asaēl pursued behind Abennēr, and he did not turn aside in going to the right or to the left from behind Abennēr.

**2 Samuel 2:20**

And Abennēr looked behind him and said, Are you this Asaēl? And he said, I am.

**2 Samuel 2:21**

And Abennēr said to him, Turn aside to the right or to the left and seize for yourself one of the young men and take for yourself his armor. But Asaēl did not want to turn aside from behind him.

**2 Samuel 2:22**

And Abennēr added still, saying to Asaēl, Stand away from me, lest I strike you to the ground. And how shall I lift my face to Iōab your brother? And where are these things? Turn toward Iōab your brother.

**2 Samuel 2:23**

And he was not willing to stand away, and Abennēr struck him with the back of the spear in the belly, and the spear came out from behind him, and he fell there and died under him. And it came to be, everyone coming to the place where Asaēl fell there and died, would stand still.

**2 Samuel 2:24**

And Iōab and Abessa pursued behind Abennēr, and the sun went down, and they came as far as the hill of Amman, which is opposite Gai on the road to the wilderness of Gabaōn.

**2 Samuel 2:25**

And the sons of Benjamin gathered behind Abennēr and became one meeting group, and they stood on the head of one hill.

**2 Samuel 2:26**

And Abennēr called to Iōab and said, Will the sword devour into victory? Do you not know that it will be bitter at the end? And until when will you not tell the people to turn back from after our brothers?

**2 Samuel 2:27**

And Iōab said, As the Lord lives, if you had not spoken, then from morning the people would have gone up, each from after his brother.

**2 Samuel 2:28**

And Iōab sounded with the trumpet, and all the people stood back and did not pursue after Israel, and they no longer added to fight.

**2 Samuel 2:29**

And Abennēr and his men went away westward all that night and crossed the Jordan and went the whole extended route and come to the camp.

**2 Samuel 2:30**

And Iōab turned back from after Abennēr and gathered all the people, and they were missing from the servants of David nineteen men and Asaēl.

**2 Samuel 2:31**

And the servants of David struck from the sons of Benjamin, from the men of Abennēr, three hundred and sixty men beside him.

**2 Samuel 2:32**

And they take Asaēl and bury him in the tomb of his father in Bēthleem, and Iōab and the men with him went all night, and it grew light for them in Chebrōn.

### Chapter 3

**2 Samuel 3:1**

And the war became long between the house of Saoul and between the house of David, and the house of David was going and growing strong, and the house of Saoul was going and growing weak.

And sons were born to David in Chebrōn, and his firstborn was Amnōn by Achinoom the Iezraēlite,

**2 Samuel 3:3**

and his second Dalouia by Abigaia the Karmelite, and the third Abessalōm son of Maacha daughter of Tholmi king of Gesir,

**2 Samuel 3:4**

and the fourth Ornia son of Phenggith, and the fifth Sabatia by Abital,

**2 Samuel 3:5**

and the sixth Ietheraam by Aigla wife of David. These were born to David in Chebrōn.

**2 Samuel 3:6**

And it came to be while the war was between the house of Saoul and between the house of David, Abennēr was holding strong the house of Saoul.

**2 Samuel 3:7**

**2 Samuel 3:8**

And Abennēr became very angry over the word of Mephibosthe and said to him, Am I a dog’s head? Today I did mercy with the house of Saoul your father and with brothers and acquaintances, and I did not defect to the house of David, and yet you seek against me over the wrongdoing of a woman today.

**2 Samuel 3:9**

Thus may God do to Abennēr and thus may he add to him, because as the Lord swore to David, thus I will do for him on this day,

**2 Samuel 3:10**

to take away the kingdom from the house of Saoul and to raise up the throne of David over Israel and over Iouda from Dan to Bērsabee.

**2 Samuel 3:11**

And Mephibosthe was no longer able to answer Abennēr a word, because he feared him.

**2 Samuel 3:12**

**2 Samuel 3:13**

And David said, I will well make a covenant with you; only one word I ask from you, saying, You will not see my face unless you bring Melchol daughter of Saoul when you come to see my face.

**2 Samuel 3:14**

And David sent messengers to Mephibosthe son of Saoul, saying, Give back to me my wife Melchol, whom I took for one hundred foreskins of foreigners.

**2 Samuel 3:15**

And Mephibosthe sent and took her from her husband, from Phaltiēl son of Sellēs.

**2 Samuel 3:16**

And her husband went with her, weeping behind her until Barakim, and Abennēr said to him, Go, return. And he returned.

**2 Samuel 3:17**

And Abennēr spoke to the elders of Israel, saying, Yesterday and the third day you were seeking David to reign over you.

**2 Samuel 3:18**

And now do it, because the Lord spoke concerning David, saying, By the hand of my servant David I will save Israel from the hand of the foreigners and from the hand of all their enemies.

**2 Samuel 3:19**

And Abennēr spoke in the ears of Benjamin, and Abennēr went to speak in the ears of David in Chebrōn all that pleased in the eyes of Israel and in the eyes of all the house of Benjamin.

**2 Samuel 3:20**

And Abennēr came to David in Chebrōn, and with him were twenty men, and David made a feast for Abennēr and for the men with him.

**2 Samuel 3:21**

And Abennēr said to David, I will rise now and go and gather to my lord the king all Israel, and I will make a covenant with you, and you will reign over all that your soul desires. And David sent Abennēr away, and he went in peace.

**2 Samuel 3:22**

And behold, the servants of David and Iōab were coming from the raid and bringing much spoil with them, and Abennēr was not with David in Chebrōn, because he had sent him away and he had gone in peace.

**2 Samuel 3:23**

And Iōab and all his army were brought in, and it was reported to Iōab, saying, Abennēr son of Nēr came to David, and he sent him away, and he went in peace.

**2 Samuel 3:24**

And Iōab came in to the king and said, What is this you have done? Behold, Abennēr came to you, and why did you send him away and he has gone in peace?

**2 Samuel 3:25**

Do you not know the evil of Abennēr son of Nēr, that he came to deceive you and to know your going out and your coming in and to know all that you do?

**2 Samuel 3:26**

And Iōab turned back from David and sent messengers after Abennēr, and they brought him back from the well of Seiram, and David did not know.

**2 Samuel 3:27**

**2 Samuel 3:28**

And David heard after this and said, Innocent am I and my kingdom from the Lord forever from the bloods of Abennēr son of Nēr.

**2 Samuel 3:29**

**2 Samuel 3:30**

And Iōab and Abessa his brother were lying in wait for Abennēr, because he killed Asaēl their brother in Gabaōn in the battle.

**2 Samuel 3:31**

And David said to Iōab and to all the people with him, Tear your garments and gird on sackcloth and mourn before Abennēr. And king David was going behind the bier.

**2 Samuel 3:32**

And they bury Abennēr in Chebrōn, and the king lifted up his voice and wept over his tomb, and all the people wept over Abennēr.

**2 Samuel 3:33**

And the king lamented over Abennēr and said, Should Abennēr die according to the death of Nabal?

**2 Samuel 3:34**

**2 Samuel 3:35**

And all the people came to make David dine with breads while it was still day, and David swore, saying, Thus may God do to me and thus may he add, if before the sun goes down I taste bread or anything whatever.

**2 Samuel 3:36**

And all the people knew, and it was pleasing before them, all that the king did before the people.

**2 Samuel 3:37**

And all the people and all Israel knew on that day that it did not come from the king to put Abennēr son of Nēr to death.

**2 Samuel 3:38**

And the king said to his servants, Do you not know that a great leader has fallen on this day in Israel?

**2 Samuel 3:39**

### Chapter 4

**2 Samuel 4:1**

And it came to be as she hurried and withdrew, he fell and became lame, and his name was Mephibosthe.

**2 Samuel 4:5**

**2 Samuel 4:9**

And David answered Rēchab and Baana his brother, sons of Remmōn the Bērōthaite, and said to them, As the Lord lives, who redeemed my life from every affliction,

**2 Samuel 4:11**

And now evil men have killed a righteous man in his house on his bed, and now I will seek out his blood from your hand and wipe you out from the earth.

**2 Samuel 4:12**

And David took still more wives and concubines from Ierousalēm after he came from Chebrōn, and there came to be still more sons and daughters to David.

**2 Samuel 5:14**

And these are the names of the ones born to him in Ierousalēm: Sammous and Sōbab and Nathan and Salōmōn,

**2 Samuel 5:15**

and Ebear and Elisous and Naphek and Iephies,

**2 Samuel 5:16**

and Elisama and Elidae and Eliphalaeth, Samae, Iessibath, Nathan, Galamaan, Iebaar, Thēsous, Elphalat, Naged, Naphek, Ianatha, Leasamys, Baalimath, Eliphalaeth.

**2 Samuel 5:17**

And the foreigners heard that David had been anointed king over Israel, and all the foreigners went up to seek David, and David heard and went down into the stronghold.

**2 Samuel 5:18**

And the foreigners come and fell in the Valley of the Titans.

**2 Samuel 5:19**

And David inquired through the Lord, saying, Shall I go up against the foreigners, and will you deliver them into my hands? And the Lord said to David, Go up, because in delivering I will deliver the foreigners into your hands.

**2 Samuel 5:20**

And David came from the upper breaches and struck the foreigners there, and David said, The Lord has broken through my enemies, the foreigners, before me, as waters break through. Because of this the name of that place was called Upper Breaches.

**2 Samuel 5:21**

And they leave their gods there, and David and the men with him took them.

**2 Samuel 5:22**

And the foreigners again added to go up and fell in the Valley of the Titans.

**2 Samuel 5:23**

And David inquired through the Lord, and the Lord said, You will not go up to meet them; turn away from them and come upon them near the grove of weeping.

**2 Samuel 5:24**

And it will be, when you hear the voice of the closing together of the grove of weeping, then you will go down to them, because then the Lord will go out before you to strike in the battle of the foreigners.

**2 Samuel 5:25**

And David did just as the Lord commanded him and struck the foreigners from Gabaōn to the land of Gazēra.

### Chapter 6

**2 Samuel 6:1**

And David gathered again every young man from Israel, about seventy thousand.

**2 Samuel 6:2**

And David rose and all the people with him from the leaders of Iouda, in the ascent to bring up from there the ark of God, on which the name of the Lord of hosts seated upon the cherubim over it had been called.

**2 Samuel 6:3**

And they set the ark of the Lord on a new wagon and took it up from the house of Aminadab on the hill, and Oza and his brothers, sons of Aminadab, were leading the wagon.

**2 Samuel 6:4**

With the ark, and his brothers were going before the ark.

**2 Samuel 6:5**

And David and the sons of Israel were playing before the Lord with fitted instruments in strength and with songs and with lyres and with harps and with tambourines and with cymbals and with pipes.

**2 Samuel 6:6**

And they come as far as the threshing floor of Nōdab, and Oza stretched out his hand upon the ark of God to hold it and seized it, because the calf pulled it aside while holding it.

**2 Samuel 6:7**

**2 Samuel 6:8**

**2 Samuel 6:9**

**2 Samuel 6:10**

**2 Samuel 6:11**

**2 Samuel 6:12**

And it was reported to king David, saying, The Lord has blessed the house of Abeddara and all his things for the sake of the ark of God. And David went and brought up the ark of the Lord from the house of Abeddara into the City of David with gladness.

**2 Samuel 6:13**

And with them were seven circles carrying the ark, and sacrifice: a calf and a lamb.

**2 Samuel 6:14**

And David was beating time with fitted instruments before the Lord, and David was clothed in an exquisite robe.

**2 Samuel 6:15**

And David and all the house of Israel brought up the ark of the Lord with shouting and with the voice of trumpet.

**2 Samuel 6:16**

**2 Samuel 6:17**

And they bring the ark of the Lord and set it in its place in the midst of the tent that David pitched for it, and David offered whole burnt offerings before the Lord and peace offerings.

**2 Samuel 6:18**

And David finished offering the whole burnt offerings and the peace offerings and blessed the people in the name of the Lord of hosts.

**2 Samuel 6:19**

And he distributed to all the people, to all the host of Israel, from Dan to Bērsabee, from man to woman, to each a cake of bread and a roasted cake and a pan-cake, and all the people went away, each to his house.

**2 Samuel 6:20**

And David returned to bless his house, and Melchol daughter of Saoul came out to meet David and blessed him and said, How glorious today was the king of Israel, who was uncovered today in the eyes of the servant-girls of his servants, just as one of the dancers uncovers himself in being uncovered.

**2 Samuel 6:21**

And David said to Melchol, I will dance before the Lord. Blessed be the Lord, who chose me over your father and over all his house, to appoint me as leader over his people, over Israel, and I will play and dance before the Lord.

**2 Samuel 6:22**

And I will uncover myself still more thus, and I will be worthless in your eyes, but with the servant-girls of whom you spoke, with them I will be glorified.

**2 Samuel 6:23**

### Chapter 7

**2 Samuel 7:1**

And it came to be when the king sat in his house, and the Lord gave him inheritance-rest all around from all his enemies around him,

**2 Samuel 7:2**

that the king said to Nathan the prophet, Behold now, I dwell in a cedar house, and the ark of God sits in the midst of the tent.

**2 Samuel 7:3**

And Nathan said to the king, All things whatever are in your heart, go and do, because the Lord is with you.

**2 Samuel 7:4**

And it came to be on that night, the word of the Lord came to Nathan, saying,

**2 Samuel 7:5**

Go and say to my servant David, Thus says the Lord: You will not build me a house for my dwelling in it.

**2 Samuel 7:6**

Because I have not dwelt in a house from the day I brought up the sons of Israel from Egypt until this day, but I was walking about in lodging and in tent.

**2 Samuel 7:7**

In all the things through which I passed in all Israel, did I ever speak a word to one tribe of Israel whom I commanded to shepherd my people Israel, saying, Why have you not built me a cedar house?

**2 Samuel 7:8**

And now thus you will say to my servant David: Thus says the Lord Almighty, I took you from the fold of the sheep, for you to be leader over my people, over Israel.

**2 Samuel 7:9**

And I was with you in all things wherever you went, and I destroyed all your enemies from before you and made you a name like the name of the great ones upon the earth.

**2 Samuel 7:10**

And I will appoint a place for my people Israel, and I will plant him, and he will tabernacle by himself and will no longer be anxious, and a son of wrongdoing will no longer add to humble him as from the beginning,

**2 Samuel 7:11**

from the days when I appointed judges over my people Israel. And I will give you rest from all your enemies, and the Lord reports to you that you will build a house for him.

**2 Samuel 7:12**

And it will be, if your days are fulfilled and you sleep with your fathers, I will raise up your seed after you, who will be from your belly, and I will make his kingdom ready.

**2 Samuel 7:13**

He will build a house for my name, and I will set upright his throne forever.

**2 Samuel 7:14**

I will be to him for a father, and he will be to me for a son, and if his wrongdoing comes, I will reprove him with the rod of men and with touches of the sons of men.

**2 Samuel 7:15**

But my mercy I will not remove from him, just as I removed it from those whom I removed from before my face.

**2 Samuel 7:16**

And his house and his kingdom will be made faithful forever before me, and his throne will be set upright forever.

**2 Samuel 7:17**

According to all these words and according to all this vision, thus Nathan spoke to David.

**2 Samuel 7:18**

And king David entered and sat before the Lord and said, Who am I, my Lord, O Lord, and what is my house, that you have loved me up to these things?

**2 Samuel 7:19**

And this was made a very small thing before you, my Lord, O Lord, and you spoke concerning the house of your servant for a long time to come. And this is the law of the human, my Lord, O Lord.

**2 Samuel 7:20**

And what will David add still to speak to you? And now you know your servant, my Lord, O Lord.

**2 Samuel 7:21**

For the sake of your word you have done and according to your heart you have done all this greatness to make it known to your servant.

**2 Samuel 7:22**

Because of making you great, my Lord, O Lord, because there is none like you, and there is no God besides you, in all things that we heard in our ears.

**2 Samuel 7:23**

And who is like your people Israel, another nation on the earth, as God led him to redeem for himself a people, to set for yourself a name, to do greatness and splendor by driving out before your people whom you redeemed for yourself from Egypt nations and tents?

**2 Samuel 7:24**

And you prepared for yourself your people Israel as a people forever, and you, Lord, became for them as God.

**2 Samuel 7:25**

And now, my Lord, O Lord, the word that you spoke concerning your servant and his house, establish forever, Lord Almighty, God of Israel, and now just as you spoke.

**2 Samuel 7:26**

May your name be magnified forever.

**2 Samuel 7:27**

Lord Almighty, God of Israel, you uncovered the ear of your servant, saying, I will build you a house. Because of this your servant found his heart to pray to you this prayer.

**2 Samuel 7:28**

And now, my Lord, O Lord, you are God, and your words will be true, and you spoke these good things concerning your servant.

**2 Samuel 7:29**

And now begin and bless the house of your servant, for it to be forever before you, because you, my Lord, O Lord, have spoken, and from your blessing the house of your servant will be blessed forever.

### Chapter 8

**2 Samuel 8:1**

And David struck Adraazar son of Raab king of Souba, as he was going to set up his hand on the river Euphrates.

And David made a name, and on his return he struck Idoumaia in Gaimel, eighteen thousand.

**2 Samuel 8:17**

### Chapter 9

**2 Samuel 9:1**

And David said, Is there still one left of the house of Saoul, that I may do mercy with him for the sake of Iōnathan?

**2 Samuel 9:2**

And from the house of Saoul there was a servant, and his name was Siba, and they call him to David, and the king said to him, Are you Siba? And he said, I am your servant.

**2 Samuel 9:3**

**2 Samuel 9:4**

And the king said, Where is he? And Siba said to the king, Behold, in the house of Machir son of Amiēl, from Ladabar.

**2 Samuel 9:5**

And king David sent and took him from the house of Machir son of Amiēl, from Ladabar.

**2 Samuel 9:6**

**2 Samuel 9:7**

And David said to him, Do not fear, because in doing I will do mercy with you for the sake of Iōnathan your father, and I will restore to you all the field of Saoul father of your father, and you will eat bread at my table continually.

**2 Samuel 9:8**

And Mephibosthe bowed down and said, What am I, your servant, that you looked upon the dead dog, one like me?

**2 Samuel 9:9**

**2 Samuel 9:10**

And work the land for him, you and your sons and your servants, and you will bring breads to the son of your lord, and he will eat them. And Mephibosthe son of your lord will continually eat bread at my table. And Siba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.

**2 Samuel 9:11**

And Siba said to the king, According to all things whatever my lord the king has commanded his servant, thus your servant will do. And Mephibosthe was eating at David’s table as one of the sons of the king.

**2 Samuel 9:12**

And to Mephibosthe there was a little son, and his name was Micha, and all the dwelling of the house of Siba were servants of Mephibosthe.

**2 Samuel 9:13**

And Mephibosthe lived in Ierousalēm, because he continually was eating at the table of the king, and he was lame in both his feet.

### Chapter 10

**2 Samuel 10:1**

And it came to be after these things, the king of the sons of Ammon died, and Anōn his son reigned instead of him.

**2 Samuel 10:2**

And David said, I will do mercy with Anōn son of Naas, in the way his father did mercy with me. And David sent to comfort him by the hand of his servants concerning his father, and the servants of David came into the land of the sons of Ammon.

**2 Samuel 10:3**

And the rulers of the sons of Ammon said to Anōn their lord, Is it to glorify your father before you that David sent comforters to you? Is it not to search the city and spy it out and inspect it that David sent his servants to you?

**2 Samuel 10:6**

**2 Samuel 10:7**

And David heard and sent Iōab and all the force, the mighty men.

**2 Samuel 10:8**

And the sons of Ammon went out and arrayed for war by the entrance of the gate, and Syria of Souba and Rōōb and Istōb and Maacha were alone in the field.

**2 Samuel 10:9**

**2 Samuel 10:10**

**2 Samuel 10:11**

And he said, If Syria grows strong beyond me, you will be for salvation to me, and if the sons of Ammon grow strong beyond you, we will be to save you.

**2 Samuel 10:12**

**2 Samuel 10:13**

And Iōab and the people with him came near to war against Syria, and they fled from before him.

**2 Samuel 10:14**

**2 Samuel 10:15**

And Syria saw that it had stumbled before Israel, and they were gathered together.

**2 Samuel 10:16**

And Adraazar sent and gathered Syria from beyond the river Chalamak, and they came to Ailam, and Sōbak, chief of the force of Adraazar, was before them.

**2 Samuel 10:17**

And it was reported to David, and he gathered all Israel and crossed the Jordan and came to Ailam, and Syria arrayed opposite David and fought with him.

**2 Samuel 10:18**

And Syria fled from before Israel, and David killed from Syria seven hundred chariots and forty thousand horsemen, and Sōbak the chief of his force he struck, and he died there.

**2 Samuel 10:19**

### Chapter 11

**2 Samuel 11:1**

And it came to be at the turning of the year, at the season of the campaigns of kings, David sent Iōab and his servants with him and all Israel, and they ravaged the sons of Ammon and sat down against Rabbath, but David sat in Ierousalēm.

**2 Samuel 11:2**

And it came to be toward evening, David rose from his bed and was walking on the roof of the king’s house, and from the roof he saw a woman bathing, and the woman was very beautiful in appearance.

**2 Samuel 11:3**

And David sent and asked about the woman, and someone said, Is not this Bērsabee daughter of Eliab, wife of Ourias the Hittite?

**2 Samuel 11:4**

And David sent messengers and took her, and he went in to her and lay with her, and she was sanctifying herself from her uncleanness, and she returned to her house.

**2 Samuel 11:5**

And the woman conceived, and having sent, she reported to David and said, I am with child.

**2 Samuel 11:6**

And David sent to Iōab, saying, Send to me Ourias the Hittite, and Iōab sent Ourias to David.

**2 Samuel 11:7**

And Ourias comes and entered to him, and David asked concerning the peace of Iōab and concerning the peace of the people and concerning the peace of the war.

**2 Samuel 11:8**

And David said to Ourias, Go down to your house and wash your feet. And Ourias went out from the king’s house, and the king’s carrying gift went out after him.

**2 Samuel 11:9**

And Ourias slept by the door of the king’s house with the servants of his lord, and he did not go down to his house.

**2 Samuel 11:10**

And they reported to David, saying that Ourias did not go down to his house, and David said to Ourias, Do you not come from a road? Why is it that you did not go down to your house?

**2 Samuel 11:11**

And Ourias said to David, The ark and Israel and Iouda dwell in tents, and my lord Iōab and the servants of my lord camp on the face of the field, and shall I enter into my house to eat and drink and to lie with my wife? As your life lives, if I do this thing.

**2 Samuel 11:12**

And David said to Ourias, Sit here today also, and tomorrow I will send you away. And Ourias sat in Ierousalēm on that day and the next day.

**2 Samuel 11:13**

And David called him, and he ate before him and drank, and he made him drunk, and he went out in the evening to lie on his bed with the servants of his lord, but to his own house he did not go down.

**2 Samuel 11:14**

And it came to be in the morning, David wrote a letter to Iōab and sent it by the hand of Ourias.

**2 Samuel 11:15**

And he wrote in the letter, saying, Bring Ourias into the front of the hard battle and turn back from behind him, and he will be struck and die.

**2 Samuel 11:16**

And it came to be while Iōab was guarding the city, he put Ourias in the place where he knew men of strength were there.

**2 Samuel 11:17**

And the men of the city came out and were fighting with Iōab, and some of the people from the servants of David fell, and also Ourias the Hittite died.

**2 Samuel 11:18**

And Iōab sent and reported to the king all the words of the war,

**2 Samuel 11:19**

and he commanded the messenger, saying, When you finish speaking all the words of the war to the king,

**2 Samuel 11:20**

it will be if the anger of the king rises and he says to you, Why did you go near the city to fight? Did you not know that they would shoot from above the wall?

**2 Samuel 11:21**

Who struck Abimelech son of Ierobaal? Did not a woman throw a piece of millstone upon him from above the wall, and he died at Themas? Why did you go near the wall? Then you will say, And also your servant Ourias the Hittite died.

**2 Samuel 11:22**

And the messenger of Iōab went to the king in Ierousalēm and came and reported to David all that Iōab reported to him, all the words of the war. And David became angry at Iōab and said to the messenger, Why did you go near the city to fight? Did you not know that you would be struck from the wall? Who struck Abimelech son of Ierobaal? Did not a woman throw a piece of millstone on him from the wall, and he died in Themas? Why did you go near the wall?

**2 Samuel 11:23**

And the messenger said to David, Because the men grew strong against us and came out against us into the field, and we came against them as far as the door of the gate,

**2 Samuel 11:24**

and the archers shot at your servants from above the wall, and some of the servants of the king died, and also your servant Ourias the Hittite died.

**2 Samuel 11:25**

And David said to the messenger, Thus you will say to Iōab: Let not this word be evil in your eyes, because once thus and once thus the sword will eat. Strengthen your battle against the city and tear it down, and strengthen him.

**2 Samuel 11:26**

And the wife of Ourias heard that Ourias her husband had died, and she mourned for her husband.

**2 Samuel 11:27**

And the mourning passed, and David sent and gathered her into his house, and she became his wife and bore him a son. But the word that David had done appeared evil in the eyes of the Lord.

### Chapter 12

**2 Samuel 12:1**

And the Lord sent Nathan the prophet to David, and he entered to him and said to him, There were two men in one city, one rich and one poor.

**2 Samuel 12:2**

And the rich man had very many flocks and herds.

**2 Samuel 12:3**

And to the poor man there was nothing except one little ewe lamb, which he acquired and kept alive and nourished, and it grew up with him and with his sons together. From his bread it would eat and from his cup it would drink and in his bosom it would sleep, and it was to him as a daughter.

**2 Samuel 12:4**

And a traveler came to the rich man, and he spared to take from his flocks and from his herds to prepare for the stranger traveler who came to him, and he took the ewe lamb of the poor man and prepared it for the man who came to him.

**2 Samuel 12:5**

And the anger of David burned greatly against the man, and David said to Nathan, As the Lord lives, the man who did this is a son of death.

**2 Samuel 12:6**

And he will repay the ewe lamb sevenfold, because he did this thing and because he did not spare.

**2 Samuel 12:7**

And Nathan said to David, You are the man who did this. Thus says the Lord God of Israel: I am the one who anointed you as king over Israel, and I am the one who delivered you from the hand of Saoul,

**2 Samuel 12:8**

and I gave you the house of your lord and the wives of your lord into your bosom, and I gave you the house of Israel and Iouda, and if this is little, I will add to you according to these things.

**2 Samuel 12:9**

Why did you count the word of the Lord as little, to do the evil in his eyes? Ourias the Hittite you struck with the sword, and his wife you took for yourself as wife, and him you killed with the sword of the sons of Ammon.

**2 Samuel 12:10**

And now the sword will not depart from your house forever, because you counted me as nothing and took the wife of Ourias the Hittite to be your wife.

**2 Samuel 12:11**

Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am raising evils against you out of your own house, and I will take your wives before your eyes and give them to your neighbor, and he will lie with your wives before this sun.

**2 Samuel 12:12**

Because you did it in secret, but I will do this word in front of all Israel and before this sun.

**2 Samuel 12:13**

And David said to Nathan, I have sinned against the Lord. And Nathan said to David, And the Lord has caused your sin to pass over; you certainly will not die.

**2 Samuel 12:14**

Only because in provoking you provoked the enemies of the Lord by this word, indeed the son born to you will surely die.

**2 Samuel 12:15**

And Nathan went to his house, and the Lord struck the child whom the wife of Ourias bore to David, and he became sick.

**2 Samuel 12:16**

And David sought God concerning the little boy, and David fasted a fast and entered and lodged in sackcloth on the ground.

**2 Samuel 12:17**

And the elders of his house stood over him to raise him up from the ground, and he was not willing, and he did not eat bread with them.

**2 Samuel 12:18**

And it came to be on the seventh day, the little boy died, and the servants of David feared to report to him that the little boy had died, because they said, Behold, while the little boy was still living we spoke to him, and he did not listen to our voice, and how shall we say to him that the little boy has died? He will do evil.

**2 Samuel 12:19**

And David understood that his servants were whispering, and David discerned that the little boy had died, and David said to his servants, Has the little boy died? And they said, He has died.

**2 Samuel 12:20**

And David rose from the ground and washed and anointed himself and changed his garments and entered into the house of God and bowed down to him. And he entered into his house and asked for bread to eat, and they set bread before him, and he ate.

**2 Samuel 12:21**

And his servants said to him, What is this word that you have done? For the little boy, while he was still alive, you were fasting and weeping and keeping watch, and when the little boy died, you rose and ate bread and have drunk.

**2 Samuel 12:22**

And David said, While the little boy was still living, I fasted and wept, because I said, Who knows whether the Lord will have mercy on me and the little boy will live?

**2 Samuel 12:23**

And now he has died. Why now am I fasting? Shall I be able to bring him back still more? I will go to him, but he will not return to me.

**2 Samuel 12:24**

**2 Samuel 12:25**

**2 Samuel 12:26**

**2 Samuel 12:27**

**2 Samuel 12:28**

**2 Samuel 12:29**

**2 Samuel 12:30**

**2 Samuel 12:31**

**2 Samuel 13:1**

**2 Samuel 13:32**

And now let not my lord the king set on his heart a word, saying, All the sons of the king have died, because only Amnōn has died.

**2 Samuel 13:38**

**2 Samuel 13:39**

### Chapter 14

**2 Samuel 14:1**

**2 Samuel 14:33**

### Chapter 15

**2 Samuel 15:1**

**2 Samuel 15:15**

And the king said to Eththi the Geththaite, Why are you also going with us? Return and dwell with the king, because you are a foreigner and because you have migrated from your place.

**2 Samuel 15:21**

And Eththi answered the king and said, As the Lord lives and as my lord the king lives, in the place where my lord is, whether for death or for life, there your servant will be.

**2 Samuel 15:23**

And the king said to Saddōk, Turn back the ark of God into the city. If I find favor in the eyes of the Lord, he will return me and show me it and its beauty.

**2 Samuel 15:26**

**2 Samuel 15:27**

**2 Samuel 15:29**

**2 Samuel 15:30**

**2 Samuel 15:31**

**2 Samuel 15:32**

**2 Samuel 15:33**

**2 Samuel 15:34**

But if you return to the city and say to Abessalōm, Your brothers have passed through, and the king behind me, your father, has passed through, and now I am your servant, king; then I was servant of your father and now again and now I am your servant, and you will scatter for me the counsel of Achitophel.

**2 Samuel 15:35**

And behold, with you there are Saddōk and Abiathar the priests, and every word whatever you hear from the house of the king, you will report to Saddōk and Abiathar the priests.

**2 Samuel 15:36**

Behold, there with them are their two sons, Achimaas to Saddōk and Iōnathan to Abiathar, and you will send by their hand to me every word whatever you hear.

**2 Samuel 15:37**

### Chapter 16

**2 Samuel 16:1**

**2 Samuel 16:2**

**2 Samuel 16:15**

**2 Samuel 16:21**

**2 Samuel 16:22**

And they pitched the tent for Abessalōm on the roof, and Abessalōm went in to the concubines of his father before the eyes of all Israel.

**2 Samuel 16:23**

And the counsel of Achitophel that he counseled in the former days was as if one inquired in the word of God. Thus was all the counsel of Achitophel, both to David and to Abessalōm.

### Chapter 17

**2 Samuel 17:1**

**2 Samuel 17:8**

**2 Samuel 17:9**

For behold, even now he is hidden in one of the hills or in one of the places, and it will happen, when some fall among them at the first attack, that whoever hears will say, A slaughter has happened among the people following Abessalom.

Then even a son of strength, whose heart is like the heart of a lion, will utterly melt, because all Israel knows that your father is mighty and the men with him are sons of strength.
