**2 Kings 5:8**

And it came to be, when Elisaie heard that the king of Israel tore his garments, he sent to the king of Israel, saying, Why have you torn your garments? Let Naiman now come to me, and let him know that there is a prophet in Israel.

**2 Kings 5:9**

And Naiman came with horse and chariot and stood at the door of the house of Elisaie.

**2 Kings 5:10**

And Elisaie sent a messenger to him, saying, Go, wash seven times in the Jordan, and your flesh will return to you, and you will be cleansed.

**2 Kings 5:11**

And Naiman grew angry and went away and said, Behold, I said to myself that he would surely come out to me and stand and call on the name of his God and put his hand on the place and remove the skin-diseased part.

**2 Kings 5:12**

Are not Abana and Pharphar, rivers of Damascus, better than the Jordan and all the waters of Israel? If I go and wash in them, will I not be cleansed? And he turned aside and went away in anger.

**2 Kings 5:13**

And his servants came near and spoke to him, saying, Father, if the prophet had spoken a great word to you, would you not do it? How much more when he said to you, Wash and be cleansed.

**2 Kings 5:14**

And Naiman went down and immersed himself in the Jordan seven times according to the word of Elisaie, and his flesh returned like the flesh of a small boy, and he was cleansed.

**2 Kings 5:15**

**2 Kings 5:16**

And Elisaie said, As the Lord lives, before whom I stand, I will not take it. And he pressed him to take it, but he refused.

**2 Kings 5:17**

In this matter may the Lord be merciful to your servant: when my lord enters the house of Remman to bow there, and he leans on my hand, and I bow in the house of Remman, when I bow in the house of Remman, may the Lord be merciful to your servant in this matter.

**2 Kings 5:19**

And Elisaie said to Naiman, Go in peace. And he went away from him a short stretch of land.

**2 Kings 5:20**

**2 Kings 5:21**

**2 Kings 5:22**

**2 Kings 5:23**

And Naiman said, Take two talents of silver. And he bound them in two bags, with two changes of garments, and gave them to two of his servant-boys, and they carried them before him.

**2 Kings 5:24**

**2 Kings 5:25**

**2 Kings 5:26**

**2 Kings 5:27**

### Chapter 6

**2 Kings 6:1**

**2 Kings 6:3**

**2 Kings 6:4**

**2 Kings 6:13**

**2 Kings 6:28**

**2 Kings 6:30**

Before the messenger came to him, Elisaie said to the elders, Do you see that this son of a murderer has sent to take away my head? See, when the messenger comes, shut the door and press him at the door. Is not the sound of the feet of his lord behind him?

**2 Kings 6:33**

### Chapter 7

**2 Kings 7:1**

And four men afflicted with skin-disease were beside the gate of the city. And one man said to his neighbor, Why do we sit here until we die?

If we say, Let us enter the city, the famine is in the city, and we will die there. And if we sit here, we will die. And now come, let us fall into the camp of Syria. If they keep us alive, we will live; and if they put us to death, we will die.

**2 Kings 7:5**

**2 Kings 7:7**

And they rose and fled in the dark and abandoned their tents and their horses and their donkeys, the camp just as it was, and fled for their own life.

**2 Kings 7:9**

And one man said to his neighbor, We are not doing right. This day is a day of good news, and we are keeping silent. If we wait until the morning light, lawlessness will find us. And now come, let us go in and report to the house of the king.

**2 Kings 7:10**

**2 Kings 7:12**

**2 Kings 7:13**

And one of his servants answered and said, Let them take now five of the horses left, which were left here. Behold, they are like all the multitude of Israel that has come to an end. Let us send and see.

**2 Kings 7:14**

**2 Kings 7:15**

**2 Kings 7:16**

**2 Kings 7:17**

**2 Kings 7:18**

**2 Kings 7:19**

And the officer answered Elisaie and said, Behold, if the Lord makes floodgates in heaven, can this thing be? And Elisaie said, Behold, you will see with your eyes, but from there you will not eat.

**2 Kings 7:20**

And so it happened to him, and the people trampled him in the gate, and he died.

**2 Kings 8:1**

**2 Kings 8:13**

**2 Kings 8:16**

In the fifth year of Joram son of Achaab, king of Israel, Jehoram son of Josaphat became king, king of Judah.

**2 Kings 8:17**

He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.

**2 Kings 8:18**

And he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as the house of Achaab had done, because the daughter of Achaab was his wife, and he did evil before the Lord.

**2 Kings 8:19**

**2 Kings 8:21**

**2 Kings 8:22**

And Edom rebelled from under the hand of Judah until this day. Then Lobena rebelled at that time.

**2 Kings 8:23**

**2 Kings 8:24**

And Joram slept with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of Dauid his father, and Ochozias his son reigned in his place.

**2 Kings 8:25**

In the twelfth year of Joram son of Achaab king of Israel, Ochozias son of Joram became king.

**2 Kings 8:26**

**2 Kings 8:27**

**2 Kings 8:28**

**2 Kings 8:29**

### Chapter 9

**2 Kings 9:1**

And Elisaie the prophet called one of the sons of the prophets and said to him, Gird your loins and take this flask of oil in your hand and go to Remmoth Galaad.

**2 Kings 9:2**

**2 Kings 9:3**

Then take the flask of oil and pour it on his head and say, Thus says the Lord, I have anointed you as king over Israel. And you will open the door and flee and not stay.

**2 Kings 9:4**

And the servant-boy, the prophet, went to Remmoth Galaad.

**2 Kings 9:5**

And he entered, and behold, the commanders of the force were sitting, and he said, I have a word for you, commander. And Iou said, For which one among all of us? And he said, For you, commander.

**2 Kings 9:6**

And he rose and entered the house, and he poured the oil on his head and said to him, Thus says the Lord God of Israel, I have anointed you as king over the people of the Lord, over Israel.

**2 Kings 9:10**

And Iou mounted and went to Jezrael, because Ioram was being healed there, and Ochozias king of Judah had gone down to see Ioram.

**2 Kings 9:18**

**2 Kings 9:19**

And he sent a second horseman, and he came to him and said, Thus says the king, Is it peace? And Iou said, What is peace to you? Turn behind me.

**2 Kings 9:20**

**2 Kings 9:21**

And Ioram said, Harness. And they harnessed his chariot, and Ioram king of Israel and Ochozias king of Judah went out, each in his chariot, to meet Iou, and they found him in the portion of Nabouthai the Jezraelite.

**2 Kings 9:22**

**2 Kings 9:24**

And Iou said to Badekar his officer, Lift him and throw him into the portion of the field of Nabouthai the Jezraelite, because I remember, I and you riding on pairs behind Achaab his father, and the Lord took up this burden against him, saying,

**2 Kings 9:36**

### Chapter 10

**2 Kings 10:1**

And Achaab had seventy sons in Samaria. And Iou wrote a letter and sent it into Samaria to the rulers of Samaria and to the elders and to the guardians of the sons of Achaab, saying,

**2 Kings 10:2**

And now when this letter comes to you, with you are the sons of your lord, and with you are the chariot and horses and fortified cities and weapons.

**2 Kings 10:3**

And you will look for the good and upright among the sons of your lord and set him on the throne of his father, and fight for the house of your lord.

**2 Kings 10:4**

And they feared greatly and said, Behold, the two kings did not stand before him, and how shall we stand?

**2 Kings 10:5**

And those over the house and those over the city and the elders and the guardians sent to Iou, saying, We are your servants, and whatever you say to us we will do. We will not make any man king. Do what is good in your eyes.

**2 Kings 10:6**

And he wrote to them a second letter, saying, If you are for me and obey my voice, take the heads of the men, the sons of your lord, and bring them to me at this time tomorrow in Jezrael. And the sons of the king, seventy men, were with the great men of the city, those rearing them.

**2 Kings 10:7**

And it came to be, when the letter came to them, they took the sons of the king and slaughtered them, seventy men, and put their heads in baskets and sent them to him in Jezrael.

**2 Kings 10:8**

And the messenger came and reported, saying, They brought the heads of the sons of the king. And he said, Put them in two heaps by the doorway of the gate until morning.

**2 Kings 10:9**

And it came to be in the morning, he went out and stood in the gate of the city and said to all the people, You are righteous. Behold, I conspired against my lord and killed him, but who struck all these?

**2 Kings 10:10**

Know now that not one thing from the word of the Lord will fall to the ground, which the Lord spoke against the house of Achaab. And the Lord has done what he spoke by the hand of his servant Elijah.

**2 Kings 10:11**

And Iou struck all those left of the house of Achaab in Jezrael and all his great men and his acquaintances and his priests until he left him no remnant.

**2 Kings 10:12**

And he rose and went to Samaria, he at Baithakad of the shepherds on the way.

**2 Kings 10:13**

And Iou found the brothers of Ochozias king of Judah and said, Who are you? And they said, We are brothers of Ochozias, and we came down to greet the sons of the king and the sons of the ruling lady.

**2 Kings 10:14**

And he said, Seize them alive. And they seized them alive and slaughtered them at Baithakad, forty-two men. He left not a man from among them.

**2 Kings 10:15**

And he went from there and found Ionadab son of Rechab on the way to meet him and blessed him and said to him, Is your heart straight with my heart, as my heart is with your heart? And Ionadab said, It is. And Iou said, If it is, give your hand. And he gave his hand, and he took him up to himself into the chariot.

**2 Kings 10:16**

And he said to him, Come with me and see in my zeal for the Lord Sabaoth. And he seated him in his chariot.

**2 Kings 10:17**

And he entered Samaria and struck all those left to Achaab in Samaria until destroying him, according to the word of the Lord which he spoke to Elijah.

**2 Kings 10:18**

And Iou gathered all the people and said to them, Achaab served Baal a little; Iou will serve him much.

**2 Kings 10:19**

And now call to me all the prophets of Baal, all his servants, and all his priests. Let not a man be overlooked, because I have a great sacrifice for Baal. Everyone who is overlooked will not live. And Iou did it in deception, in order to destroy the servants of Baal.

**2 Kings 10:20**

And Iou said, Sanctify a festival for Baal. And they proclaimed it.

**2 Kings 10:21**

And Iou sent through all Israel, and all the servants of Baal and all his priests and all his prophets came. No one was left out who did not come. And they entered the house of Baal, and the house of Baal was filled from mouth to mouth.

**2 Kings 10:22**

And Iou said to the one over the wardrobe, Bring out garments for all the servants of Baal. And the dresser brought out garments for them.

**2 Kings 10:23**

And Iou and Ionadab son of Rechab entered the house of Baal and said to the servants of Baal, Search and see whether there is with you any of the servants of the Lord, because only the servants of Baal are here.

**2 Kings 10:24**

And they went in to offer the sacrifices and whole-burnt-offerings. And Iou stationed for himself outside eighty men and said, The man who lets escape any from the men whom I bring into your hands, his life will be for that man's life.

**2 Kings 10:25**

And it came to be, when he finished offering the whole-burnt-offering, Iou said to the runners and to the officers, Go in and strike them down. Let not a man come out. And they struck them with the edge of the sword, and the runners and the officers cast them out and went into the inner city of the house of Baal.

**2 Kings 10:26**

And they brought out the pillar of Baal and burned it.

**2 Kings 10:27**

And they tore down the pillars of Baal and demolished the house of Baal and made it latrines to this day.

**2 Kings 10:28**

And Iou destroyed Baal from Israel.

**2 Kings 10:29**

Only, from the sins of Ieroboam son of Nabat, who made Israel sin, Iou did not turn away from after them, the golden calves in Baithēl and in Dan.

**2 Kings 10:30**

And the Lord said to Iou, Because you did well in doing what was right in my eyes and did to the house of Achaab all that was in my heart, fourth sons will sit for you on the throne of Israel.

**2 Kings 10:31**

And Iou was not careful to walk in the law of the Lord God of Israel with all his heart. He did not turn from the sins of Ieroboam son of Nabat, who made Israel sin.

**2 Kings 10:32**

In those days the Lord began to cut away in Israel, and Hazael struck them in every border of Israel,

**2 Kings 10:33**

from the Jordan toward sunrise, all the land of Galaad, of Gad and of Rouben and of Manasse, from Aroēr, which is on the lip of the wadi Arnon, even Galaad and Basan.

**2 Kings 10:34**

And the rest of the words of Iou and all that he did and all his might, are these not written in the book of the words of the days for the kings of Israel?

**2 Kings 10:35**

And Iou slept with his fathers, and they buried him in Samaria, and Ioachas his son reigned in his place.

**2 Kings 10:36**

And the days which Iou reigned over Israel were twenty-eight years in Samaria.

### Chapter 11

**2 Kings 11:1**

And Gotholia, the mother of Ochozias, saw that her sons were dead, and she destroyed all the royal seed.

**2 Kings 11:2**

And Iosabee daughter of king Ioram, sister of Ochozias, took Ioas son of her brother and stole him from the midst of the sons of the king being put to death, him and his nurse, into the bedchamber, and hid him from Gotholia, and he was not put to death.

**2 Kings 11:3**

And he was with her hidden in the house of the Lord six years, while Gotholia was reigning over the land.

**2 Kings 11:4**

And in the seventh year Iōdae the priest sent and took the centurions, the Chorrhi and the Rasim, and brought them to himself into the house of the Lord and made a covenant with them before the Lord and made them swear and showed them the king's son.

**2 Kings 11:5**

And he commanded them, saying, This is the word that you shall do: a third of you, those entering on the Sabbath, shall keep watch of the king's house at the gate.

**2 Kings 11:6**

And a third at the gate of the roads and a third at the gate behind the runners, and you shall keep the watch of the house.

**2 Kings 11:7**

And two divisions among you, all going out on the Sabbath, shall keep the watch of the house of the Lord for the king.

**2 Kings 11:8**

And surround the king all around, each man with his weapon in his hand, and the one entering within the ranks shall die. And be with the king in his going out and in his coming in.

**2 Kings 11:9**

And the centurions did all that Iōdae the priest commanded, and each man took his men, those entering on the Sabbath along with those going out on the Sabbath, and came to Iōdae the priest.

**2 Kings 11:10**

And the priest gave to the centurions the king Dauid's spears and shields, those in the house of the Lord.

**2 Kings 11:11**

And the runners stood, each man with his weapon in his hand, from the right side of the house to the left side of the house, by the altar and the house, around the king.

**2 Kings 11:12**

And he brought out the king's son and put on him the crown and the testimony and made him king and anointed him, and they clapped with the hand and said, Let the king live.

**2 Kings 11:13**

And Gotholia heard the sound of the runners of the people and entered to the people in the house of the Lord.

**2 Kings 11:14**

And she saw, and behold, the king was standing by the pillar according to the custom, and the singers and the trumpets were by the king, and all the people of the land were rejoicing and blowing with trumpets. And Gotholia tore her garments and cried, Conspiracy, conspiracy!

**2 Kings 11:15**

And Iōdae the priest commanded the centurions, the officers of the force, and said to them, Bring her out from within the ranks, and whoever enters after her shall certainly be put to death by the sword, because the priest said, Let her not die in the house of the Lord.

**2 Kings 11:16**

And they laid hands on her, and she went by way of the horse entrance of the king's house, and she died there.

**2 Kings 11:17**

And Iōdae made a covenant between the Lord and the king and the people, that they should be a people to the Lord, and between the king and the people.

**2 Kings 11:18**

And all the people of the land entered the house of Baal and tore it down, and his altars and his images they broke well, and Matthan priest of Baal they killed before the altars. And the priest set overseers over the house of the Lord.

**2 Kings 11:19**

And he took the centurions and the Chorrhi and the Rasim and all the people of the land and brought the king down from the house of the Lord and entered by way of the gate of the runners to the king's house, and they seated him on the throne of the kings.

**2 Kings 11:20**

And all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet, and they put Gotholia to death by the sword in the king's house.

### Chapter 12

**2 Kings 12:1**

Ioas was seven years old when he became king.

**2 Kings 12:2**

In the seventh year of Iou, Ioas became king, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother was Abia from Bērsabee.

**2 Kings 12:3**

And Ioas did what was right before the Lord all the days in which Iōdae the priest instructed him.

**2 Kings 12:4**

Only, the high places were not removed, and there the people still sacrificed and burned incense at the high places.

**2 Kings 12:5**

And Ioas said to the priests, All the silver of the holy things brought into the house of the Lord, silver of assessment, a man's silver from assessed value, every silver that comes up upon a man's heart to bring into the house of the Lord,

**2 Kings 12:6**

let the priests take it for themselves, each from his collection, and they themselves shall repair the breach of the house wherever any breach is found there.

**2 Kings 12:7**

And it came to be in the twenty-third year of king Ioas, the priests had not repaired the breach of the house.

**2 Kings 12:8**

And king Ioas called Iōdae the priest and the priests and said to them, Why is it that you do not repair the breach of the house? And now do not take silver from your collections, because you will give it for the breach of the house.

**2 Kings 12:9**

And the priests agreed not to take silver from the people and not to repair the breach of the house.

**2 Kings 12:10**

And Iōdae the priest took one chest and bored a hole in its lid and set it beside the altar, at the right side as a man enters the house of the Lord. And the priests keeping the threshold put there all the silver found in the house of the Lord.

**2 Kings 12:11**

And it came to be, when they saw that there was much silver in the chest, the king's scribe and the high priest went up and tied and counted the silver found in the house of the Lord.

**2 Kings 12:12**

And they gave the silver, weighed out, into the hands of those doing the works, the overseers of the house of the Lord, and they spent it on the carpenters of wood and on the builders doing work in the house of the Lord,

**2 Kings 12:13**

and on the masons and on the stonecutters to buy timber and quarried stones to hold together the breach of the house of the Lord, for everything laid out on the house to strengthen it.

**2 Kings 12:14**

Only, there were not made for the house of the Lord silver bowls, snuffers, basins, trumpets, any vessel of gold or vessel of silver, from the silver brought into the house of the Lord,

**2 Kings 12:15**

because they would give it to those doing the works, and they strengthened with it the house of the Lord.

**2 Kings 12:16**

And they did not reckon with the men into whose hands they gave the silver to give to those doing the works, because they acted in faithfulness.

**2 Kings 12:17**

Silver for sin and silver for trespass, whatever was brought into the house of the Lord, became the priests'.

**2 Kings 12:18**

Then Hazael king of Syria went up and fought against Geth and took it, and Hazael set his face to go up against Jerusalem.

**2 Kings 12:19**

And Ioas king of Judah took all the holy things that Iosaphat and Ioram and Ochozias his fathers, kings of Judah, had dedicated, and his own holy things and all the gold found in the treasuries of the house of the Lord and of the king's house, and sent them to Hazael king of Syria, and he went up away from Jerusalem.

**2 Kings 12:20**

And the rest of the words of Ioas and all that he did, are these not written in the book of the words of the days for the kings of Judah?

**2 Kings 12:21**

And his servants rose and bound a conspiracy and struck Ioas at the house Mallo in Gaalla.

**2 Kings 12:22**

And Iezichar son of Iemouath and Iezebouth his servant, son of Sōmēr, struck him, and he died. And they buried him with his fathers in the city of Dauid, and Amessias his son reigned in his place.

### Chapter 13

**2 Kings 13:1**

In the twenty-third year of Ioas son of Ochozias, king of Judah, Ioachas son of Iou reigned in Samaria seventeen years.

**2 Kings 13:2**

And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord and went after the sins of Ieroboam son of Nabat, who made Israel sin. He did not depart from them.

**2 Kings 13:3**

And the Lord grew angry in wrath against Israel and gave them into the hand of Hazael king of Syria and into the hand of son of Ader son of Hazael all the days.

**2 Kings 13:4**

And Ioachas entreated the face of the Lord, and the Lord listened to him, because he saw the oppression of Israel, that the king of Syria oppressed them.

**2 Kings 13:5**

And the Lord gave salvation to Israel, and he went out from under the hand of Syria, and the sons of Israel sat in their tents as formerly.

**2 Kings 13:6**

Only, they did not depart from the sins of the house of Ieroboam, who made Israel sin. In them they walked, and even the grove stood in Samaria.

**2 Kings 13:7**

Because there was not left to Ioachas a people except fifty horsemen and ten chariots and ten thousand footmen, because the king of Syria destroyed them and set them like dust for trampling.

**2 Kings 13:8**

And the rest of the words of Ioachas and all that he did and his acts of power, are these not written in the book of the words of the days for the kings of Israel?

**2 Kings 13:9**

And Ioachas slept with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in Samaria, and Ioas his son reigned in his place.

**2 Kings 13:10**

In the thirty-seventh year of Ioas king of Judah, Ioas son of Ioachas reigned over Israel in Samaria sixteen years.

**2 Kings 13:11**

And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord. He did not depart from all the sins of Ieroboam son of Nabat, who made Israel sin. In them he walked.

**2 Kings 13:12**

And the rest of the words of Ioas and all that he did and his acts of power with which he fought with Amessias king of Judah, are these not written in the book of the words of the days for the kings of Israel?

**2 Kings 13:13**

And Ioas slept with his fathers, and Ieroboam sat upon his throne in Samaria among the sons of Israel.

**2 Kings 13:14**

And Elisaie became sick with the sickness by which he died, and Ioas king of Israel came down to him and wept over his face and said, My father, my father, chariot of Israel and its horseman.

**2 Kings 13:15**

And Elisaie said to him, Take a bow and arrows. And he took for himself a bow and arrows.

**2 Kings 13:16**

And he said to the king, Lay your hand upon the bow. And Ioas laid his hand upon the bow, and Elisaie placed his hands upon the hands of the king.

**2 Kings 13:17**

And he said, Open the window toward the east. And he opened it. And Elisaie said, Shoot. And he shot. And he said, An arrow of salvation for the Lord and an arrow of salvation against Syria, and you will strike Syria at Aphek until completion.

**2 Kings 13:18**

And Elisaie said to him, Take the arrows. And he took them. And he said to the king of Israel, Strike into the ground. And the king struck three times and stopped.

**2 Kings 13:19**

And the man of God was grieved over him and said, If you had struck five or six times, then you would have struck Syria until completion. But now three times you will strike Syria.

**2 Kings 13:20**

And Elisaie died, and they buried him. And raiding bands of Moab came into the land at the coming of the year.

**2 Kings 13:21**

And it came to be, while they were burying a man, behold, they saw the raiding band, and they threw the man into the tomb of Elisaie. And he went and touched the bones of Elisaie and lived and stood on his feet.

**2 Kings 13:22**

And Hazael oppressed Israel all the days of Ioachas.

**2 Kings 13:23**

And the Lord had mercy on them and pitied them and looked toward them because of his covenant with Abraam and Isaak and Iakob, and the Lord did not wish to destroy them and did not cast them from before his face until now.

**2 Kings 13:24**

And Hazael king of Syria died, and son of Ader his son reigned in his place.

**2 Kings 13:25**

And Ioas son of Ioachas returned and took the cities from the hand of son of Ader son of Hazael, which he took from the hand of Ioachas his father in war. Three times Ioas struck him and recovered the cities of Israel.

### Chapter 14

**2 Kings 14:1**

In the second year of Ioas son of Ioachas, king of Israel, Amessias son of Ioas king of Judah reigned.

**2 Kings 14:2**

He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother was Ioadin from Jerusalem.

**2 Kings 14:3**

And he did what was right in the eyes of the Lord, but not like Dauid his father. According to all that Ioas his father did, he did.

**2 Kings 14:4**

Only, the high places he did not remove. The people still sacrificed and burned incense at the high places.

**2 Kings 14:5**

And it came to be, when the kingdom grew strong in his hand, he struck his servants who struck his father.

**2 Kings 14:6**

But the sons of those who struck him he did not put to death, just as it is written in the book of the laws of Moses, as the Lord commanded, saying, Fathers shall not die for sons, and sons shall not die for fathers, because each will die in his own sins.

**2 Kings 14:7**

He struck Edom in Gai-melē, ten thousand, and captured Petra in war and called its name Kathoēl to this day.

**2 Kings 14:8**

Then Amessias sent messengers to Ioas son of Ioachas son of Iou, king of Israel, saying, Come, let us look one another in the face.

**2 Kings 14:9**

And Ioas king of Israel sent to Amessias king of Judah, saying, The thornbush in Lebanon sent to the cedar in Lebanon, saying, Give your daughter to my son for a wife. And the beasts of the field passed by, those in Lebanon, and trampled the thornbush.

**2 Kings 14:10**

Striking, you struck Edom, and your heart lifted you up. Be glorified by sitting in your house. Why do you provoke evil against yourself, so that you fall, you and Judah with you?

**2 Kings 14:11**

And Amessias did not listen, and the king of Israel went up, and he and Amessias king of Judah looked one another in the face at Baithsamis of Judah.

**2 Kings 14:12**

And Judah stumbled before Israel, and each man fled to his tent.

**2 Kings 14:13**

And Ioas son of Ioachas king of Israel captured Amessias son of Ioas son of Ochozias, king of Judah, at Baithsamis, and he came to Jerusalem and tore down the wall of Jerusalem from the gate of Ephraim to the Corner Gate, four hundred cubits.

**2 Kings 14:14**

And he took the gold and the silver and all the vessels found in the house of the Lord and in the treasuries of the king's house and the hostages, and he returned to Samaria.

**2 Kings 14:15**

And the rest of the words of Ioas, what he did in his might, how he fought with Amessias king of Judah, are these not written in the book of the words of the days for the kings of Israel?

**2 Kings 14:16**

And Ioas slept with his fathers and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel, and Ieroboam his son reigned in his place.

**2 Kings 14:17**

And Amessias son of Ioas king of Judah lived fifteen years after the death of Ioas son of Ioachas king of Israel.

**2 Kings 14:18**

And the rest of the words of Amessias and all that he did, are these not written in the book of the words of the days for the kings of Judah?

**2 Kings 14:19**

And they conspired a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachis. And they sent after him to Lachis and killed him there.

**2 Kings 14:20**

And they carried him on horses, and he was buried in Jerusalem with his fathers in the city of Dauid.

**2 Kings 14:21**

And all the people of Judah took Azarias, and he was sixteen years old, and they made him king instead of his father Amessias.

**2 Kings 14:22**

He built Ailoth and restored it to Judah after the king slept with his fathers.

**2 Kings 14:23**

In the fifteenth year of Amessias son of Ioas king of Judah, Ieroboam son of Ioas reigned over Israel in Samaria forty-one years.

**2 Kings 14:24**

And he did evil before the Lord. He did not depart from all the sins of Ieroboam son of Nabat, who made Israel sin.

**2 Kings 14:25**

He restored the border of Israel from the entrance of Aimath to the sea of the Arabah, according to the word of the Lord God of Israel, which he spoke by the hand of his servant Iōnas son of Amathi, the prophet from Gethchober.

**2 Kings 14:26**

Because the Lord saw the affliction of Israel, that it was very bitter, and those held in and those diminished and those abandoned were few, and there was none helping Israel.

**2 Kings 14:27**

And the Lord did not speak to blot out the seed of Israel from under heaven, and he saved them by the hand of Ieroboam son of Ioas.

**2 Kings 14:28**

And the rest of the words of Ieroboam and all that he did and his acts of power, how he fought and how he restored Damascus and Aimath to Judah in Israel, are these not written in the book of the words of the days for the kings of Israel?

**2 Kings 14:29**

And Ieroboam slept with his fathers, with the kings of Israel, and Azarias son of Amessias reigned in place of his father.

### Chapter 15

**2 Kings 15:1**

In the twenty-seventh year of Ieroboam king of Israel, Azarias son of Amessias king of Judah reigned.

**2 Kings 15:2**

He was sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother was Chalia from Jerusalem.

**2 Kings 15:3**

And he did what was right in the eyes of the Lord, according to all that Amessias his father did.

**2 Kings 15:4**

Only, the high places he did not remove. The people still sacrificed and burned incense at the high places.

**2 Kings 15:5**

And the Lord touched the king, and he was afflicted with skin-disease until the day of his death, and he reigned in a separate house, and Iōatham son of the king was over the house, judging the people of the land.

**2 Kings 15:6**

And the rest of the words of Azarias and all that he did, are these not written in the book of the words of the days for the kings of Judah?

**2 Kings 15:7**

And Azarias slept with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in the city of Dauid, and Iōatham his son reigned in his place.

**2 Kings 15:8**

In the thirty-eighth year of Azarias king of Judah, Zacharias son of Ieroboam reigned over Israel in Samaria six months.

**2 Kings 15:9**

And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord, as his fathers did. He did not depart from the sins of Ieroboam son of Nabat, who made Israel sin.
