**Esther 5:3**

**Esther 5:6**

**Esther 5:7**

And she said, My petition and my request are this:

**Esther 5:8**

**Esther 5:9**

**Esther 5:10**

**Esther 5:11**

**Esther 5:12**

**Esther 5:13**

**Esther 5:14**

### Chapter 6

**Esther 6:1**

**Esther 6:8**

**Esther 6:13**

### Chapter 7

**Esther 7:1**

**Esther 7:6**

**Esther 7:7**

**Esther 7:8**

**Esther 7:9**

And Aman was hanged on the timber which he prepared for Mardochaios, and then the king ceased from wrath.

**Esther 8:1**

**Esther 8:3**

**Esther 8:10**

And it was written through the king and sealed with his ring, and they sent the letters through book-carriers,

**Esther 8:11**

**Esther 8:12**

**Esther 8:13**

**Esther 8:15**

**Esther 8:16**

**Esther 8:17**

### Chapter 9

**Esther 9:1**

**Esther 9:2**

**Esther 9:3**

**Esther 9:4**

**Esther 9:6**

**Esther 9:7**

**Esther 9:8**

**Esther 9:9**

and Marmasima and Arouphaios and Arsaios and Zabouthaithan,

**Esther 9:10**

**Esther 9:12**

**Esther 9:13**

**Esther 9:14**

**Esther 9:15**

**Esther 9:16**

**Esther 9:17**

And they rested on the fourteenth of the same month and kept it as day of rest with joy and gladness.

**Esther 9:18**

**Esther 9:19**

**Esther 9:20**

And Mardochaios wrote these words into a book and sent to the Ioudaioi, as many as were in kingdom of Artaxerxes, both near and far,

**Esther 9:21**

**Esther 9:22**

**Esther 9:23**

And the Ioudaioi accepted it, just as Mardochaios wrote to them,

**Esther 9:24**

**Esther 9:25**

**Esther 9:26**

**Esther 9:27**

And the Ioudaioi established and accepted it upon themselves and upon their seed and upon those added to them, and they will use no other way, but these days will be a memorial kept generation by generation and city and father-house and province.

**Esther 9:28**

And these days of Phrourai will be kept for all time, and their memorial shall never fail from the generations.

**Esther 9:29**

**Esther 9:31**

**Esther 9:32**

**Esther 10:1**

## Job

### Chapter 1

**Job 1:1**

There was a certain man in the land of Ausitis, whose name was Iōb, and that man was true, blameless, righteous, god-fearing, turning away from every evil thing.

**Job 1:2**

And there came to him seven sons and three daughters.

**Job 1:3**

And his livestock was seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen, five hundred grazing she-donkeys, and very much service, and great works were his upon the land. And that man was noblest of those from sunrise.

**Job 1:4**

And his sons, going to one another, were making a feast each day, bringing along also their three sisters to eat and drink with them.

**Job 1:5**

And when days of the feast were completed, Iōb sent and purified them. Rising early, he offered sacrifices for them according to their number, and one calf for sin concerning their souls. For Iōb said, Lest my sons thought evil things in their mind toward God. Thus Iōb was doing all the days.

**Job 1:6**

And when this day came, behold, angels of God came to stand before the Lord, and the slanderer came with them.

**Job 1:7**

And the Lord said to the slanderer, From where are you here? And answering, the slanderer said to the Lord, After going around the earth and walking about under heaven, I am here.

**Job 1:8**

And the Lord said to him, Did you set your mind against my servant Iōb, because there is no man like him on the earth, blameless, true, god-fearing, turning away from every evil thing?

**Job 1:9**

And the slanderer answered and said before the Lord, Does Iōb fear God for nothing?

**Job 1:10**

Did you not fence in things outside him and inside his house and outside all that belongs to him round about? Works of his hands you blessed, and his cattle you made many upon the earth.

**Job 1:11**

But stretch out your hand and touch all that he has, and surely he will bless you to your face.

**Job 1:12**

Then the Lord said to the slanderer, Behold, all things that are his I give into your hand, only do not touch him. And the slanderer went out from the Lord.

**Job 1:13**

And it happened on a day when Iōb's sons and daughters were drinking wine in house of their elder brother,

**Job 1:14**

and behold, a messenger came to Iōb and said to him, The yoke of oxen were plowing, and the she-donkeys were grazing beside them,

**Job 1:15**

and the raiders came and took them captive, and the servants they killed with swords. And I alone escaped and came to report to you.

**Job 1:16**

While this one was still speaking, another messenger came and said to Iōb, Fire fell from heaven and burned up the sheep and devoured the shepherds likewise. And I alone escaped and came to report to you.

**Job 1:17**

While this one was still speaking, another messenger came and said to Iōb, The horsemen made against us three heads, and they surrounded the camels and took them captive, and the servants they killed with swords. And I alone escaped and came to report to you.

**Job 1:18**

While this one was still speaking, another messenger came, saying to Iōb, Your sons and your daughters were eating and drinking at their elder brother's house,

**Job 1:19**

and suddenly a great wind came from the wilderness and touched the four corners of the house, and the house fell on your children, and they died. And I alone escaped and came to report to you.

**Job 1:20**

So Iōb rose, tore his garments, shaved hair of his head, and falling to the ground worshiped and said,

**Job 1:21**

Naked I came out from womb of my mother, naked also I will go away there. The Lord gave, the Lord took away. As it seemed good to the Lord, so also it came to pass. Let name of the Lord be blessed.

**Job 1:22**

In all these things that happened to him, Iōb sinned in nothing before the Lord and gave no folly to God.

### Chapter 2

**Job 2:1**

And it came to be on this day also that angels of God came to stand before the Lord, and the slanderer came among them to stand before the Lord.

**Job 2:2**

And the Lord said to the slanderer, From where do you come? Then the slanderer said before the Lord, After passing through what is under heaven and walking all around, I am here.

**Job 2:3**

And the Lord said to the slanderer, Did you then give attention to my servant Iōb, because there is no man like him on the earth, innocent, true, blameless, god-fearing, turning away from every evil, and he still holds fast his innocence? Yet you spoke against his possessions to destroy them for nothing.

**Job 2:4**

**Job 2:5**

**Job 2:6**

And the Lord said to the slanderer, Behold, I hand him over to you; only preserve his life.

**Job 2:7**

**Job 2:8**

**Job 2:9**

And when much time had passed, his wife said to him, How long will you endure, saying, Behold, I wait yet a little time, expecting hope of my deliverance? For behold, your memorial has vanished from the earth, sons and daughters of my womb, pangs and labors which I toiled for in vain with hardships. And you yourself sit in decay of worms, passing the night in the open air. And I am a wanderer and servant, going from place to place and house to house, waiting for sun to set so that I may rest from labors and pains that now hold me fast. But speak some word to the Lord and die.

**Job 2:10**

And looking at her, he said to her, You spoke like one of the foolish women. If we accepted good things from hand of the Lord, shall we not bear evil things? In all these things that happened to him, Iōb sinned in nothing with his lips before God.

**Job 2:11**

And hearing all the evils that came upon him, his three friends came, each from his own country, to him: Eliphas the Thaimanite king, Baldad the Sauchaian tyrant, and Sophar the Minaian king. And they came to him with one purpose, to encourage and visit him.

**Job 2:12**

And seeing him from far off, they did not recognize him, and crying with a loud voice they wept, each tearing his own robe and scattering dust.

**Job 2:13**

They sat with him seven days and seven nights, and none of them spoke, for they saw that the blow was dreadful and very great.

### Chapter 3

**Job 3:1**

After this Iōb opened his mouth

**Job 3:2**

and cursed his day, saying,

**Job 3:3**

Let the day perish in which I was born, and the night in which they said, Behold, a male.

**Job 3:4**

Let that day be darkness, and let not the Lord seek it from above, nor let light come upon it.

**Job 3:5**

Let darkness and shadow of death take it. Let gloom come upon it.

**Job 3:6**

Let the day and that night be cursed. Let darkness take it away. Let it not be among days of the year, nor counted among days of months.

**Job 3:7**

But let that night be pain, and let no gladness come upon it, nor joy.

**Job 3:8**

But let the one cursing that day curse it, the one preparing to master the great sea-beast.

**Job 3:9**

Let stars of that night be darkened. Let it wait and not come into light, nor see morning-star rising,

**Job 3:10**

**Job 3:11**

For why did I not die in the belly? And coming out from the womb, why did I not immediately perish?

**Job 3:12**

Why then did knees meet me? And why breasts, that I sucked?

**Job 3:13**

Now, having lain down, I would have been quiet. Having slept, I would have rested

**Job 3:14**

with kings, counselors of earth, who gloried themselves over swords,

**Job 3:15**

or with rulers whose gold was much, who filled their houses with silver,

**Job 3:16**

or like miscarriage coming out from womb of a mother, or like infants who never saw light.

**Job 3:17**

There the ungodly burned out rage of wrath. There the weary in body rested.

**Job 3:18**

And there the eternal ones together did not hear voice of tax-collector.

**Job 3:19**

**Job 3:20**

Why then is light given to those in bitterness, and life to souls in pains,

**Job 3:21**

**Job 3:22**

**Job 3:23**

Death is rest to a man, for God shut in against him.

**Job 3:24**

For before my food, groaning comes to me, and I weep, being held fast by fear.

**Job 3:25**

For fear which I pondered came upon me, and what I dreaded met me.

**Job 3:26**

I neither had peace nor was quiet nor rested, but wrath came to me.

### Chapter 4

**Job 4:1**

And taking up the matter, Eliphas the Thaimanite says,

**Job 4:2**

Were many times spoken to you in distress? But strength of your words, who will bear?

**Job 4:3**

For you instructed many and encouraged weak hands.

**Job 4:4**

And those failing you raised up by words, and upon knees without strength you put courage.

**Job 4:5**

But now pain comes upon you and touches you, and you were hasty.

**Job 4:6**

Is not your fear foolishness, and your hope, and innocence of your way?

**Job 4:7**

**Job 4:8**

**Job 4:9**

**Job 4:10**

Strength of lion, voice of lioness, and boast of dragons were quenched.

**Job 4:11**

**Job 4:12**

**Job 4:13**

**Job 4:14**

**Job 4:15**

And a spirit came upon my face, and my hairs and flesh shuddered.

**Job 4:16**

I stood up and did not recognize; I looked, and there was no form before my eyes, but only a breeze, and I was hearing a voice:

**Job 4:17**

What then? Shall mortal be pure before the Lord, or shall a man be blameless by his works?

**Job 4:18**

**Job 4:19**

**Job 4:20**

And from morning until evening they no longer exist, because they were not able to help themselves. They perished.

**Job 4:21**

For he breathed on them and they dried up. They perished for not having wisdom.

### Chapter 5

**Job 5:1**

But call, if anyone will hear you, or if you will see any of the holy angels.

**Job 5:2**

For anger kills the fool, and jealousy kills the wandering one.

**Job 5:3**

**Job 5:4**

**Job 5:5**

**Job 5:6**

**Job 5:7**

**Job 5:8**

**Job 5:9**

**Job 5:10**

**Job 5:11**

**Job 5:12**

**Job 5:13**

**Job 5:14**

**Job 5:15**

**Job 5:16**

**Job 5:17**

**Job 5:18**

**Job 5:19**

**Job 5:20**

**Job 5:21**

**Job 5:22**

**Job 5:23**

**Job 5:24**

**Job 5:25**

**Job 5:26**

**Job 5:27**

### Chapter 6

**Job 6:1**

And taking up the matter, Iōb says,

**Job 6:2**

**Job 6:3**

**Job 6:4**

**Job 6:5**

**Job 6:6**

**Job 6:7**

**Job 6:8**

**Job 6:9**

**Job 6:10**

**Job 6:11**

**Job 6:12**

**Job 6:13**

**Job 6:14**

**Job 6:15**

My near ones did not regard me; like failing torrents, or like wave they passed me by.

**Job 6:16**

**Job 6:17**

**Job 6:18**

**Job 6:19**

**Job 6:20**

**Job 6:21**

**Job 6:22**

**Job 6:23**

**Job 6:24**

**Job 6:25**

As it seems, words of truth are worthless, for I do not ask strength from you.

**Job 6:26**

**Job 6:27**

**Job 6:28**

**Job 6:29**

**Job 6:30**

### Chapter 7

**Job 7:1**

Is not life of man on earth a trial, and his life like that of day-laborer?

**Job 7:2**

**Job 7:3**

**Job 7:4**

**Job 7:5**

**Job 7:6**

My life is lighter than speech, and has perished in empty hope.

**Job 7:7**

**Job 7:8**

**Job 7:9**

**Job 7:10**

**Job 7:11**

**Job 7:12**

**Job 7:13**

**Job 7:14**

**Job 7:15**

**Job 7:16**

**Job 7:17**

**Job 7:18**

**Job 7:19**

**Job 7:20**

**Job 7:21**

### Chapter 8

**Job 8:1**

And taking up the matter, Baldad the Sauchite says,

**Job 8:2**

**Job 8:3**

**Job 8:4**

**Job 8:5**

**Job 8:6**

**Job 8:7**

**Job 8:8**

**Job 8:9**

**Job 8:10**

**Job 8:11**

**Job 8:13**

**Job 8:14**

**Job 8:15**

**Job 8:16**

**Job 8:17**

**Job 8:18**

**Job 8:19**

**Job 8:20**

**Job 8:21**

**Job 8:22**

### Chapter 9

**Job 9:1**

And taking up the matter, Iōb says,

**Job 9:2**

**Job 9:6**

**Job 9:7**

**Job 9:8**

**Job 9:10**

**Job 9:11**

**Job 9:14**

**Job 9:15**

**Job 9:16**

**Job 9:22**

**Job 9:23**

**Job 9:24**

**Job 9:25**

**Job 9:26**

**Job 9:27**

**Job 9:28**

**Job 9:30**

**Job 9:31**

**Job 9:32**

**Job 9:33**

**Job 9:34**

**Job 9:35**

### Chapter 10

**Job 10:1**

**Job 10:2**

**Job 10:4**

**Job 10:5**

**Job 10:7**

**Job 10:8**

**Job 10:10**

**Job 10:12**

**Job 10:13**

**Job 10:14**

**Job 10:15**

**Job 10:16**

**Job 10:17**

**Job 10:18**

**Job 10:19**

**Job 10:20**

**Job 10:22**

### Chapter 11

**Job 11:1**

**Job 11:10**

**Job 11:11**

**Job 11:12**

**Job 11:13**

**Job 11:15**

**Job 11:16**

**Job 11:17**

**Job 11:18**

**Job 11:19**

**Job 11:20**

### Chapter 12

**Job 12:1**

And taking up the matter, Iōb says,

**Job 12:2**

**Job 12:3**

**Job 12:4**

**Job 12:5**

**Job 12:6**

**Job 12:14**

**Job 12:16**

**Job 12:17**

**Job 12:18**

**Job 12:19**

**Job 12:20**

**Job 12:21**

**Job 12:23**

**Job 12:25**

### Chapter 13

**Job 13:1**

**Job 13:26**

### Chapter 14

**Job 14:1**

### Chapter 15

**Job 15:1**

And taking up the matter, Eliphas the Thaimanite says,

**Job 15:14**

**Job 15:15**

**Job 15:16**

**Job 15:17**

**Job 15:18**

**Job 15:19**

**Job 15:20**

**Job 15:21**

**Job 15:22**

**Job 15:23**

**Job 15:24**

**Job 15:25**

**Job 15:26**

**Job 15:27**

**Job 15:28**

**Job 15:29**

He will by no means grow rich, nor will his possessions remain; his shadow will not fall on earth.

**Job 15:30**

**Job 15:31**

Let him not believe he endures, for empty things will turn out for him.

**Job 15:32**

His cutting-down will be completed before its time, and his shoot will not flourish.

**Job 15:33**

Let him be harvested like unripe grape before its time, and fall off like flower of olive.

**Job 15:34**

For witness of ungodly is death, and fire will burn houses of gift-takers.

**Job 15:35**

In belly he will receive pains, and empty things will turn out for him, and his belly will bear deceit.

### Chapter 16

**Job 16:1**

And taking up the matter, Iōb says,

**Job 16:2**

I heard many such things, all of you comforters of evils.

**Job 16:3**

For is there not order to windy words? Or what troubles you that you answer?

**Job 16:4**

I too would speak like you, if only your soul lay in place of mine; then I would exult over you with words and shake head against you.

**Job 16:5**

But let there be strength in my mouth; I will not spare movement of my lips.

**Job 16:6**

**Job 16:7**

**Job 16:8**

**Job 16:9**

**Job 16:10**

**Job 16:11**

**Job 16:12**

**Job 16:13**

**Job 16:14**

**Job 16:15**

**Job 16:16**

**Job 16:17**

**Job 16:18**

**Job 16:19**

**Job 16:20**

**Job 16:21**

Let there be reproof for man before Lord, and son of man for his neighbor.

**Job 16:22**

### Chapter 17

**Job 17:1**

I am ruined, carried by breath; I beg for burial and do not obtain it.

**Job 17:2**

I am worn out in supplication. And what have I done?

**Job 17:3**

Strangers stole my goods. Who is this? Let him be bound with my hand.

**Job 17:4**

**Job 17:5**

He will declare evils for a share, and my eyes melted away over my sons.

**Job 17:6**

And you set me for byword among nations, and I became a laughingstock to them.

**Job 17:7**

**Job 17:8**

**Job 17:9**

**Job 17:10**

**Job 17:11**

**Job 17:12**

**Job 17:13**

For if I endure, Hades is my house; in gloom my bed is spread.

**Job 17:14**

**Job 17:15**

**Job 17:16**

### Chapter 18

**Job 18:1**

And taking up the matter, Baldad the Sauchite says,

**Job 18:2**

How long will you not stop? Hold back, so we also may speak.

**Job 18:3**

**Job 18:4**

**Job 18:5**

But light of ungodly will be quenched, and flame of theirs will not blaze forth.

**Job 18:6**

His light is darkness in his dwelling, and lamp over him will be extinguished.

**Job 18:7**

**Job 18:8**

His foot is cast into snare, and let him be twisted in net.

**Job 18:9**

Let traps come upon him, and let thirsty ones overpower him.

**Job 18:10**

**Job 18:11**

Let pains destroy him around, and let many come about his feet in hunger.

**Job 18:12**

**Job 18:13**

Let branches of his feet be eaten, and let death devour his beauties.

**Job 18:14**

Let healing be torn from his dwelling, and let royal necessity seize him.

**Job 18:15**

**Job 18:16**

His roots below will be dried up, and above his harvest will fall.

**Job 18:17**

His memorial perish from earth, and let there be no name of his on outside.

**Job 18:18**

Let him be driven from light into darkness.

**Job 18:19**

He will not be known among his people, nor saved under heaven his house; others will live in what is his.

**Job 18:20**

**Job 18:21**

### Chapter 19

**Job 19:1**

And taking up the matter, Iōb says,

**Job 19:2**

Until when will you trouble my soul and tear me down with words?

**Job 19:3**

Know only that Lord did this to me. Speaking against me, not ashamed, you press upon me.

**Job 19:4**

Yes then, if in truth I went astray, my wandering lodges with me. To speak word not needed, my words wander and not in season.

**Job 19:5**

If indeed you magnify yourselves against me and throw reproach at me,

**Job 19:6**

**Job 19:7**

**Job 19:8**

**Job 19:9**

He stripped glory from me and took crown from my head.

**Job 19:10**

**Job 19:11**

**Job 19:12**

**Job 19:13**

**Job 19:14**

**Job 19:15**

**Job 19:16**

**Job 19:17**

**Job 19:18**

**Job 19:19**

**Job 19:20**

**Job 19:21**

**Job 19:22**

**Job 19:23**

If only someone would grant my words be written, and set down in book forever,

**Job 19:24**

**Job 19:25**

For I know that one about to free me is eternal, and upon earth

**Job 19:26**

**Job 19:27**

**Job 19:28**

**Job 19:29**

### Chapter 20

**Job 20:1**

And taking up the matter, Sophar the Minaian says,

**Job 20:2**

**Job 20:4**

**Job 20:10**

**Job 20:11**

**Job 20:12**

**Job 20:13**

**Job 20:14**

**Job 20:15**

**Job 20:16**

**Job 20:17**

**Job 20:18**

**Job 20:19**

**Job 20:20**

**Job 20:21**

**Job 20:22**

**Job 20:23**

**Job 20:24**

**Job 20:25**

**Job 20:26**

**Job 20:27**

**Job 20:28**

### Chapter 21

**Job 21:1**

And taking up the matter, Iōb says,

**Job 21:2**

**Job 21:3**

**Job 21:4**

**Job 21:6**

**Job 21:7**

**Job 21:10**

**Job 21:11**

**Job 21:12**

**Job 21:13**

**Job 21:14**

**Job 21:18**

**Job 21:23**

**Job 21:24**

**Job 21:25**

**Job 21:26**

**Job 21:27**

**Job 21:28**

**Job 21:29**

**Job 21:30**

**Job 21:31**

**Job 21:32**

**Job 21:33**

**Job 21:34**

### Chapter 22

**Job 22:1**

And taking up the matter, Eliphas the Thaimanite says,

**Job 22:2**

**Job 22:3**

**Job 22:4**

**Job 22:5**

**Job 22:7**

**Job 22:8**

**Job 22:9**

**Job 22:10**

**Job 22:11**

**Job 22:12**

**Job 22:13**

**Job 22:15**

**Job 22:17**

**Job 22:18**

**Job 22:22**

**Job 22:23**

**Job 22:24**

**Job 22:25**

**Job 22:26**

**Job 22:27**

**Job 22:28**

**Job 22:29**

**Job 22:30**

### Chapter 23

**Job 23:1**

And taking up the matter, Iōb says,

**Job 23:3**

**Job 23:5**

**Job 23:7**

**Job 23:8**

**Job 23:10**

**Job 23:11**

**Job 23:12**

**Job 23:13**

**Job 23:15**

**Job 23:16**

**Job 23:17**

### Chapter 24

**Job 24:1**

**Job 24:2**

**Job 24:3**

**Job 24:4**

**Job 24:5**

**Job 24:7**

**Job 24:8**

**Job 24:9**

**Job 24:11**

**Job 24:12**

**Job 24:14**

**Job 24:16**

**Job 24:17**

**Job 24:18**

**Job 24:19**

**Job 24:20**

**Job 24:21**

**Job 24:22**

**Job 24:23**

**Job 24:24**

**Job 24:25**

### Chapter 25

**Job 25:1**

And taking up the matter, Baldad the Sauchite says,

**Job 25:2**

**Job 25:3**

**Job 25:4**

**Job 25:5**

**Job 25:6**

### Chapter 26

**Job 26:1**

And taking up the matter, Iōb says,

**Job 26:2**

**Job 26:3**

**Job 26:4**

**Job 26:5**

**Job 26:6**

**Job 26:7**

**Job 26:8**

**Job 26:9**

**Job 26:10**

**Job 26:11**

**Job 26:12**

**Job 26:13**

### Chapter 27

**Job 27:1**

**Job 27:14**

**Job 27:18**

**Job 27:19**

**Job 27:20**

**Job 27:21**

And your garment is warm; yet earth rests quietly.

**Job 37:18**

Will you make firm with him ancient things, strong as vision of molten metal?

**Job 37:19**

Why? Teach me what we shall say to him, and let us stop saying many things.

**Job 37:20**

Did book or scribe stand by me, that standing I should make man silent?

**Job 37:21**

But light is not visible to all; it shines afar in ancient things, like what is with him upon clouds.

**Job 37:22**

From north clouds shine with gold; over these things is great glory and honor of Almighty.

**Job 37:23**

And we do not find another like his strength; judging righteous things, he does not think to hear.

**Job 37:24**

Therefore men will fear him, and wise of heart will fear him.

### Chapter 38

**Job 38:1**

And after Elioun ceased from speech, Lord said to Iōb through whirlwind and clouds,

**Job 38:2**

Who is this hiding counsel, and holding words in heart, but thinking to hide them from me?

**Job 38:3**

Gird your loins like man; I will ask you, and you answer me.

**Job 38:4**

Where were you when I founded earth? Declare to me, if you know understanding.

**Job 38:5**

Who set its measures, if you know, or who stretched line upon it?

**Job 38:6**

Upon what have its rings been fastened? And who is one laying cornerstone upon it,

**Job 38:7**

when stars were born and all my angels praised me with loud voice?

**Job 38:8**

And I fenced in sea with gates when it rushed out, coming forth from womb of its mother,

**Job 38:9**

and I put cloud as its clothing and wrapped it in mist,

**Job 38:10**

and I put boundaries to it, setting bars and gates around,

**Job 38:11**

and I said to it, Up to this you will come and not pass beyond, but in yourself your waves will be broken.

**Job 38:12**

Or did I arrange morning light for you, and morning-star see its own order,

**Job 38:13**

to seize wings of earth and shake ungodly men out of it?

**Job 38:14**

Or did you take earth, clay, and shape living thing, and set speaking one upon earth?

**Job 38:15**

And you took light from ungodly men, and shattered arm of proud men.

**Job 38:16**

And did you come upon spring of sea, and walk in tracks of deep?

**Job 38:17**

And are gates of death opened to you in fear, and gatekeepers of Hades, seeing you, were terrified?

**Job 38:18**

And did you perceive breadth of what is under heaven? Declare then to me how great it is.

**Job 38:19**

And what land does light lodge in, and what is place of darkness,

**Job 38:20**

if you would bring me to their boundaries and know their paths?

**Job 38:21**

I know then that you were born at that time, and number of your years is great.

**Job 38:22**

And did you come upon treasuries of snow, and see treasuries of hail,

**Job 38:23**

kept aside for you for hour of enemies, for day of war and battle?

**Job 38:24**

And from where does frost come out, or south wind scatter into what is under heaven?

**Job 38:25**

And who prepared channel for violent rain, and way for thunderings,

**Job 38:26**

to rain upon land where there is no man, wilderness where no man exists in it,

**Job 38:27**

to satisfy pathless and uninhabited land and make growth of grass spring out?

**Job 38:28**

Who is father of rain, and who begot clods of dew?

**Job 38:29**

And from whose womb does ice come out, and who begot frost in heaven?

**Job 38:30**

Or does it descend like flowing water, and who froze face of deep?

**Job 38:31**

And did you understand bond of Pleiad, and open barrier of Orion?

**Job 38:32**

Or will you open Mazzaroth in its season, and bring Evening Star with its tail?

**Job 38:33**

And do you know turnings of heaven, or things happening together under heaven?

**Job 38:34**

And will you call cloud with voice, and will trembling of abundant water obey you?

**Job 38:35**

And will you send out lightnings, and they will go and say to you, What is it?

**Job 38:36**

And who gave women skill in weaving, or embroidered knowledge?

**Job 38:37**

And who counts clouds in wisdom, and bent heaven down to earth,

**Job 38:38**

and it was poured out like dusty earth, and I glued it together like stone cube?

**Job 38:39**

And will you hunt food for lions, and fill souls of dragons,

**Job 38:40**

for they fear in their lairs and sit in woods lying in wait?

**Job 38:41**

And who prepared food for raven? For its young cry to Lord, wandering and seeking food.

### Chapter 39

**Job 39:1**

Do you know time of giving birth of rock-goats, and did you watch birth-pangs of hinds?

**Job 39:2**

And did you count full months of their bearing, and loosen their pangs?

**Job 39:3**

And did you rear their young without fear, and send out their birth-pangs?

**Job 39:4**

Their young will burst forth, increase with produce, go out and by no means return to them.

**Job 39:5**

And who let wild donkey go free, and who loosed its bonds?

**Job 39:6**

And I set its dwelling in wilderness, and its tents in salt land.

**Job 39:7**

Laughing at tumult of city, and not hearing rebuke of tax-collector,

**Job 39:8**

it will inspect mountains for its pasture and seek after every green thing.

**Job 39:9**

Will unicorn be willing to serve you, or sleep at your manger?

**Job 39:10**

And will you bind its yoke with straps, or will it drag your furrows in plain?

**Job 39:11**

And do you trust in it because its strength is great? And will you leave your works to it?

**Job 39:12**

And will you trust that it will return your seed and bring it into your threshing floor?

**Job 39:13**

Wing of rejoicing ostriches, if it should conceive stork and hawk,

**Job 39:14**

because it will leave its eggs in earth and brood them upon dust,

**Job 39:15**

and forgot that foot will scatter them and beasts of field trample them.

**Job 39:16**

It hardened its young so as not to be its own; for nothing it labored without fear,

**Job 39:17**

because God made wisdom silent to it and did not divide understanding to it.

**Job 39:18**

At time on high it will raise itself up; it will laugh at horse and its rider.

**Job 39:19**

And did you clothe horse with strength, and put fear on its neck?

**Job 39:20**

And did you put armor on it, and boldness on its chest?

**Job 39:21**

Pawing in plain in pride, it goes out to field in strength.

**Job 39:22**

Meeting arrow, it laughs and will by no means turn back from iron.

**Job 39:23**

Over it boast bow and sword.

**Job 39:24**

And anger will destroy earth, and it will by no means believe until trumpet sounds.

**Job 39:25**

And when trumpet sounds it says, Good! And from far off it smells war with leap and cry.

**Job 39:26**

And by your knowledge has hawk stood still, spreading out wings motionless and looking southward?

**Job 39:27**

And by your command does eagle rise up, and vulture, sitting, lodge at its nest?

**Job 39:28**

Upon projection of rock and hidden place.

**Job 39:29**

From there, being there, it seeks foods; its eyes watch from far away.

**Job 39:30**

And its young wallow in blood, and wherever corpses are, they are immediately found.

### Chapter 40

**Job 40:1**

And Lord God answered Iōb and said,

**Job 40:2**

Will one turning aside judgment with Sufficient One, reproving God, answer this?

**Job 40:3**

And taking up the matter, Iōb says to Lord,

**Job 40:4**

Why am I still judged, being admonished and reproving Lord, hearing such things while I am nothing? What answer shall I give to these things? I will put hand on my mouth.

**Job 40:5**

Once I spoke, but on second time I will not add.

**Job 40:6**

And again taking up the matter, Lord said to Iōb out of cloud,

**Job 40:7**

But gird your loins like man; I will ask you, and you answer me.

**Job 40:8**

Do not reject my judgment; do you think I have dealt with you otherwise than that you might appear righteous?

**Job 40:9**

Or is arm of yours against Lord, or your voice thundering against him?

**Job 40:10**

Take up then height and power, and clothe yourself with glory and honor.

**Job 40:11**

And send out angels in wrath, and humble every arrogant man.

**Job 40:12**

And quench proud man, and rot ungodly men at once.

**Job 40:13**

Hide them together outside in earth, and fill their faces with dishonor.

**Job 40:14**

Then I too will confess that your right hand can save.

**Job 40:15**

But now behold beasts beside you; it eats grass like oxen.

**Job 40:16**

Behold then its strength upon loins, and its power upon navel of belly.

**Job 40:17**

It set tail like cypress, and its sinews are interwoven.

**Job 40:18**

Its ribs are bronze ribs, and its backbone cast iron.

**Job 40:19**

This is beginning of Lord's creation, made to be mocked by his angels.

**Job 40:20**

And going upon steep mountain, it made joy for quadrupeds in Tartarus.

**Job 40:21**

It sleeps under every kind of tree, beside papyrus and reed and rush.

**Job 40:22**

And great trees shade it, with branches and shoots of agnus-tree.

**Job 40:23**

If flood happens, it will not notice; it trusts that Jordan will dash into its mouth.

**Job 40:24**

Will one take it in its eye? With snare one will pierce its nose.

**Job 40:25**

And will you lead dragon with hook, and put halter around its nose?

**Job 40:26**

Or will you bind ring in its nostril and pierce its lip with bracelet?

**Job 40:27**

And will it speak to you with petition, making supplications softly?

**Job 40:28**

And will it make covenant with you, and you will take it for eternal slave?

**Job 40:29**

And will you play with it like bird, or bind it like sparrow for child?

**Job 40:30**

And nations feed upon it, and races of Phoenicians divide it up.

**Job 40:31**

And all ships gathered together will by no means carry one skin of its tail, nor in fishing boats its head.

**Job 40:32**

And will you lay hand upon it, remembering war happening in its body, and let it happen no more?

### Chapter 41

**Job 41:1**

Have you not seen it, nor marveled at things spoken of it?

**Job 41:2**

Have you not feared because it has been prepared for me? For who is one standing against me?

**Job 41:3**

Or who will withstand me and endure, if all that is under heaven is mine?

**Job 41:4**

I will not be silent because of it, and word of power will have mercy on its equal.

**Job 41:5**

Who will uncover face of its clothing? And who would enter fold of its breastplate?

**Job 41:6**

Who will open gates of its face? Around its teeth is fear.

**Job 41:7**

Its inward parts are bronze shields, and its binding like emery stone.

**Job 41:8**

One cleaving to another, and breath will by no means pass through it.

**Job 41:9**

A man to his brother will be glued; they hold together and will by no means be torn apart.

**Job 41:10**

At its sneezing light shines, and its eyes like form of morning star.

**Job 41:11**

From its mouth go out burning lamps, and hearths of fire are scattered abroad.

**Job 41:12**

From its nostrils comes out smoke of furnace burning with coals of fire.

**Job 41:13**

Its soul is coals, and flame goes out from its mouth.

**Job 41:14**

And in its neck strength lodges; destruction runs before it.

**Job 41:15**

Fleshes of its body are joined together; he will pour upon it, and it will not be shaken.

**Job 41:16**

Its heart is fixed like stone, standing like unhammersmitten anvil.

**Job 41:17**

When it turns, there is fear to beasts, to quadrupeds on earth leaping.

**Job 41:18**

If spears meet it, they will do nothing, nor raised spear and breastplate.

**Job 41:19**

For it counts iron as straw, and bronze as rotten wood.

**Job 41:20**

Bronze bow will by no means wound it; it counts stone-slinger as grass.

**Job 41:21**

Hammers were counted as reed, and it laughs at shaking of fire-bearer.

**Job 41:22**

Its bed is sharp spits, and all gold of sea under it like immeasurable clay.

**Job 41:23**

It makes deep boil like bronze pot, and counts sea like perfume-vessel.

**Job 41:24**

And Tartarus of deep it counted like captive, and deep for its walking.

**Job 41:25**

There is nothing upon earth like it, made to be mocked by my angels.

**Job 41:26**

It sees every high thing; and it is king of all things in waters.

### Chapter 42

**Job 42:1**

And taking up the matter, Iōb says to Lord,

**Job 42:2**

I know that you can do all things, and nothing is impossible for you.

**Job 42:3**

For who is one hiding counsel from you, sparing words, and thinking to hide you? And who will tell me things I did not know, great and wonderful things which I did not understand?

**Job 42:4**

Hear me, Lord, that I too may speak; I will ask you, and you teach me.

**Job 42:5**

By hearing of ear I formerly heard you, but now my eye has seen you.

**Job 42:6**

Therefore I despised myself and melted away, and I count myself earth and ashes.

**Job 42:7**

And it happened after Lord spoke all these words to Iōb, Lord said to Eliphas the Thaimanite, You and your two friends sinned, for you spoke nothing true before me, as my servant Iōb did.

**Job 42:8**

Now then take seven calves and seven rams and go to my servant Iōb, and he will make fruit-offering concerning you. And my servant Iōb will pray concerning you, because unless I receive his face, for his sake I would have destroyed you, for you did not speak truth concerning my servant Iōb.

**Job 42:9**

And Eliphas the Thaimanite and Baldad the Sauchite and Sophar the Minaian went and did as Lord instructed them, and through Iōb he loosed their sin.

**Job 42:10**

And Lord increased Iōb. And when he prayed also concerning his friends, he forgave them their sin. And Lord gave double whatever had been before Iōb, for doubling.

**Job 42:11**

And all his brothers and sisters heard all things that happened to him, and they came to him, and all who had known him from first. And eating and drinking with him, they comforted him and marveled over all that Lord brought upon him. And each gave him one lamb and a gold four-drachma piece unstamped.

**Job 42:12**

And Lord blessed last things of Iōb more than former things. And his livestock was fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, one thousand yoke of oxen, and one thousand female grazing donkeys.

**Job 42:13**

And seven sons and three daughters were born to him.

**Job 42:14**

And he called first Day, second Cassia, and third Horn of Amaltheia.

**Job 42:15**

And no women under heaven were found better than daughters of Iōb, and father gave them inheritance among their brothers.

**Job 42:16**

And Iōb lived after the blow one hundred seventy years; altogether he lived two hundred forty-eight years, and Iōb saw his sons and sons of his sons, fourth generation.

**Job 42:17**

And Iōb died old and full of days. And it is written that he will rise again with those whom Lord raises up. This man, interpreted from Syriac book, dwelt in land Ausitis on borders of Idumaia and Arabia, and his former name was Iōbab. Taking Arabian wife, he fathered son whose name was Ennon. And he himself was son of Zare, one of sons of Esau, from mother Bosorra, so as to be fifth from Abraham. And these were kings who reigned in Edom, over which he also first ruled: Balak son of Beōr, and name of his city was Dennaba; after Balak, Iōbab called Iōb; after him Asom, ruler from country of Thaimanitis; after him Adad son of Barad, who cut down Madiam in plain of Mōab, and name of his city was Geththaim. And friends coming to him were Eliphas king of sons of Esau from Thaimanites, Baldad tyrant of Sauchites, and Sophar king of Minaians.

## Psalms

### Chapter 1

**Psalms 1:1**

Blessed man who did not walk in counsel of ungodly men, and did not stand in way of sinners, and did not sit upon seat of pestilent men,

**Psalms 1:2**

but his delight is in law of Lord, and in his law he will meditate day and night.

**Psalms 1:3**

And he will be like tree planted by outlets of waters, which will give its fruit in its season, and its leaf will not wither, and all things whatever he does will prosper.

**Psalms 1:4**

Not so ungodly men, not so, but like chaff which wind throws from face of earth.

**Psalms 1:5**

Because of this ungodly men will not stand in judgment, nor sinners in counsel of righteous men.

**Psalms 1:6**

For Lord knows way of righteous men, but way of ungodly men will perish.

### Chapter 2

**Psalms 2:1**

Why did nations rage, and peoples meditate empty things?

**Psalms 2:2**

Kings of earth stood by, and rulers were gathered together against Lord and against his Anointed. Interlude.

**Psalms 2:3**

Let us tear their bonds apart and cast their yoke from us.

**Psalms 2:4**

One dwelling in heavens will laugh at them, and Lord will mock them.

**Psalms 2:5**

Then he will speak to them in his wrath and trouble them in his anger.

**Psalms 2:6**

But I was set as king by him upon Sion, his holy mountain,

**Psalms 2:7**

declaring decree of Lord. Lord said to me, You are my son; today I have begotten you.

**Psalms 2:8**

Ask from me, and I will give nations as your inheritance and ends of earth as your possession.

**Psalms 2:9**

You will shepherd them with iron rod; like potter's vessel you will shatter them.

**Psalms 2:10**

And now, kings, understand; be instructed, all judging earth.

**Psalms 2:11**

Serve Lord in fear and rejoice in him with trembling.

**Psalms 2:12**

Take hold of instruction lest Lord be angered and you perish from righteous way when his wrath is quickly kindled. Blessed all who trust in him.

### Chapter 3

**Psalms 3:1**

Psalm of David, when he fled from face of Abessalōm his son.

**Psalms 3:2**

Lord, why were those afflicting me multiplied? Many rise up against me.

**Psalms 3:3**

Many say to my soul, There is no salvation for him in his God. Interlude.

**Psalms 3:4**

But you, Lord, are my defender, my glory, and one lifting my head.

**Psalms 3:5**

With my voice I cried to Lord, and he heard me from his holy mountain. Interlude.

**Psalms 3:6**

I lay down and slept; I awoke, because Lord will help me.

**Psalms 3:7**

I will not fear from myriads of people those surrounding and attacking me.

**Psalms 3:8**

Rise up, Lord; save me, my God, because you struck all who hate me for nothing; teeth of sinners you shattered.

**Psalms 3:9**

Salvation belongs to Lord, and your blessing upon your people.

### Chapter 4

**Psalms 4:1**

For end. In psalms. Song of David.

**Psalms 4:2**

When I call, God of my righteousness heard me; in affliction you widened space for me. Have pity on me and hear my prayer.

**Psalms 4:3**

Sons of men, until when heavy-hearted? Why do you love vanity and seek lie? Interlude.

**Psalms 4:4**

And know that Lord made his holy one wondrous; Lord will hear me when I cry to him.

**Psalms 4:5**

Be angry and do not sin; say within your hearts, and upon your beds be pierced through. Interlude.

**Psalms 4:6**

Sacrifice sacrifice of righteousness and hope upon Lord.

**Psalms 4:7**

Many say, Who will show us good things? Light of your face, Lord, was marked upon us.

**Psalms 4:8**

You gave gladness into my heart, from season when their grain and wine and oil were multiplied.

**Psalms 4:9**

In peace, at same time, I will lie down and sleep, because you, Lord, alone settled me in hope.

### Chapter 5

**Psalms 5:1**

For end. Concerning her who inherits. Psalm of David.

**Psalms 5:2**

Give ear to my words, Lord; understand my cry.

**Psalms 5:3**

Attend to voice of my petition, my King and my God, because to you I will pray, Lord.

**Psalms 5:4**

In morning you will hear my voice; in morning I will stand before you and keep watch.

**Psalms 5:5**

For you are not God willing lawlessness, nor will one doing evil dwell with you.

**Psalms 5:6**

Lawless men will not remain before your eyes; you hated all working lawlessness.

**Psalms 5:7**

You will destroy all speaking lie; man of bloods and deceit Lord abhors.

**Psalms 5:8**

But I, in multitude of your mercy, will enter into your house; I will worship toward your holy temple in your fear.

**Psalms 5:9**

Lord, lead me in your righteousness because of my enemies; make your way straight before me.

**Psalms 5:10**

Because there is no truth in their mouth; their heart is vain; their throat open grave; with their tongues they dealt deceitfully.

**Psalms 5:11**

Judge them, God; let them fall from their counsels. According to multitude of their ungodliness cast them out, because they embittered you, Lord.

**Psalms 5:12**

And let all hoping in you be glad; into age they will rejoice, and you will dwell among them; and all loving your name will boast in you.

**Psalms 5:13**

Because you will bless righteous man, Lord; as with weapon of favor you crowned us.

### Chapter 6

**Psalms 6:1**

For end. In hymns. Concerning eighth. Psalm of David.

**Psalms 6:2**

Lord, do not reprove me in your fury, nor discipline me in your anger.

**Psalms 6:3**

Have mercy on me, Lord, because I am weak. Heal me, Lord, because my bones were troubled.

**Psalms 6:4**

And my soul was greatly troubled. And you, Lord, until when?

**Psalms 6:5**

Turn back, Lord; rescue my soul. Save me because of your mercy.

**Psalms 6:6**

Because in death there is none remembering you; and in Hades who will confess to you?

**Psalms 6:7**

I toiled in my groaning; every night I will wash my bed, with my tears I will soak my couch.

**Psalms 6:8**

My eye was troubled from anger; I grew old among all my enemies.

**Psalms 6:9**

Depart from me, all working lawlessness, because Lord heard voice of my weeping.

**Psalms 6:10**

Lord heard my petition; Lord received my prayer.

**Psalms 6:11**

Let all my enemies be ashamed and greatly troubled; let them turn back and be greatly ashamed very quickly.

### Chapter 7

**Psalms 7:1**

Psalm of David, which he sang to Lord concerning words of Chousi son of Iemeni.

**Psalms 7:2**

Lord my God, upon you I hoped; save me from all pursuing me and rescue me,

**Psalms 7:3**

lest he seize my soul like lion, while there is none redeeming and none saving.

**Psalms 7:4**

Lord my God, if I did this, if there is injustice in my hands,

**Psalms 7:5**

if I repaid evil to those repaying me, then let me fall away from my enemies empty.

**Psalms 7:6**

Then let enemy pursue my soul and seize it, and trample my life into earth, and settle my glory in dust. Interlude.

**Psalms 7:7**

Rise up, Lord, in your anger; be lifted up at ends of my enemies. Wake up, Lord my God, in command which you enjoined.

**Psalms 7:8**

And gathering of peoples will encircle you, and over this return on high.

**Psalms 7:9**

Lord judges peoples. Judge me, Lord, according to my righteousness and according to my innocence upon me.

**Psalms 7:10**

Let evil of sinners come to end, and you will set righteous man straight, examining hearts and kidneys, O God.

**Psalms 7:11**

My help is righteous from God, the one saving upright ones in heart.

**Psalms 7:12**

God is righteous judge, strong and patient, not bringing on anger each day.

**Psalms 7:13**

If you do not turn back, he will polish his sword, stretch his bow, and prepare it.

**Psalms 7:14**

And in it he prepared instruments of death; his arrows he worked out for burning ones.

**Psalms 7:15**

Behold, he travailed with injustice, conceived toil, and gave birth to lawlessness.

**Psalms 7:16**

He dug pit and scooped it out, and he will fall into hole which he made.

**Psalms 7:17**

His toil will return upon his head, and his injustice will come down upon his crown.

**Psalms 7:18**

I will confess to Lord according to his righteousness, and I will sing praise to name of Lord Most High.

### Chapter 8

**Psalms 8:1**

For end. Concerning winepresses. Psalm of David.

**Psalms 8:2**

Lord, our Lord, how wondrous your name in all earth, because your magnificence was lifted above heavens.

**Psalms 8:3**

Out of mouth of infants and nursing ones you prepared praise, because of your enemies, to tear down enemy and avenger.

**Psalms 8:4**

Because I will see heavens, works of your fingers, moon and stars which you founded.

**Psalms 8:5**

What is man, that you remember him, or son of man, that you visit him?

**Psalms 8:6**

You lessened him a little from angels; with glory and honor you crowned him.

**Psalms 8:7**

And you set him over works of your hands; all things you subjected under his feet:

**Psalms 8:8**

sheep and oxen, all of them, and also beasts of field,

**Psalms 8:9**

birds of heaven and fish of sea, things passing through paths of seas.

**Psalms 8:10**

Lord, our Lord, how wondrous your name in all earth.

### Chapter 9

**Psalms 9:1**

For end. Concerning hidden things of son. Psalm of David.

**Psalms 9:2**

I will confess to you, Lord, with whole heart; I will recount all your wondrous deeds.

**Psalms 9:3**

I will be glad and rejoice in you; I will sing praise to your name, Most High,

**Psalms 9:4**

when my enemy turns back. They will grow weak and perish from your face,

**Psalms 9:5**

because you made my judgment and my case. You sat upon throne, one judging righteousness.

**Psalms 9:6**

You rebuked nations, and ungodly man perished. Their name you wiped out into age and into age of age.

**Psalms 9:7**

Swords of enemy failed to end, and you pulled down cities. Their memorial perished with noise.

**Psalms 9:8**

But Lord remains into age; he prepared his throne in judgment.

**Psalms 9:9**

And he himself will judge inhabited world in righteousness; he will judge peoples in uprightness.

**Psalms 9:10**

And Lord became refuge for poor man, helper in opportunities, in affliction.

**Psalms 9:11**

And let those knowing your name hope upon you, because you did not forsake those seeking you, Lord.

**Psalms 9:12**

Sing praise to Lord dwelling in Sion; announce among nations his deeds.

**Psalms 9:13**

Because, seeking out their bloods, he remembered; he did not forget cry of poor men.

**Psalms 9:14**

Have mercy on me, Lord; see my humiliation from my enemies, you lifting me up from gates of death,

**Psalms 9:15**

so that I may declare all your praises in gates of daughter of Sion. I will rejoice in your salvation.

**Psalms 9:16**

Nations were trapped in corruption which they made; in this snare which they hid, their foot was caught.

**Psalms 9:17**

Lord is known, making judgments; in works of his hands sinner was caught. Song of interlude.

**Psalms 9:18**

Let sinners turn back into Hades, all nations forgetting God.

**Psalms 9:19**

Because poor man will not be forgotten to end, and endurance of poor men will not perish into age.

**Psalms 9:20**

Rise up, Lord; let not man prevail. Let nations be judged before you.

**Psalms 9:21**

Appoint lawgiver over them, Lord; let nations know that they are men. Interlude.

**Psalms 9:22**

Why, Lord, have you stood far off, overlooking in opportunities, in affliction?

**Psalms 9:23**

When ungodly man acts proudly, poor man is set on fire; they are caught in schemes which they devise.

**Psalms 9:24**

Because sinner is praised in desires of his soul, and unjust man is blessed.

**Psalms 9:25**

Sinner provoked Lord; according to multitude of his anger he will not seek him. God is not before him.

**Psalms 9:26**

His ways are profaned in every season; your judgments are taken away from before him. He will dominate all his enemies.

**Psalms 9:27**

For he said in his heart, I will not be shaken from generation to generation, without evil.

**Psalms 9:28**

His mouth is full of curse and bitterness and deceit; under his tongue are toil and pain.

**Psalms 9:29**

He sits in ambush with rich men in hidden places to kill innocent man; his eyes look toward poor man.

**Psalms 9:30**

He lies in ambush in hidden place like lion in its den, lying in ambush to seize poor man, to seize poor man by dragging him away.

**Psalms 9:31**

In his snare he will humble him; he will crouch and fall when he dominates poor men.

**Psalms 9:32**

For he said in his heart, God has forgotten; he turned away his face so as never to see.

**Psalms 9:33**

Rise up, Lord God; let your hand be lifted high. Do not forget poor men.

**Psalms 9:34**

For what reason did ungodly man provoke God? For he said in his heart, He will not seek out.

**Psalms 9:35**

You see, because you observe toil and wrath, to hand them over into your hands. To you poor man is left; you were helper to orphan.

**Psalms 9:36**

Break arm of sinner and evil man; his sin will be sought and by no means found because of it.

**Psalms 9:37**

Lord will reign into age and into age of age; nations, you will perish from his land.

**Psalms 9:38**

Desire of poor men Lord heard; to preparation of their heart your ear attended,

**Psalms 9:39**

to judge orphan and lowly man, so that man upon earth may no longer add to acting great.

### Chapter 10

**Psalms 10:1**

For end. Psalm of David. In Lord I trusted. How will you say to my soul, Migrate to mountains like sparrow?

**Psalms 10:2**

Because behold, sinners stretched bow, prepared arrows in quiver, to shoot in darkness at upright ones in heart.

**Psalms 10:3**

Because what you fitted together they tore down; but righteous man, what did he do?

**Psalms 10:4**

Lord in his holy temple; Lord, his throne in heaven. His eyes look toward poor man; his eyelids examine sons of men.

**Psalms 10:5**

Lord examines righteous man and ungodly man, but one loving injustice hates his own soul.

**Psalms 10:6**

He will rain snares upon sinners, fire and sulfur and blast of storm, portion of their cup.

**Psalms 10:7**

Because Lord is righteous and loved righteousnesses; his face saw uprightness.

### Chapter 11

**Psalms 11:1**

For end. Concerning eighth. Psalm of David.

**Psalms 11:2**

Save me, Lord, because holy man failed, because truths were diminished from sons of men.

**Psalms 11:3**

Each spoke vain things to his neighbor; with deceitful lips, with heart and heart they spoke.

**Psalms 11:4**

May Lord utterly destroy all deceitful lips and tongue speaking great things,

**Psalms 11:5**

those saying, We will magnify our tongue; our lips are with us; who is lord over us?

**Psalms 11:6**

Because of misery of poor men and groaning of needy men, now I will rise up, says Lord; I will set him in salvation; I will speak boldly in him.

**Psalms 11:7**

Words of Lord are pure words, silver refined by fire, tested in earth, purified sevenfold.

**Psalms 11:8**

You, Lord, will guard us and preserve us from this generation and into age.

**Psalms 11:9**

Ungodly men walk around in circle; according to your height you made sons of men much observed.

### Chapter 12

**Psalms 12:1**

For end. Psalm of David.

**Psalms 12:2**

Until when, Lord, will you forget me to end? Until when will you turn your face from me?

**Psalms 12:3**

Until when will I place counsels in my soul, pains in my heart by day? Until when will my enemy be lifted up over me?

**Psalms 12:4**

Look, hear me, Lord my God. Enlighten my eyes, lest I sleep into death,

**Psalms 12:5**

lest my enemy say, I prevailed against him. Those afflicting me will rejoice if I am shaken.

**Psalms 12:6**

But I hoped in your mercy; my heart will rejoice in your salvation. I will sing to Lord who did good to me, and sing praise to name of Lord Most High.

### Chapter 13

**Psalms 13:1**

For end. Psalm of David. Fool said in his heart, There is no God. They were corrupted and became abominable in pursuits; there is none doing kindness, there is not even one.

**Psalms 13:2**

Lord looked down from heaven upon sons of men to see if there is one understanding or seeking God.

**Psalms 13:3**

All turned aside; together they became useless. There is none doing kindness, there is not even one. Their throat open grave; with their tongues they dealt deceitfully; venom of asps under their lips; whose mouth is full of curse and bitterness; their feet sharp to pour out blood.

**Psalms 13:4**

Will not all workers of lawlessness know, those eating my people as food of bread? They did not call upon Lord.

**Psalms 13:5**

There they feared with fear where there was no fear, because God is in righteous generation.

**Psalms 13:6**

You shamed counsel of poor man, because Lord is his hope.

**Psalms 13:7**

Who will give from Sion salvation of Israel? When Lord turns back captivity of his people, let Iakōb rejoice and Israel be glad.

### Chapter 14

**Psalms 14:1**

Psalm of David. Lord, who will sojourn in your tent, and who will camp on your holy mountain?

**Psalms 14:2**

One walking blamelessly and working righteousness, speaking truth in his heart,

**Psalms 14:3**

who did not deal deceitfully with his tongue, nor do evil to his neighbor, and did not take reproach against those near him.

**Psalms 14:4**

Evildoer is despised before him, but those fearing Lord he glorifies; one swearing to his neighbor and not setting it aside,

**Psalms 14:5**

his silver he did not give at interest, and did not take gifts against innocent men. One doing these things will not be shaken into age.

### Chapter 15

**Psalms 15:1**

Inscription of David. Guard me, Lord, because upon you I hoped.

**Psalms 15:2**

I said to Lord, You are my Lord, because you have no need of my good things.

**Psalms 15:3**

To holy ones in his land he made all his wills wondrous in them.

**Psalms 15:4**

Their weaknesses were multiplied; after these things they hastened. I will by no means gather their gatherings from bloods, nor by any means remember their names with my lips.

**Psalms 15:5**

Lord, portion of my inheritance and of my cup, you are one restoring my inheritance to me.

**Psalms 15:6**

Measuring lines fell to me among best things, and indeed my inheritance is best to me.

**Psalms 15:7**

I will bless Lord who gave me understanding; and still, until night, my kidneys disciplined me.

**Psalms 15:8**

I foresaw Lord before me through all things, because he is at my right hand so that I may not be shaken.

**Psalms 15:9**

Because of this my heart was gladdened and my tongue rejoiced; and still my flesh will camp in hope,

**Psalms 15:10**

because you will not forsake my soul to Hades, nor will you give your holy one to see corruption.

**Psalms 15:11**

You made known to me ways of life; you will fill me with gladness with your face; delights at your right hand to end.

### Chapter 16

**Psalms 16:1**

Prayer of David. Hear, Lord, my righteousness; attend to my petition; give ear to my prayer, not with deceitful lips.

**Psalms 16:2**

Let my judgment come out from your face; let my eyes see straight things.

**Psalms 16:3**

You tested my heart, visited by night, refined me, and injustice was not found in me.

**Psalms 16:4**

So that my mouth might not speak works of men, because of words of your lips I kept hard ways.

**Psalms 16:5**

Set right my steps in your tracks, so that my steps may not be shaken.

**Psalms 16:6**

I cried out because you heard me, God. Incline your ear to me and hear my words.

**Psalms 16:7**

Make your mercies wondrous, you saving those hoping upon you from those standing against your right hand.

**Psalms 16:8**

Guard me as apple of eye; in shelter of your wings you will cover me

**Psalms 16:9**

from face of ungodly men who distressed me. My enemies enclosed my soul.

**Psalms 16:10**

Their fat they shut up; their mouth spoke arrogance.

**Psalms 16:11**

Casting me out, now they encircled me; their eyes they set to turn aside into earth.

**Psalms 16:12**

They took me up like lion ready for hunt and like lion-cub dwelling in hidden places.

**Psalms 16:13**

Rise up, Lord; get before them and trip them up. Rescue my soul from ungodly men, your sword, from enemies of your hand,

**Psalms 16:14**

Lord, from few men of earth divide them in their life; and with your hidden things their belly was filled. They were satisfied with sons and left remainders to their little ones.

**Psalms 16:15**

But I in righteousness will appear before your face; I will be satisfied when your glory appears.

### Chapter 17

**Psalms 17:1**

For end. To servant of Lord, David, what he spoke to Lord, words of this song, in day when Lord rescued him from hand of all his enemies and from hand of Saoul.

**Psalms 17:2**

And he said, I will love you, Lord, my strength.

**Psalms 17:3**

Lord my firm place and my refuge and my rescuer, my God my helper, and I will hope upon him, my defender and horn of my salvation, my supporter.

**Psalms 17:4**

Praising, I will call upon Lord, and from my enemies I will be saved.

**Psalms 17:5**

Pangs of death enclosed me, and torrents of lawlessness troubled me.

**Psalms 17:6**

Pangs of Hades surrounded me; snares of death came before me.

**Psalms 17:7**

And in my affliction I called upon Lord, and to my God I cried out. He heard my voice from his holy temple, and my cry before him will enter into his ears.

**Psalms 17:8**

And earth was shaken and became trembling; foundations of mountains were troubled and shaken, because God was angered with them.

**Psalms 17:9**

Smoke went up in his anger, and fire from his face flamed up; coals were kindled from him.

**Psalms 17:10**

And he bent heaven and came down, and gloom under his feet.

**Psalms 17:11**

And he mounted cheroub and flew; he flew upon wings of winds.

**Psalms 17:12**

And he made darkness his hiding place; around him his tent, dark water in clouds of air.

**Psalms 17:13**

From brightness before him clouds passed through, hail and coals of fire.

**Psalms 17:14**

And Lord thundered from heaven, and Most High gave his voice.

**Psalms 17:15**

And he sent out arrows and scattered them; he multiplied lightnings and threw them into confusion.

**Psalms 17:16**

And fountains of waters were seen, and foundations of inhabited world were uncovered from your rebuke, Lord, from breath of spirit of your wrath.

**Psalms 17:17**

He sent from on high and took me; he received me out of many waters.

**Psalms 17:18**

He will rescue me from my strong enemies and from those hating me, because they were stronger than I.

**Psalms 17:19**

They came before me in day of my affliction, and Lord became my support.

**Psalms 17:20**

And he brought me out into broad place; he will rescue me because he desired me.

**Psalms 17:21**

And Lord will repay me according to my righteousness, and according to purity of my hands he will repay me,

**Psalms 17:22**

because I kept ways of Lord and did not act ungodly from my God.

**Psalms 17:23**

Because all his judgments were before me, and his ordinances I did not turn away from me.

**Psalms 17:24**

And I will be blameless with him, and guard myself from my lawlessness.

**Psalms 17:25**

And Lord will repay me according to my righteousness and according to purity of my hands before his eyes.

**Psalms 17:26**

With holy one you will be holy, and with innocent man you will be innocent.

**Psalms 17:27**

And with chosen one you will be chosen, and with crooked one you will twist.

**Psalms 17:28**

Because you will save humble people and humble eyes of proud men.

**Psalms 17:29**

Because you will light my lamp, Lord; my God, you will light my darkness.

**Psalms 17:30**

Because in you I will be rescued from trap, and in my God I will leap over wall.

**Psalms 17:31**

My God, his way blameless; words of Lord refined by fire. He is defender of all hoping upon him.

**Psalms 17:32**

Because who is God besides Lord, and who is God besides our God?

**Psalms 17:33**

God who girds me with strength and set my way blameless,

**Psalms 17:34**

fitting my feet like deer and setting me upon heights,

**Psalms 17:35**

teaching my hands for war, and you made my arms bronze bow.

**Psalms 17:36**

And you gave me defense of my salvation, and your right hand held me up, and your discipline set me straight to end, and this discipline of yours will teach me.

**Psalms 17:37**

You widened my steps under me, and my tracks did not weaken.

**Psalms 17:38**

I will pursue my enemies and overtake them, and I will not turn back until they fail.

**Psalms 17:39**

I will crush them and they will not be able to stand; they will fall under my feet.

**Psalms 17:40**

And you girded me with strength for war; you shackled under me all rising against me.

**Psalms 17:41**

And my enemies you gave to me back, and those hating me you destroyed.

**Psalms 17:42**

They cried out, and there was none saving, to Lord, and he did not hear them.

**Psalms 17:43**

And I will pulverize them like dust before wind; like mud of streets I will smooth them down.

**Psalms 17:44**

Rescue me from contradictions of people; you will set me as head of nations. People whom I did not know served me.

**Psalms 17:45**

At hearing of ear they obeyed me; foreign sons lied to me.

**Psalms 17:46**

Foreign sons grew old and limped from their paths.

**Psalms 17:47**

Lord lives, and blessed my God, and let God of my salvation be exalted,

**Psalms 17:48**

God giving vengeance to me and subjecting peoples under me,

**Psalms 17:49**

my rescuer from angry enemies. From those rising against me you will lift me up; from unjust man you will rescue me.

**Psalms 17:50**

Because of this I will confess to you among nations, Lord, and to your name I will sing praise,

**Psalms 17:51**

magnifying salvations of his king and doing mercy to his Anointed, to David and to his seed into age.

### Chapter 18

**Psalms 18:1**

For end. Psalm of David.

**Psalms 18:2**

Heavens recount glory of God, and firmament announces making of his hands.

**Psalms 18:3**

Day to day gushes word, and night to night announces knowledge.

**Psalms 18:4**

There are no speeches nor words where their voices are not heard.

**Psalms 18:5**

Into all earth their sound went out, and to ends of inhabited world their words. In sun he set his tent.

**Psalms 18:6**

And he as bridegroom coming out of bridal chamber will rejoice like giant to run his course.

**Psalms 18:7**

From edge of heaven is his going out, and his return to edge of heaven, and there is none who will hide from his heat.

**Psalms 18:8**

Law of Lord blameless, turning souls back; testimony of Lord faithful, making little ones wise.

**Psalms 18:9**

Ordinances of Lord straight, gladdening heart; command of Lord radiant, enlightening eyes.

**Psalms 18:10**

Fear of Lord pure, remaining into age of age; judgments of Lord true, justified together.

**Psalms 18:11**

More to be desired than gold and much precious stone, and sweeter than honey and honeycomb.

**Psalms 18:12**

And indeed your servant guards them; in guarding them, much repayment.

**Psalms 18:13**

Who will understand trespasses? From my hidden ones cleanse me,

**Psalms 18:14**

and from strangers spare your servant. If they do not dominate me, then I will be blameless, and I will be cleansed from great sin.

**Psalms 18:15**

And words of my mouth and meditation of my heart will be for favor before you through all things, Lord, my helper and my redeemer.

### Chapter 19

**Psalms 19:1**

For end. Psalm of David.

**Psalms 19:2**

May Lord hear you in day of affliction; may name of God of Iakōb defend you.

**Psalms 19:3**

May he send you help from holy place, and from Sion may he support you.

**Psalms 19:4**

May he remember all your sacrifice and let your whole burnt offering be fat. Interlude.

**Psalms 19:5**

May he give you according to your heart and fulfill all your counsel.

**Psalms 19:6**

We will rejoice in your salvation, and in name of our God we will be magnified. May Lord fulfill all your requests.

**Psalms 19:7**

Now I knew that Lord saved his Anointed; he will hear him from his holy heaven. Salvation of his right hand is in acts of power.

**Psalms 19:8**

These in chariots and these in horses, but we in name of Lord our God will be magnified.

**Psalms 19:9**

They were shackled and fell, but we rose and were set upright.

**Psalms 19:10**

Lord, save your king, and hear us in whatever day we call upon you.

### Chapter 20

**Psalms 20:1**

For end. Psalm of David.

**Psalms 20:2**

Lord, in your strength king will be gladdened, and in your salvation he will greatly rejoice.

**Psalms 20:3**

Desire of his soul you gave to him, and longing of his lips you did not deprive him of. Interlude.

**Psalms 20:4**

Because you got before him with blessings of goodness; you set upon his head crown from precious stone.

**Psalms 20:5**

He asked life from you, and you gave it to him, length of days into age of age.

**Psalms 20:6**

Great his glory in your salvation; glory and magnificence you will place upon him.

**Psalms 20:7**

Because you will give him blessing into age of age; you will gladden him with joy with your face.

**Psalms 20:8**

Because king hopes upon Lord, and in mercy of Most High he will by no means be shaken.

**Psalms 20:9**

May your hand be found by all your enemies; may your right hand find all hating you.

**Psalms 20:10**

You will set them like furnace of fire in time of your face; Lord in his anger will trouble them, and fire will devour them.

**Psalms 20:11**

Their fruit from earth you will destroy, and their seed from sons of men,

**Psalms 20:12**

because they bent evils toward you; they devised counsel which they will not be able to establish.

**Psalms 20:13**

Because you will set them as back in your remnants; you will prepare their face.

**Psalms 20:14**

Be exalted, Lord, in your strength; we will sing and praise your mighty acts.

### Chapter 21

**Psalms 21:1**

For end. Concerning morning help. Psalm of David.

**Psalms 21:2**

God, my God, attend to me. Why did you forsake me? Far from my salvation are words of my trespasses.

**Psalms 21:3**

My God, I will cry by day and you will not hear, and by night, and it is not folly to me.

**Psalms 21:4**

But you dwell among holy ones, praise of Israel.

**Psalms 21:5**

Upon you our fathers hoped; they hoped and you rescued them.

**Psalms 21:6**

To you they cried and were saved; upon you they hoped and were not ashamed.

**Psalms 21:7**

But I am worm and not man, reproach of man and despising of people.

**Psalms 21:8**

All seeing me mocked me; they spoke with lips, they shook head,

**Psalms 21:9**

He hoped upon Lord; let him rescue him, let him save him, because he wants him.

**Psalms 21:10**

Because you are one drawing me out from womb, my hope from breasts of my mother.

**Psalms 21:11**

Upon you I was cast from womb; from belly of my mother you are my God.

**Psalms 21:12**

Do not stand far from me, because affliction is near, because there is no helper.

**Psalms 21:13**

Many calves encircled me; fat bulls surrounded me.

**Psalms 21:14**

They opened their mouth upon me like lion seizing and roaring.

**Psalms 21:15**

Like water I was poured out, and all my bones were scattered; my heart became like wax melting in midst of my belly.

**Psalms 21:16**

My strength dried up like potsherd, and my tongue was glued to my throat, and you brought me down into dust of death.

**Psalms 21:17**

Because many dogs encircled me; gathering of evildoers surrounded me; they dug my hands and feet.

**Psalms 21:18**

I counted all my bones, and they observed and looked on me.

**Psalms 21:19**

They divided my garments among themselves, and cast lot upon my clothing.

**Psalms 21:20**

But you, Lord, do not put my help far away; attend to my support.

**Psalms 21:21**

Rescue my soul from sword, and my only one from hand of dog.

**Psalms 21:22**

Save me from mouth of lion, and my humiliation from horns of unicorns.

**Psalms 21:23**

I will recount your name to my brothers; in midst of assembly I will hymn you.

**Psalms 21:24**

You fearing Lord, praise him; all seed of Iakōb, glorify him; let all seed of Israel fear him,

**Psalms 21:25**

because he did not despise nor loathe petition of poor man, nor turn his face from me, and when I cried to him he heard me.

**Psalms 21:26**

From you my praise in great assembly; my vows I will repay before those fearing him.

**Psalms 21:27**

Poor men will eat and be filled, and those seeking him will praise Lord; their hearts will live into age of age.

**Psalms 21:28**

All ends of earth will remember and turn to Lord, and all families of nations will worship before you.

**Psalms 21:29**

Because kingdom belongs to Lord, and he rules nations.

**Psalms 21:30**

All fat ones of earth ate and worshiped; before him all going down into earth will fall down, and my soul lives to him.

**Psalms 21:31**

And my seed will serve him; coming generation will be announced to Lord.

**Psalms 21:32**

And they will announce his righteousness to people being born, because Lord did it.

### Chapter 22

**Psalms 22:1**

Psalm of David. Lord shepherds me, and nothing will fail me.

**Psalms 22:2**

Into place of grass there he camped me; beside water of rest he nourished me.

**Psalms 22:3**

He turned my soul back; he led me upon tracks of righteousness for sake of his name.

**Psalms 22:4**

For even if I walk in midst of shadow of death, I will not fear evils, because you are with me; your rod and your staff, these comforted me.

**Psalms 22:5**

You prepared table before me opposite those afflicting me; you anointed my head with oil, and your cup intoxicating like strongest wine.

**Psalms 22:6**

And your mercy will pursue me all days of my life, and my dwelling in house of Lord to length of days.

### Chapter 23

**Psalms 23:1**

Psalm of David. Of first of Sabbaths. Earth belongs to Lord and its fullness, inhabited world and all dwelling in it.

**Psalms 23:2**

He founded it upon seas and prepared it upon rivers.

**Psalms 23:3**

Who will go up to mountain of Lord, and who will stand in his holy place?

**Psalms 23:4**

Innocent in hands and clean in heart, who did not take his soul upon vanity and did not swear in deceit to his neighbor.

**Psalms 23:5**

This one will receive blessing from Lord and mercy from God his savior.

**Psalms 23:6**

This is generation of those seeking him, seeking face of God of Iakōb. Interlude.

**Psalms 23:7**

Lift up gates, your rulers, and be lifted up, everlasting gates, and king of glory will enter.

**Psalms 23:8**

Who is this king of glory? Lord strong and mighty, Lord mighty in war.

**Psalms 23:9**

Lift up gates, your rulers, and be lifted up, everlasting gates, and king of glory will enter.

**Psalms 23:10**

Who is this king of glory? Lord of hosts, he is king of glory.

### Chapter 24

**Psalms 24:1**

Psalm of David. To you, Lord, I lifted my soul, O my God.

**Psalms 24:2**

Upon you I trusted; may I not be ashamed, nor let my enemies mock me.

**Psalms 24:3**

For indeed all enduring you will by no means be ashamed; let all acting lawlessly for nothing be ashamed.

**Psalms 24:4**

Your ways, Lord, make known to me, and your paths teach me.

**Psalms 24:5**

Lead me upon your truth and teach me, because you are God my savior, and I endured you all day.

**Psalms 24:6**

Remember your compassions, Lord, and your mercies, because they are from age.

**Psalms 24:7**

Sins of my youth and my ignorances do not remember; according to your mercy remember me, because of your goodness, Lord.

**Psalms 24:8**

Good and upright is Lord; because of this he will give law to sinners in way.

**Psalms 24:9**

He will guide meek ones in judgment; he will teach meek ones his ways.

**Psalms 24:10**

All ways of Lord are mercy and truth to those seeking out his covenant and his testimonies.

**Psalms 24:11**

For sake of your name, Lord, you will be propitious to my sin, because it is great.

**Psalms 24:12**

Who is man fearing Lord? He will give law to him in way which he chose.

**Psalms 24:13**

His soul will lodge among good things, and his seed will inherit earth.

**Psalms 24:14**

Lord is stronghold of those fearing him, and name of Lord belongs to those fearing him, and his covenant to show it to them.

**Psalms 24:15**

My eyes are always toward Lord, because he will draw my feet out of snare.

**Psalms 24:16**

Look upon me and have mercy on me, because I am only one and poor.

**Psalms 24:17**

Afflictions of my heart were widened; out of my necessities bring me out.

**Psalms 24:18**

See my humiliation and my toil, and forgive all my sins.

**Psalms 24:19**

See my enemies, because they were multiplied and hated me with unjust hatred.

**Psalms 24:20**

Guard my soul and rescue me; may I not be ashamed, because I hoped upon you.

**Psalms 24:21**

Blameless and upright men clung to me, because I endured you, Lord.

**Psalms 24:22**

Redeem, O God, Israel from all his afflictions.

### Chapter 25

**Psalms 25:1**

Of David. Judge me, Lord, because I walked in my innocence, and hoping upon Lord I will by no means weaken.

**Psalms 25:2**

Test me, Lord, and try me; refine my kidneys and my heart.

**Psalms 25:3**

Because your mercy is before my eyes, and I was well-pleasing in your truth.

**Psalms 25:4**

I did not sit with assembly of vanity, and with lawless men I will by no means enter.

**Psalms 25:5**

I hated assembly of evildoers, and with ungodly men I will by no means sit.

**Psalms 25:6**

I will wash my hands among innocent ones, and circle your altar, Lord,

**Psalms 25:7**

to hear voice of praise and recount all your wondrous deeds.

**Psalms 25:8**

Lord, I loved beauty of your house and place of tent of your glory.

**Psalms 25:9**

Do not destroy my soul together with ungodly men, nor my life with men of bloods,

**Psalms 25:10**

in whose hands are lawless acts, and their right hand was filled with gifts.

**Psalms 25:11**

But I walked in my innocence; redeem me and have mercy on me.

**Psalms 25:12**

For my foot stood in uprightness; in assemblies I will bless you, Lord.

### Chapter 26

**Psalms 26:1**

Of David, before being anointed. The Lord is my illumination and my savior; whom shall I fear? The Lord is defender of my life; from whom shall I be afraid?

**Psalms 26:2**

When evildoers draw near upon me to eat my flesh, those afflicting me and my enemies, they weakened and fell.

**Psalms 26:3**

If camp should line up against me, my heart will not fear. If war rise up against me, in this I hope.

**Psalms 26:4**

One thing I asked from Lord; this I will seek out: to dwell me in house of Lord all days of my life, to behold delight of Lord and visit his temple.

**Psalms 26:5**

Because he hid me in tent in day of my evils; he sheltered me in hidden place of his tent; on rock he lifted me up.

**Psalms 26:6**

And now behold, he lifted my head over enemies around me. I went around and sacrificed in his tent sacrifice of shouting; I will sing and praise Lord.

**Psalms 26:7**

Hear, Lord, my voice with which I cried out; have mercy on me and hear me.

**Psalms 26:8**

To you my heart said, My face sought your face; your face, Lord, I will seek.

**Psalms 26:9**

Do not turn your face from me, nor turn away in anger from your servant. Become my helper; do not cast me off and do not forsake me, God my savior.

**Psalms 26:10**

Because my father and my mother forsook me, but Lord took me in.

**Psalms 26:11**

Give me law, Lord, in your way, and lead me in straight path because of my enemies.

**Psalms 26:12**

Do not hand me over to souls of those afflicting me, because unjust witnesses rose against me and injustice lied to itself.

**Psalms 26:13**

I believe to see good things of Lord in land of living ones.

**Psalms 26:14**

Endure Lord; act like man, and let your heart be strengthened, and endure Lord.

### Chapter 27

**Psalms 27:1**

Of David. To you, Lord, I cried out. My God, do not be silent from me, lest if you be silent from me, I become like those going down into pit.

**Psalms 27:2**

Hear voice of my petition when I beg to you, when I lift my hands toward your holy temple.

**Psalms 27:3**

Do not drag my soul away with sinners, and do not destroy me together with those working injustice, those speaking peace with their neighbors while evils are in their hearts.

**Psalms 27:4**

Give to them according to their works and according to evil of their pursuits; according to works of their hands give to them; repay to them their repayment.

**Psalms 27:5**

Because they did not understand works of Lord and works of his hands, you will pull them down and by no means build them up.

**Psalms 27:6**

Blessed Lord, because he heard voice of my petition.

**Psalms 27:7**

Lord my helper and my defender; upon him my heart hoped and I was helped, and my flesh bloomed again, and by my will I will confess to him.

**Psalms 27:8**

Lord is strength of his people, and defender of salvations of his Anointed is he.

**Psalms 27:9**

Save your people and bless your inheritance, and shepherd them and lift them up until age.

### Chapter 28

**Psalms 28:1**

Psalm of David. Of exiting tent. Bring to Lord, sons of God; bring to Lord sons of rams; bring to Lord glory and honor.

**Psalms 28:2**

Bring to Lord glory to his name; worship Lord in his holy court.

**Psalms 28:3**

Voice of Lord upon waters; God of glory thundered; Lord upon many waters.

**Psalms 28:4**

Voice of Lord in strength; voice of Lord in magnificence.

**Psalms 28:5**

Voice of Lord shattering cedars, and Lord will shatter cedars of Lebanon.

**Psalms 28:6**

And he will pulverize them like calf, Lebanon, and the beloved one like son of unicorns.

**Psalms 28:7**

Voice of Lord cutting through flame of fire.

**Psalms 28:8**

Voice of Lord shaking wilderness, and Lord will shake wilderness of Kadēs.

**Psalms 28:9**

Voice of Lord fitting deer and uncovering forests; and in his temple every one says, Glory.

**Psalms 28:10**

Lord will dwell over flood, and Lord will sit king into age.

**Psalms 28:11**

Lord will give strength to his people; Lord will bless his people in peace.

### Chapter 29

**Psalms 29:1**

For end. Psalm, song of dedication of house, of David.

**Psalms 29:2**

I will exalt you, Lord, because you took me up and did not gladden my enemies over me.

**Psalms 29:3**

Lord my God, I cried to you and you healed me.

**Psalms 29:4**

Lord, you brought up my soul from Hades; you saved me from those going down into pit.

**Psalms 29:5**

Sing praise to Lord, his holy ones, and confess to remembrance of his holiness.

**Psalms 29:6**

Because anger in his wrath and life in his will. At evening weeping will lodge, and by morning glad shouting.

**Psalms 29:7**
