**Psalms 103:25**

This sea, great and broad-spaced: there creeping things without number, small animals with great.

**Psalms 103:26**

There ships pass through; this dragon you formed to play in it.

**Psalms 103:27**

**Psalms 103:28**

**Psalms 103:29**

**Psalms 103:30**

**Psalms 103:31**

Let glory of Lord be forever; Lord will rejoice in his works,

**Psalms 103:32**

**Psalms 103:33**

I will sing to Lord in my life; I will make melody to my God while I exist.

**Psalms 103:34**

**Psalms 103:35**

Let sinners fail from earth, and lawless ones so as not to exist. Bless Lord, my soul.

### Chapter 104

**Psalms 104:1**

**Psalms 104:2**

**Psalms 104:3**

**Psalms 104:4**

**Psalms 104:5**

**Psalms 104:6**

**Psalms 104:7**

He Lord our God; in all earth his judgments.

**Psalms 104:8**

**Psalms 104:9**

**Psalms 104:27**

**Psalms 104:28**

**Psalms 104:29**

**Psalms 104:30**

**Psalms 104:31**

**Psalms 104:32**

**Psalms 104:33**

**Psalms 104:34**

**Psalms 104:35**

**Psalms 104:36**

**Psalms 104:37**

**Psalms 104:39**

**Psalms 104:40**

**Psalms 104:41**

**Psalms 104:42**

**Psalms 104:43**

And he led out his people with exultation and his chosen ones with gladness.

**Psalms 104:44**

And he gave them lands of nations, and they inherited labors of peoples,

### Chapter 105

**Psalms 105:1**

Alleluia. Confess to Lord, because kind, because his mercy forever.

**Psalms 105:2**

**Psalms 105:3**

**Psalms 105:4**

**Psalms 105:5**

**Psalms 105:6**

**Psalms 105:7**

**Psalms 105:8**

And he saved them for sake of his name, to make known his dominion.

**Psalms 105:9**

And he rebuked Red Sea and it dried up, and he guided them in deep as in wilderness.

**Psalms 105:10**

**Psalms 105:11**

**Psalms 105:12**

**Psalms 105:13**

**Psalms 105:14**

**Psalms 105:15**

And he gave them their request and sent fullness into their souls.

**Psalms 105:16**

And they angered Moses in camp, and Aaron, holy one of Lord.

**Psalms 105:17**

**Psalms 105:18**

And fire burned in their assembly; flame consumed sinners.

**Psalms 105:19**

And they made calf in Horeb and worshiped carved image.

**Psalms 105:20**

**Psalms 105:21**

**Psalms 105:22**

**Psalms 105:23**

And he said to destroy them, if not Moses, his chosen one, stood in breaking before him to turn back his anger, so as not to destroy.

**Psalms 105:24**

And they despised desirable land; they did not believe his word.

**Psalms 105:25**

**Psalms 105:26**

And he raised his hand against them, to cast them down in wilderness,

**Psalms 105:27**

**Psalms 105:28**

And they were joined to Beelphegor and ate sacrifices of dead ones.

**Psalms 105:29**

And they provoked him in their practices, and falling was multiplied among them.

**Psalms 105:30**

And Phinehas stood and propitiated, and breaking ceased.

**Psalms 105:31**

And it was counted to him as righteousness from generation to generation forever.

**Psalms 105:32**

And they angered him at water of contradiction, and Moses was harmed because of them,

**Psalms 105:33**

**Psalms 105:34**

**Psalms 105:35**

**Psalms 105:36**

**Psalms 105:37**

**Psalms 105:38**

**Psalms 105:39**

And they were defiled in their works and prostituted in their practices.

**Psalms 105:40**

And Lord was angered in fury against his people and abhorred his inheritance.

**Psalms 105:41**

And he handed them into hands of nations, and those hating them ruled over them.

**Psalms 105:42**

And their enemies afflicted them, and they were humbled under their hands.

**Psalms 105:43**

**Psalms 105:44**

And he saw when they were afflicted, when he heard their supplication.

**Psalms 105:45**

And he remembered his covenant and relented according to multitude of his mercy.

**Psalms 105:46**

And he gave them into compassions before all who had taken them captive.

**Psalms 105:47**

### Chapter 106

**Psalms 106:1**

Alleluia. Confess to Lord, because kind, because his mercy forever.

**Psalms 106:3**

### Chapter 107

**Psalms 107:1**

### Chapter 108

**Psalms 108:1**

**Psalms 108:3**

**Psalms 108:5**

**Psalms 108:6**

**Psalms 108:7**

**Psalms 108:8**

**Psalms 108:9**

**Psalms 108:20**

**Psalms 108:21**

**Psalms 108:22**

**Psalms 108:23**

**Psalms 108:24**

**Psalms 108:26**

Let your hand come to save me, because I chose your commandments.

**Psalms 118:174**

I longed for your salvation, Lord, and your law my meditation.

**Psalms 118:175**

My soul will live and praise you, and your judgments will help me.

**Psalms 118:176**

I wandered like sheep lost; seek your servant, because your commandments I did not forget.

### Chapter 119

**Psalms 119:1**

Song of ascents. To Lord, in my being afflicted, I cried, and he heard me.

**Psalms 119:2**

Lord, rescue my soul from unjust lips and from deceitful tongue.

**Psalms 119:3**

What should be given to you, and what should be added to you, against deceitful tongue?

**Psalms 119:4**

Sharpened arrows of mighty one, with desert coals.

**Psalms 119:5**

Alas me, because my sojourning lengthened; I camped with tents of Kedar.

**Psalms 119:6**

My soul long sojourned.

**Psalms 119:7**

With those hating peace, I was peaceable; when I spoke to them, they warred against me for nothing.

### Chapter 120

**Psalms 120:1**

Song of ascents. I lifted my eyes to mountains; from where will my help come?

**Psalms 120:2**

My help from Lord, maker of heaven and earth.

**Psalms 120:3**

Do not let your foot be shaken; may one guarding you not slumber.

**Psalms 120:4**

Behold, keeper of Israel will neither slumber nor sleep.

**Psalms 120:5**

Lord will guard you; Lord your shelter at right hand.

**Psalms 120:6**

By day sun will not burn you, nor moon by night.

**Psalms 120:7**

Lord will guard you from every evil; he will guard your soul.

**Psalms 120:8**

Lord will guard your going in and your going out, from now and until age.

### Chapter 121

**Psalms 121:1**

Song of ascents. I rejoiced over those saying to me, "To house of Lord we will go."

**Psalms 121:2**

Our feet stood in your courts, Jerusalem.

**Psalms 121:3**

Jerusalem, being built as city whose fellowship together one and same.

**Psalms 121:4**

For there tribes went up, tribes of Lord, testimony for Israel, to give thanks to name of Lord.

**Psalms 121:5**

Because there thrones sat for judgment, thrones over house of David.

**Psalms 121:6**

Ask now things for peace of Jerusalem, and prosperity to those loving you.

**Psalms 121:7**

Let peace now be in your strength, and prosperity in your towers.

**Psalms 121:8**

For sake of my brothers and neighbors, I kept speaking peace concerning you.

**Psalms 121:9**

For sake of house of Lord our God, I sought good things for you.

### Chapter 122

**Psalms 122:1**

Song of ascents. To you I lifted my eyes, one dwelling in heaven.

**Psalms 122:2**

Behold, as eyes of servants toward hands of their masters, as eyes of maidservant toward hands of her mistress, so our eyes toward Lord our God until he shows us mercy.

**Psalms 122:3**

Have mercy on us, Lord, have mercy on us, because greatly we were filled with contempt.

**Psalms 122:4**

Still more our soul filled with reproach from prosperous ones and contempt from proud ones.

### Chapter 123

**Psalms 123:1**

Song of ascents. If not that Lord was among us, let Israel say now.

**Psalms 123:2**

If not that Lord was among us when men rose against us,

**Psalms 123:3**

then alive they would have swallowed us when their anger blazed against us.

**Psalms 123:4**

Then water would have drowned us; torrent passed over our soul.

**Psalms 123:5**

Then our soul passed over water unendurable.

**Psalms 123:6**

Blessed Lord, who did not give us for prey to their teeth.

**Psalms 123:7**

Our soul like sparrow rescued from snare of hunters; snare crushed, and we rescued.

**Psalms 123:8**

Our help in name of Lord, maker of heaven and earth.

### Chapter 124

**Psalms 124:1**

Song of ascents. Those trusting in Lord like Mount Zion, not shaken forever.

**Psalms 124:2**

Mountains around her, and Lord around his people, from now and until age.

**Psalms 124:3**

Because Lord will not leave rod of sinners upon lot of righteous, lest righteous stretch out their hands in lawlessness.

**Psalms 124:4**

Do good, Lord, to good ones and to upright in heart.

**Psalms 124:5**

But those turning aside into crooked ways Lord will lead away with workers of lawlessness. Peace on Israel.

### Chapter 125

**Psalms 125:1**

Song of ascents. When Lord turned back captivity of Zion, we became like comforted ones.

**Psalms 125:2**

Then our mouth filled with joy and our tongue with exultation; then they will say among nations, "Lord magnified doing with them."

**Psalms 125:3**

Lord magnified doing with us; we became rejoicing.

**Psalms 125:4**

Turn back, Lord, our captivity, like torrents in south.

**Psalms 125:5**

Those sowing in tears will reap in exultation.

**Psalms 125:6**

Going they went and wept, carrying their seeds; coming they will come in exultation, carrying their sheaves.

### Chapter 126

**Psalms 126:1**

Song of ascents. Of Solomon. Unless Lord build house, in vain builders labored; unless Lord guard city, in vain guard kept awake.

**Psalms 126:2**

In vain for you to rise early, to rise after sitting down, you eating bread of pain, when he gives sleep to his beloved.

**Psalms 126:3**

Behold, sons inheritance of Lord, reward of fruit of womb.

**Psalms 126:4**

Like arrows in hand of mighty one, so sons of those thrust out.

**Psalms 126:5**

Blessed man who will fill his desire from them; they will not be shamed when they speak with their enemies in gate.

### Chapter 127

**Psalms 127:1**

Song of ascents. Blessed all fearing Lord, those walking in his ways.

**Psalms 127:2**

Labors of your fruits you will eat; blessed you, and well for you.

**Psalms 127:3**

Your wife like vine flourishing in recesses of your house; your sons like olive shoots around your table.

**Psalms 127:4**

Behold, thus man fearing Lord will be blessed.

**Psalms 127:5**

May Lord bless you from Zion, and may you see good things of Jerusalem all days of your life.

**Psalms 127:6**

And may you see sons of your sons. Peace upon Israel.

### Chapter 128

**Psalms 128:1**

Song of ascents. Many times they warred against me from my youth; let Israel say now.

**Psalms 128:2**

Many times they warred against me from my youth, yet indeed they were not able against me.

**Psalms 128:3**

On my back sinners built; they lengthened their lawlessness.

**Psalms 128:4**

Lord righteous cut necks of sinners.

**Psalms 128:5**

Let all hating Zion be shamed and turned backward.

**Psalms 128:6**

Let them become like grass of housetops, which before being pulled up dried up.

**Psalms 128:7**

With which reaper did not fill his hand, nor gatherer of sheaves his bosom.

**Psalms 128:8**

And passersby did not say, "Blessing of Lord upon you; we blessed you in name of Lord."

### Chapter 129

**Psalms 129:1**

Song of ascents. Out of depths I cried to you, Lord.

**Psalms 129:2**

Lord, hear my voice; let your ears attend to voice of my supplication.

**Psalms 129:3**

If you should watch lawless deeds, Lord, Lord, who will stand?

**Psalms 129:4**

Because with you propitiation.

**Psalms 129:5**

For sake of your law I waited for you, Lord; my soul waited for your word.

**Psalms 129:6**

My soul hoped in Lord from morning watch until night; from morning watch let Israel hope in Lord.

**Psalms 129:7**

Because with Lord mercy, and much redemption with him.

**Psalms 129:8**

And he will redeem Israel from all his lawless deeds.

### Chapter 130

**Psalms 130:1**

Song of ascents. Of David. Lord, my heart not exalted, nor my eyes raised high, nor I walked in great things nor in marvels beyond me.

**Psalms 130:2**

If not, I was humble-minded, but I lifted my soul like child weaned against its mother, like recompense upon my soul.

**Psalms 130:3**

Let Israel hope in Lord from now and until age.

### Chapter 131

**Psalms 131:1**

Song of ascents. Remember, Lord, David and all his gentleness.

**Psalms 131:2**

How he swore to Lord, vowed to God of Jacob.

**Psalms 131:3**

If I enter tent of my house, if I go up upon bed of my couch,

**Psalms 131:4**

if I give sleep to my eyes and slumber to my eyelids and rest to my temples,

**Psalms 131:5**

until I find place for Lord, tabernacle for God of Jacob.

**Psalms 131:6**

Behold, we heard of it in Ephratha; we found it in fields of the wood.

**Psalms 131:7**

We will enter his tabernacles; we will worship at place where his feet stood.

**Psalms 131:8**

Rise, Lord, into your rest, you and ark of your holiness.

**Psalms 131:9**

Your priests will clothe themselves with righteousness, and your holy ones will exult.

**Psalms 131:10**

For sake of David your servant, do not turn away face of your anointed.

**Psalms 131:11**

Lord swore truth to David, and he will not set it aside: from fruit of your belly I will set upon your throne.

**Psalms 131:12**

If your sons keep my covenant and these testimonies that I will teach them, their sons also forever will sit upon your throne.

**Psalms 131:13**

Because Lord chose Zion; he chose her for dwelling to himself.

**Psalms 131:14**

This my resting-place forever and ever; here I will dwell, because I chose her.

**Psalms 131:15**

Her provision blessing I will bless; her poor I will satisfy with breads.

**Psalms 131:16**

Her priests I will clothe with salvation, and her holy ones with exultation will exult.

**Psalms 131:17**

There I will cause horn to spring up for David; I prepared lamp for my anointed.

**Psalms 131:18**

His enemies I will clothe with shame, but upon him my holiness will flower.

### Chapter 132

**Psalms 132:1**

Song of ascents. Of David. Behold now, what good or what pleasant, but brothers dwelling together.

**Psalms 132:2**

Like oil upon head, descending upon beard, beard of Aaron, descending upon hem of his garment.

**Psalms 132:3**

Like dew of Hermon descending upon mountains of Zion, because there Lord commanded blessing and life until age.

### Chapter 133

**Psalms 133:1**

Song of ascents. Behold now, bless Lord, all servants of Lord, standing in house of Lord, in courts of house of our God.

**Psalms 133:2**

In nights lift your hands to holy things and bless Lord.

**Psalms 133:3**

Lord bless you from Zion, maker of heaven and earth.

### Chapter 134

**Psalms 134:1**

Hallelujah. Praise name of Lord; praise Lord, servants.

**Psalms 134:2**

Those standing in house of Lord, in courts of house of our God.

**Psalms 134:3**

Praise Lord, because Lord good; sing psalms to his name, because good.

**Psalms 134:4**

Because Lord chose Jacob for himself, Israel for his special possession.

**Psalms 134:5**

Because I knew Lord great, and our Lord beyond all gods.

**Psalms 134:6**

All that Lord wanted he did in heaven and on earth, in seas and in all deeps.

**Psalms 134:7**

Raising clouds from ends of earth, he made lightnings for rain, bringing winds from his treasuries.

**Psalms 134:8**

Who struck firstborn of Egypt, from man to beast.

**Psalms 134:9**

He sent signs and wonders into your midst, Egypt, against Pharaoh and all his servants.

**Psalms 134:10**

Who struck many nations and killed mighty kings.

**Psalms 134:11**

Sihon king of Amorites and Og king of Bashan and all kingdoms of Canaan.

**Psalms 134:12**

And gave their land inheritance, inheritance to Israel his people.

**Psalms 134:13**

Lord, your name forever; Lord, your memorial from generation to generation.

**Psalms 134:14**

Because Lord will judge his people and over his servants he will be comforted.

**Psalms 134:15**

Idols of nations silver and gold, works of hands of men.

**Psalms 134:16**

Mouths they have and will not speak; eyes they have and will not see.

**Psalms 134:17**

Ears they have and will not hear; noses they have and will not smell; hands they have and will not feel; feet they have and will not walk; no sound in their throat, for no spirit in their mouth.

**Psalms 134:18**

Like them may those making them become, and all trusting in them.

**Psalms 134:19**

House of Israel, bless Lord; house of Aaron, bless Lord.

**Psalms 134:20**

House of Levi, bless Lord; those fearing Lord, bless Lord.

**Psalms 134:21**

Blessed Lord from Zion, one dwelling in Jerusalem.

### Chapter 135

**Psalms 135:1**

Hallelujah. Give thanks to Lord, because kind, because his mercy forever.

**Psalms 135:2**

Give thanks to God of gods, because his mercy forever.

**Psalms 135:3**

Give thanks to Lord of lords, because his mercy forever.

**Psalms 135:4**

To one doing great wonders alone, because his mercy forever.

**Psalms 135:5**

To one making heavens in understanding, because his mercy forever.

**Psalms 135:6**

To one establishing earth upon waters, because his mercy forever.

**Psalms 135:7**

To one making great lights alone, because his mercy forever.

**Psalms 135:8**

Sun for authority of day, because his mercy forever.

**Psalms 135:9**

Moon and stars for authority of night, because his mercy forever.

**Psalms 135:10**

To one striking Egypt with their firstborn, because his mercy forever.

**Psalms 135:11**

And bringing Israel out from their midst, because his mercy forever.

**Psalms 135:12**

With strong hand and with high arm, because his mercy forever.

**Psalms 135:13**

To one cutting Red Sea into divisions, because his mercy forever.

**Psalms 135:14**

And leading Israel through its midst, because his mercy forever.

**Psalms 135:15**

And shaking off Pharaoh and his force into Red Sea, because his mercy forever.

**Psalms 135:16**

To one leading his people through wilderness, because his mercy forever; to one bringing water from sheer rock, because his mercy forever.

**Psalms 135:17**

To one striking great kings, because his mercy forever.

**Psalms 135:18**

And killing mighty kings, because his mercy forever.

**Psalms 135:19**

Sihon king of Amorites, because his mercy forever.

**Psalms 135:20**

And Og king of Bashan, because his mercy forever.

**Psalms 135:21**

And giving their land inheritance, because his mercy forever.

**Psalms 135:22**

Inheritance to Israel his servant, because his mercy forever.

**Psalms 135:23**

Because in our humiliation Lord remembered us, because his mercy forever.

**Psalms 135:24**

And redeemed us from our enemies, because his mercy forever.

**Psalms 135:25**

One giving food to all flesh, because his mercy forever.

**Psalms 135:26**

Give thanks to God of heaven, because his mercy forever. Give thanks to Lord of lords, because his mercy forever.

### Chapter 136

**Psalms 136:1**

Of David. By rivers of Babylon, there we sat and wept when remembering Zion.

**Psalms 136:2**

On willows in midst of it we hung our instruments.

**Psalms 136:3**

Because there those taking us captive asked us for words of songs, and those carrying us away asked hymn: "Sing us from songs of Zion."

**Psalms 136:4**

How should we sing song of Lord on foreign land?

**Psalms 136:5**

If I forget you, Jerusalem, let my right hand be forgotten.

**Psalms 136:6**

Let my tongue cling to my throat if I do not remember you, if I do not set Jerusalem first at beginning of my gladness.

**Psalms 136:7**

Remember, Lord, sons of Edom in day of Jerusalem, those saying, "Empty it, empty it, down to its foundation."

**Psalms 136:8**

Daughter of Babylon, wretched one, blessed who will repay you repayment that you repaid to us.

**Psalms 136:9**

Blessed who will seize and dash your infants against rock.

### Chapter 137

**Psalms 137:1**

Of David. I will give thanks to you, Lord, with whole heart, because you heard sayings of my mouth; before angels I will sing psalms to you.

**Psalms 137:2**

I will worship toward your holy temple and give thanks to your name for your mercy and your truth, because you magnified your saying above every name.

**Psalms 137:3**

In whatever day I call on you, quickly hear me; with power in my soul you will greatly strengthen me.

**Psalms 137:4**

Let all kings of earth give thanks to you, Lord, because they heard all sayings of your mouth.

**Psalms 137:5**

And let them sing in ways of Lord, because great glory of Lord.

**Psalms 137:6**

Because Lord high and looks upon humble things, and high things he knows from far away.

**Psalms 137:7**

If I walk in midst of affliction, you will make me live; against anger of my enemies you stretched out your hand, and your right hand saved me.

**Psalms 137:8**

Lord will repay on my behalf; Lord, your mercy forever. Works of your hands do not disregard.

### Chapter 138

**Psalms 138:1**

For end. Psalm of David. Lord, you tested me and knew me.

**Psalms 138:2**

You knew my sitting down and my rising up; you understood my thoughts from far away.

**Psalms 138:3**

My path and my measuring line you traced out, and all my ways you foresaw.

**Psalms 138:4**

Because no word on my tongue—

**Psalms 138:5**

behold, Lord, you knew all last things and first things; you formed me and laid your hand upon me.

**Psalms 138:6**

Your knowledge made wondrous beyond me; it grew strong; I will not be able toward it.

**Psalms 138:7**

Where should I go from your spirit, and where should I flee from your face?

**Psalms 138:8**

If I go up into heaven, you there; if I go down into Hades, present.

**Psalms 138:9**

If I take up my wings at dawn and dwell in uttermost parts of sea,

**Psalms 138:10**

even there your hand will guide me and your right hand will hold me fast.

**Psalms 138:11**

And I said, "Then darkness will trample me," yet night illumination in my delight.

**Psalms 138:12**

Because darkness will not be darkened from you, and night will be lit as day; as its darkness, so also its light.

**Psalms 138:13**

Because you acquired my inward parts, Lord; you took hold of me from my mother's womb.

**Psalms 138:14**

I will give thanks to you because fearfully I was made wondrous; wondrous your works, and my soul knows very much.

**Psalms 138:15**

My bone not hidden from you, which you made in secret, and my substance in lowest parts of earth.

**Psalms 138:16**

Your eyes saw my unformed thing, and in your book all will be written; days will be formed, and no one among them.

**Psalms 138:17**

To me your friends, God, were greatly honored; their chief ones grew very strong.

**Psalms 138:18**

I will number them, and beyond sand they will multiply; I awoke, and still I am with you.

**Psalms 138:19**

If only you would kill sinners, God; men of blood, turn aside from me.

**Psalms 138:20**

Because they speak of you for scheming; they will take your cities in vain.

**Psalms 138:21**

Did I not hate those hating you, Lord, and waste away over your enemies?

**Psalms 138:22**

With perfect hatred I hated them; they became enemies to me.

**Psalms 138:23**

Test me, God, and know my heart; examine me and know my paths.

**Psalms 138:24**

And see if way of lawlessness in me, and guide me in age-lasting way.

### Chapter 139

**Psalms 139:1**

For end. Psalm of David.

**Psalms 139:2**

Rescue me, Lord, from evil man; from unjust man deliver me.

**Psalms 139:3**

Who devised injustices in heart; whole day they arrayed wars.

**Psalms 139:4**

They sharpened their tongue like serpent; venom of asps under their lips. Selah.

**Psalms 139:5**

Guard me, Lord, from hand of sinner; from unjust men deliver me, who devised to trip my steps.

**Psalms 139:6**

Proud ones hid snare for me and stretched ropes; traps for my feet, beside path they set stumbling block for me. Selah.

**Psalms 139:7**

I said to Lord, "My God you." Give ear, Lord, to voice of my supplication.

**Psalms 139:8**

Lord, Lord, strength of my salvation, you overshadowed over my head in day of war.

**Psalms 139:9**

Do not give me over, Lord, from my desire to sinner; they schemed against me; do not abandon me, lest they be exalted. Selah.

**Psalms 139:10**

Head of their encirclement—labor of their lips will cover them.

**Psalms 139:11**

Coals will fall upon them; in fire you will cast them down, in miseries they will not withstand.

**Psalms 139:12**

Tongue-man will not be directed on earth; evil will hunt unjust man into destruction.

**Psalms 139:13**

I knew Lord will do judgment of poor one and justice of needy.

**Psalms 139:14**

Yet righteous will give thanks to your name, and upright will dwell with your face.

### Chapter 140

**Psalms 140:1**

Psalm of David. Lord, I cried to you; hear me. Attend to voice of my supplication when I cry to you.

**Psalms 140:2**

Let my prayer be set straight as incense before you, lifting up of my hands evening sacrifice.

**Psalms 140:3**

Set guard, Lord, for my mouth, and door of enclosure around my lips.

**Psalms 140:4**

Do not incline my heart to words of evil, to make excuses of excuses in sins with men working lawlessness, and I will not join with their chosen ones.

**Psalms 140:5**

Righteous will instruct me in mercy and reprove me, but oil of sinner may it not fatten my head; because still my prayer against their pleasures.

**Psalms 140:6**

Their judges were swallowed up beside rock; they will hear my words because they were pleasant.

**Psalms 140:7**

Like thickness of earth broken up upon ground, our bones were scattered beside Hades.

**Psalms 140:8**

Because toward you, Lord, Lord, my eyes; in you I hoped; do not take away my soul.

**Psalms 140:9**

Guard me from snare they set together for me and from stumbling blocks of workers of lawlessness.

**Psalms 140:10**

Sinners will fall in his net; alone I am until I pass by.

### Chapter 141

**Psalms 141:1**

Of understanding. Of David, when he was in cave. Prayer.

**Psalms 141:2**

With my voice to Lord I cried; with my voice to Lord I made supplication.

**Psalms 141:3**

I pour out before him my supplication; my affliction before him I declare.

**Psalms 141:4**

When my spirit was failing from me, then you knew my paths. In this way where I walked, they hid snare for me.

**Psalms 141:5**

I was looking to right and watching, and there was none knowing me; flight perished from me, and none seeking my soul.

**Psalms 141:6**

I cried to you, Lord; I said, "You my hope, my portion in land of living."

**Psalms 141:7**

Attend to my supplication, because I was greatly humbled; rescue me from those pursuing me, because they grew stronger than I.

**Psalms 141:8**

Bring my soul out from prison to give thanks to your name, Lord. Righteous will wait for me until you repay me.

### Chapter 142

**Psalms 142:1**

Psalm of David, when son pursued him. Lord, hear my prayer; give ear to my supplication in your truth; hear me in your righteousness.

**Psalms 142:2**

And do not enter into judgment with your servant, because no living one will be justified before you.

**Psalms 142:3**

Because enemy pursued my soul; he humbled my life to earth; he seated me in dark places like dead of age.

**Psalms 142:4**

And my spirit grew weary upon me; within me my heart troubled.

**Psalms 142:5**

I remembered ancient days and meditated on all your works; in works of your hands I kept meditating.

**Psalms 142:6**

I spread out my hands to you; my soul as waterless land to you. Selah.

**Psalms 142:7**

Quickly hear me, Lord; my spirit failed. Do not turn away your face from me, and I will be likened to those going down into pit.

**Psalms 142:8**

Make your mercy heard to me in morning, because on you I hoped. Make known to me, Lord, way in which I should walk, because to you I lifted my soul.

**Psalms 142:9**

Rescue me from my enemies, Lord, because to you I fled.

**Psalms 142:10**

Teach me to do your will, because you my God. Your good spirit will guide me in straight land.

**Psalms 142:11**

For sake of your name, Lord, you will make me live; in your righteousness you will bring my soul out from affliction.

**Psalms 142:12**

And in your mercy you will utterly destroy my enemies and destroy all afflicting my soul, because I your servant.

### Chapter 143

**Psalms 143:1**

Of David, against Goliath. Blessed Lord my God, teaching my hands for battle, my fingers for war.

**Psalms 143:2**

My mercy and my refuge, my helper and my deliverer, my protector, and on him I hoped, one subduing my people under me.

**Psalms 143:3**

Lord, what man that you became known to him, or son of man that you count him?

**Psalms 143:4**

Man was likened to vanity; his days like passing shadow.

**Psalms 143:5**

Lord, bend your heavens and come down; touch mountains and they will smoke.

**Psalms 143:6**

Flash lightning and you will scatter them; send out your arrows and you will throw them into confusion.

**Psalms 143:7**

Send out your hand from height; rescue me and deliver me from many waters, from hand of foreign sons,

**Psalms 143:8**

whose mouth spoke vanity and their right hand right hand of injustice.

**Psalms 143:9**

God, I will sing new song to you; on ten-stringed psaltery I will sing psalms to you.

**Psalms 143:10**

To one giving salvation to kings, to one redeeming David his servant from evil sword.

**Psalms 143:11**

Rescue me and deliver me from hand of foreign sons, whose mouth spoke vanity and their right hand right hand of injustice.

**Psalms 143:12**

Whose sons like young shoots established in their youth; their daughters beautified, adorned like likeness of temple.

**Psalms 143:13**

Their storehouses full, pouring out from this into that; their sheep many-bearing, multiplying in their outings.

**Psalms 143:14**

Their oxen fat; no breach of wall, no passing out, no outcry in their squares.

**Psalms 143:15**

They called blessed people to whom these things belong; blessed people whose Lord their God.

### Chapter 144

**Psalms 144:1**

Praise of David. I will exalt you, my God, my king, and bless your name forever and forever of age.

**Psalms 144:2**

Each day I will bless you and praise your name forever and forever of age.

**Psalms 144:3**

Great Lord and greatly praiseworthy, and of his greatness no end.

**Psalms 144:4**

Generation and generation will praise your works, and they will declare your power.

**Psalms 144:5**

They will speak of magnificence of glory of your holiness, and they will relate your wonders.

**Psalms 144:6**

They will speak of power of your fearful deeds, and they will recount your greatness.

**Psalms 144:7**

They will pour forth memory of abundance of your kindness, and exult in your righteousness.

**Psalms 144:8**

Compassionate and merciful Lord, long-suffering and very merciful.

**Psalms 144:9**

Lord kind to all, and his compassions over all his works.

## Proverbs

### Chapter 1

**Proverbs 1:1**

Proverbs of Solomon son of David, who reigned in Israel.

**Proverbs 1:2**

To know wisdom and discipline, and to understand words of insight.

**Proverbs 1:3**

To receive turnings of words, and to understand true righteousness and judgment, and to direct judgment.

**Proverbs 1:4**

So that I may give shrewdness to innocent ones, and to child, young perception and understanding.

**Proverbs 1:5**

For hearing these, wise will become wiser, and understanding man will acquire guidance.

**Proverbs 1:6**

**Proverbs 1:7**

Beginning of wisdom fear of God; good understanding for all doing it; piety toward God beginning of perception, but wisdom and discipline ungodly will despise.

**Proverbs 1:8**

Hear, son, discipline of your father, and do not reject decrees of your mother.

**Proverbs 1:9**

For you will receive crown of graces for your head and golden chain around your neck.

**Proverbs 1:10**

Son, let ungodly men not lead you astray, nor be willing if they urge you, saying,

**Proverbs 1:11**

"Come with us, share blood; let us hide in earth righteous man unjustly.

**Proverbs 1:12**

Let us swallow him alive like Hades, and lift his memory from earth.

**Proverbs 1:13**

Let us seize his costly possession and fill our houses with spoils.

**Proverbs 1:14**

Throw your lot in among us; let us all get common purse, and let one pouch be among us."

**Proverbs 1:15**

Do not go in way with them; turn your foot away from their tracks.

**Proverbs 1:16**

For their feet run to evil and swift to pour out blood.

**Proverbs 1:17**

For not for nothing are nets spread for winged creatures.

**Proverbs 1:18**

For these sharing in murder store up evils for themselves, and destruction of lawless men evil.

**Proverbs 1:19**

These ways of all carrying out lawless things, for by ungodliness they take away their own soul.

**Proverbs 1:20**

Wisdom hymns in exits, and in broad places she leads boldness.

**Proverbs 1:21**

Upon heights of walls she is proclaimed, and beside gates of rulers she sits, and beside gates of city, speaking boldly, says,

**Proverbs 1:22**

"As long as innocent ones hold to righteousness, they will not be shamed; but fools, being desirers of insolence, becoming ungodly, hated perception.

**Proverbs 1:23**

And they became liable to rebukes. Behold, I will bring forth for you utterance of my spirit, and teach you my word.

**Proverbs 1:24**

Since I called and you did not heed, and I stretched out words and you did not attend,

**Proverbs 1:25**

but you kept making my counsels invalid, and to my rebukes disobeyed,

**Proverbs 1:26**

therefore I too will laugh at your ruin and rejoice when destruction comes to you,

**Proverbs 1:27**

and when sudden turmoil comes upon you, and downfall comes like storm, and when affliction and siege or destruction comes upon you.

**Proverbs 1:28**

For it will be when you call on me, I will not hear you; evil men will seek me and not find.

**Proverbs 1:29**

For they hated wisdom, and fear of Lord they did not choose.

**Proverbs 1:30**

Nor were they willing to heed my counsels, and they sneered at my rebukes.

**Proverbs 1:31**

Therefore they will eat fruits of their own way and be filled from their own ungodliness.

**Proverbs 1:32**

For because they wronged simple ones, they will be killed, and scrutiny destroys ungodly.

**Proverbs 1:33**

But one hearing me will settle in hope and rest fearless from every evil."

## Ecclesiastes

### Chapter 1

**Ecclesiastes 1:1**

Words of Ecclesiastes, son of David, king of Israel in Jerusalem.

**Ecclesiastes 1:2**

Vanity of vanities, said Ecclesiastes; vanity of vanities, all things vanity.

**Ecclesiastes 1:3**

What surplus for man in all his toil with which he toils under sun?

**Ecclesiastes 1:4**

Generation goes and generation comes, but earth stands into age.

**Ecclesiastes 1:5**

And sun rises and sun sets and draws to its place,

**Ecclesiastes 1:6**

rising there. It goes toward south and circles toward north; circling its circles the wind goes, and on its circles the wind returns.

**Ecclesiastes 1:7**

All torrents go into sea, yet sea will not be filled; to place where torrents go, there they return to go.

**Ecclesiastes 1:8**

All words are wearisome; man will not be able to speak, and eye will not be filled with seeing, nor ear filled from hearing.

**Ecclesiastes 1:9**

What happened, this will be what happens; and what has been done, this what will be done; and there is nothing fresh under sun.

**Ecclesiastes 1:10**

Who will speak and say, "Look, this is new"? It already happened in ages that came before us.

**Ecclesiastes 1:11**

There is no memory for first things, and even for last things that come there will be no memory for them with things yet to be at end.

**Ecclesiastes 1:12**

I, Ecclesiastes, became king over Israel in Jerusalem.

**Ecclesiastes 1:13**

And I gave my heart to seek out and to inspect in wisdom concerning all things happening under heaven, because evil distraction God gave to sons of man to be distracted in it.

**Ecclesiastes 1:14**

I saw all works done under sun, and look, all vanity and choice of spirit.

**Ecclesiastes 1:15**

What is twisted cannot be adorned, and what is lacking cannot be numbered.

**Ecclesiastes 1:16**

I spoke in my heart saying, "I, look, grew great and added wisdom above all who were before me in Jerusalem," and my heart saw much wisdom and knowledge.

**Ecclesiastes 1:17**

And I gave my heart to know wisdom and knowledge, parables and skill; I knew that this too is choice of spirit.

**Ecclesiastes 1:18**

Because in much wisdom much knowledge, and one adding knowledge will add pain.

### Chapter 2

**Ecclesiastes 2:1**

I said in my heart, "Come now, I will test you in gladness and see in good," and look, this too vanity.

**Ecclesiastes 2:2**

To laughter I said, "Madness," and to gladness, "What does this do?"

**Ecclesiastes 2:3**

I examined in my heart to draw my flesh into wine, and my heart led in wisdom, and to take hold upon folly until I should see what good for sons of men they will do under sun, number of days of their life.

**Ecclesiastes 2:4**

I magnified my work; I built houses for myself, I planted vineyards for myself.

**Ecclesiastes 2:5**

I made gardens and parks for myself, and planted in them every fruit tree.

**Ecclesiastes 2:6**

I made pools of waters for myself, to water from them forest sprouting trees.

**Ecclesiastes 2:7**

I acquired male servants and female servants, and home-born servants became mine; and much possession of herds and flocks became mine beyond all before me in Jerusalem.

**Ecclesiastes 2:8**

I gathered for myself also silver and gold and treasures of kings and provinces; I made for myself singers and singing women and delights of sons of men, cupbearer and cupbearers.

**Ecclesiastes 2:9**

And I grew great and increased beyond all before me in Jerusalem, and my wisdom stood by me.

**Ecclesiastes 2:10**

And all my eyes asked, I did not withhold from them; I did not restrain my heart from any gladness, because my heart rejoiced in all my toil, and this became my portion from all my toil.

**Ecclesiastes 2:11**

And I looked on all my works which my hands made and on toil in which I toiled to do, and look, all vanity and choice of spirit, and there is no surplus under sun.

**Ecclesiastes 2:12**

And I looked to see wisdom and wandering and folly, because what kind of man will come after counsel? The things it made.

**Ecclesiastes 2:13**

And I saw that wisdom has surplus over folly as surplus of light over darkness.

**Ecclesiastes 2:14**

Eyes of wise man in his head, but fool walks in darkness; and I knew, yes I, that one meeting meets them all.

**Ecclesiastes 2:15**

And I said in my heart, "As meeting of fool, so also to me it will meet; and why then did I become wise more?" I spoke in my heart that this too vanity, because fool speaks from surplus.

**Ecclesiastes 2:16**

For there is no memory of wise with fool forever, since already days coming all were forgotten; and how will wise die with fool?

**Ecclesiastes 2:17**

And I hated life, because evil to me was work done under sun, because all vanity and choice of spirit.

**Ecclesiastes 2:18**

And I hated all my toil with which I toil under sun, because I leave it to man coming after me.

**Ecclesiastes 2:19**

And who knows whether he will be wise or fool? Yet he rules over all my toil in which I toiled and became wise under sun; and this too vanity.

**Ecclesiastes 2:20**

And I turned to bid my heart farewell concerning all toil in which I toiled under sun.

**Ecclesiastes 2:21**

Because there is man whose toil is in wisdom and knowledge and courage, and to man who did not toil in it he will give his portion; and this too vanity and great evil.

**Ecclesiastes 2:22**

For what comes to man in all his toil and in choice of his heart in which he toils under sun?

**Ecclesiastes 2:23**

Because all his days are pains, and his distraction wrath; even in night his heart does not sleep, and this too vanity.

**Ecclesiastes 2:24**

There is no good in man except that he should eat and drink and show his soul good in his toil; and this too I saw, that it is from hand of God.

**Ecclesiastes 2:25**

For who will eat and who will spare apart from him?

**Ecclesiastes 2:26**

Because to the man who is good before him he gave wisdom and knowledge and gladness, but to the sinner he gave distraction, to add and to gather in order to give to one good before the face of God; because this too is vanity and choice of spirit.

### Chapter 3

**Ecclesiastes 3:1**

For all things time, and season for every matter under heaven.

**Ecclesiastes 3:2**

Time to bear and time to die; time to plant and time to pull up planted thing.

**Ecclesiastes 3:3**

Time to kill and time to heal; time to tear down and time to build.

**Ecclesiastes 3:4**

Time to weep and time to laugh; time to mourn and time to dance.

**Ecclesiastes 3:5**

Time to throw stones and time to gather stones; time to embrace and time to keep far from embracing.

**Ecclesiastes 3:6**

Time to seek and time to lose; time to keep and time to cast out.

**Ecclesiastes 3:7**

Time to tear and time to sew; time to be silent and time to speak.

**Ecclesiastes 3:8**

Time to love and time to hate; time of war and time of peace.

**Ecclesiastes 3:9**

What surplus to doer in things in which he toils?

**Ecclesiastes 3:10**

I saw distraction which God gave to sons of man to be distracted in it.

**Ecclesiastes 3:11**

Together he made all things beautiful in its time, and also together he gave age in their heart, so that man might not find work God made from beginning even to end.

**Ecclesiastes 3:12**

I knew there is no good in them except to rejoice and to do good in his life.

**Ecclesiastes 3:13**

And also every man who eats and drinks and sees good in all his toil, it is gift of God.

**Ecclesiastes 3:14**

I knew that all things whatever God made, these will be forever; on it there is nothing to add and from it nothing to take away, and God made it so that they may fear before his face.

**Ecclesiastes 3:15**

What came to be already is, and what is to come to be already happened, and God will seek what is pursued.

**Ecclesiastes 3:16**

And further I saw under sun place of judgment, there ungodly, and place of righteous, there ungodly.

**Ecclesiastes 3:17**

I said in my heart, "The righteous and the ungodly God will judge, because season for every matter and over every work."

**Ecclesiastes 3:18**

There I said in my heart about speech of sons of man, that God will sort them out and show that they are beasts, even they themselves.

**Ecclesiastes 3:19**

Because meeting of sons of man and meeting of beast, one meeting for them; as death of this one, so death of that one, and one spirit in all, and what did man have more than beast? Nothing, because all vanity.

**Ecclesiastes 3:20**

All go to one place; all became from dust, and all return to dust.

**Ecclesiastes 3:21**

And who knows whether spirit of sons of man goes upward, and spirit of beast goes down to earth?

**Ecclesiastes 3:22**

And I saw there is no good except that man will rejoice in his works, because this his portion; for who will bring him to see what will happen after him?

### Chapter 4

**Ecclesiastes 4:1**

**Ecclesiastes 4:2**

**Ecclesiastes 4:3**

**Ecclesiastes 4:6**

**Ecclesiastes 4:7**

And I turned and saw vanity under sun:

**Ecclesiastes 4:8**

**Ecclesiastes 4:9**

**Ecclesiastes 4:10**

**Ecclesiastes 4:11**

**Ecclesiastes 4:12**

**Ecclesiastes 6:7**

**Ecclesiastes 7:1**

**Ecclesiastes 7:4**

**Ecclesiastes 12:1**

## Song of Solomon

### Chapter 1

**Song of Solomon 1:1**

Song of songs, which is Solomon's.

**Song of Solomon 1:2**

Let him kiss me with kisses of his mouth, because your breasts are better than wine.

**Song of Solomon 1:3**

And scent of your perfumes above all spices; your name = poured-out perfume, therefore young women loved you.

**Song of Solomon 1:4**

They drew you; after you, into scent of your perfumes we will run. King brought me into his chamber. We will rejoice and be glad in you; we will love your breasts more than wine; the upright loved you.

**Song of Solomon 1:5**

Black I am and beautiful, daughters of Jerusalem, like tents of Kedar, like skins of Solomon.

**Song of Solomon 1:6**

Do not look at me because I am darkened, because sun looked past me. Sons of my mother fought in me; they set me keeping vineyards; my own vineyard I did not keep.

**Song of Solomon 1:7**

Tell me, you whom my soul loved, where do you shepherd, where do you rest at noon, lest I become as one veiled over flocks of your companions?

**Song of Solomon 1:8**

If you do not know yourself, beautiful among women, go out on heels of flocks and shepherd your young goats by tents of shepherds.

**Song of Solomon 1:9**

To my mare among chariots of Pharaoh I likened you, my dear one.

**Song of Solomon 1:10**

How beautiful your cheeks as turtledoves, your neck as necklaces.

**Song of Solomon 1:11**

We will make for you likenesses of gold with marks of silver.

**Song of Solomon 1:12**

Until king is at his recline, my nard gave its scent.

**Song of Solomon 1:13**

Bundle of myrrh my beloved to me; between my breasts he will lodge.

**Song of Solomon 1:14**

Cluster of cypress my beloved to me in vineyards of En-gedi.

**Song of Solomon 1:15**

Look, you are beautiful, my dear one, look, you are beautiful; your eyes doves.

**Song of Solomon 1:16**

Look, you are beautiful, my beloved, and indeed lovely; our bed shadowed.

**Song of Solomon 1:17**

Beams of our houses cedars, our rafters cypresses.

### Chapter 2

**Song of Solomon 2:1**

I = flower of field, lily of valleys.

**Song of Solomon 2:2**

As lily in midst of thorns, so my dear one in midst of daughters.

**Song of Solomon 2:3**

As an apple tree among trees of the grove, so my beloved in midst of sons. In his shadow I desired and sat, and his fruit was sweet to my palate.

**Song of Solomon 2:4**

Bring me into house of wine; arrange love upon me.

**Song of Solomon 2:5**

Strengthen me with perfumes, heap me with apples, because I am wounded by love.

**Song of Solomon 2:6**

His left under my head, and his right will embrace me.

**Song of Solomon 2:7**

I bound you by oath, daughters of Jerusalem, by powers and by strengths of field, that you not rouse and awaken love until it wishes.

**Song of Solomon 2:8**

Voice of my beloved. Look, he comes, leaping on mountains, springing on hills.

**Song of Solomon 2:9**

My beloved is like gazelle or fawn of deer on mountains of Bethel. Look, he stands behind our wall, peering through windows, looking through lattices.

**Song of Solomon 2:10**

My beloved answers and says to me, "Rise, come, my dear one, my beautiful one, my dove."

**Song of Solomon 2:11**

Because look, winter passed, rain departed, went away for itself.

**Song of Solomon 2:12**

Flowers appeared in land, time of pruning arrived, voice of turtledove was heard in our land.

**Song of Solomon 2:13**

Fig tree brought forth its early figs; vineyards in blossom gave scent. Rise, come, my dear one, my beautiful one, my dove.

**Song of Solomon 2:14**

And come, my dove, in shelter of rock, close to the forewall; show me your face and let me hear your voice, because your voice sweet and your face beautiful.

**Song of Solomon 2:15**

Catch for us foxes, little foxes destroying vineyards, and our vineyards are blossoming.

**Song of Solomon 2:16**

My beloved to me, and I to him, the one shepherding among lilies.

**Song of Solomon 2:17**

Until day breathes and shadows move, turn back; be like, my beloved, a gazelle or fawn of deer on cleft mountains.

### Chapter 3

**Song of Solomon 3:1**

On my bed by nights I sought the one my soul loved; I sought him and did not find him; I called him and he did not answer me.

**Song of Solomon 3:2**

I will rise now and circle in city, in markets and squares, and seek one my soul loved; I sought him and did not find him.

**Song of Solomon 3:3**

**Song of Solomon 3:4**

Scarcely when I passed from them, until I found one my soul loved. I seized him and will not let him go until I brought him into house of my mother and into chamber of one who conceived me.

**Song of Solomon 3:5**

I bound you by oath, daughters of Jerusalem, by powers and by strengths of field, that you not rouse and awaken love until it wishes.

**Song of Solomon 3:6**

Who is this coming up from wilderness like columns of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, from all powders of perfumer?

**Song of Solomon 3:7**

Look, Solomon's couch: sixty mighty men around it, from mighty men of Israel.

**Song of Solomon 3:8**

All holding sword, trained in war, each man his sword on his thigh from terrors in nights.

**Song of Solomon 3:9**

King Solomon made for himself litter from woods of Lebanon.

**Song of Solomon 3:10**

He made its pillars silver and its recliner gold, its seat purple, its inside paved with love from daughters of Jerusalem.

**Song of Solomon 3:11**

Come out and see in King Solomon, with crown with which his mother crowned him in day of his wedding and in day of gladness of his heart.

### Chapter 4

**Song of Solomon 4:1**

Look, you beautiful, my dear one, look, you beautiful; your eyes doves behind your veil. Your hair like herds of goats that were revealed from Gilead.

**Song of Solomon 4:2**

Your teeth like herd of shorn sheep that came up from washing, all bearing twins, and barren one not among them.

**Song of Solomon 4:3**

As scarlet cord your lips, and your speech beautiful; as piece of pomegranate your cheek behind your veil.

**Song of Solomon 4:4**

As tower of David your neck, built for ranks; thousand shields hang upon it, all darts of mighty men.

**Song of Solomon 4:5**

Your two breasts like two fawns, twins of gazelle, grazing among lilies.

**Song of Solomon 4:6**

Until day breathes and shadows move, I will go for myself to mountain of myrrh and hill of frankincense.

**Song of Solomon 4:7**

All beautiful you, my dear one, and blemish not in you.

**Song of Solomon 4:8**

Come from Lebanon, bride, come from Lebanon; you will come and pass from summit of Faith, from top of Senir and Hermon, from dens of lions, from mountains of leopards.

**Song of Solomon 4:9**

You heartened us, my sister bride, you heartened us with one of your eyes, with one chain of your neck.

**Song of Solomon 4:10**

How beautiful your breasts, my sister bride; how beautiful your breasts beyond wine, and scent of your garments above all spices.

**Song of Solomon 4:11**

Honeycomb drips from your lips, bride; honey and milk under your tongue, and scent of your garments as scent of Lebanon.

**Song of Solomon 4:12**

Garden shut, my sister bride; garden shut, spring sealed.

**Song of Solomon 4:13**

Your shoots = orchard of pomegranates with fruit of choice things, cypresses with nards.

**Song of Solomon 4:14**

Nard and saffron, cane and cinnamon with all woods of Lebanon, myrrh and aloes with all first perfumes.

**Song of Solomon 4:15**

Spring of gardens, well of living water and rushing from Lebanon.

**Song of Solomon 4:16**

Awake, north, and come, south. Breathe through my garden, and let my perfumes flow. Let my beloved go down into his garden and eat fruit of his choice things.

### Chapter 5

**Song of Solomon 5:1**

I entered my garden, my sister bride; I gathered my myrrh with my spices; I ate my bread with my honey, I drank my wine with my milk. Eat, companions, and drink and be drunk, brothers.

**Song of Solomon 5:2**

I sleep, and my heart wakes. Voice of my beloved knocks at door: "Open to me, my sister, my dear one, my dove, my perfect one, because my head filled with dew and my locks with drops of night."

**Song of Solomon 5:3**

I stripped my tunic; how shall I put it on? I washed my feet; how shall I soil them?

**Song of Solomon 5:4**

My beloved sent his hand through opening, and my inward parts trembled for him.

**Song of Solomon 5:5**

I rose, I, to open to my beloved; my hands dripped myrrh, my fingers full myrrh upon handles of lock.

**Song of Solomon 5:6**

I opened, I, to my beloved; my beloved passed by. My soul went out at his word. I sought him and did not find him; I called him and he did not answer me.

**Song of Solomon 5:7**

Watchmen found me, those circling in city. They struck me, they wounded me; watchers of walls took my veil from me.

**Song of Solomon 5:8**

I bound you by oath, daughters of Jerusalem, by powers and strengths of field, if you find my beloved, what will you report to him? That I am wounded by love.

**Song of Solomon 5:9**

What is your beloved beyond beloved, beautiful among women? What is your beloved beyond beloved, that thus you bound us by oath?

**Song of Solomon 5:10**

My beloved white and ruddy, singled out from myriads.

**Song of Solomon 5:11**

His head gold and fine gold; his curls like palm branches, black as raven.

**Song of Solomon 5:12**

His eyes like doves by fillings of waters, washed in milk, sitting by fullness of waters.

**Song of Solomon 5:13**

His cheeks like bowls of spice, growing perfumes; his lips lilies dripping full myrrh.

**Song of Solomon 5:14**

His hands gold-carved, filled with Tarshish; his belly ivory box on sapphire stone.

**Song of Solomon 5:15**

His legs marble pillars founded on gold bases; his appearance like Lebanon, choice as cedars.

**Song of Solomon 5:16**

His throat sweetness, and he whole = desire. This my beloved and this my dear one, daughters of Jerusalem.

### Chapter 6

**Song of Solomon 6:1**

Where did your beloved go, beautiful among women? Where did your beloved look away, and we will seek him with you?

**Song of Solomon 6:2**

My beloved went down into his garden, into bowls of spice, to shepherd in gardens and gather lilies.

**Song of Solomon 6:3**

I to my beloved, and my beloved to me, one shepherding among lilies.

**Song of Solomon 6:4**

Beautiful you, my dear one, as Delight; lovely as Jerusalem; awe as battle-lines.

**Song of Solomon 6:5**

Turn your eyes from before me, because they gave me wings. Your hair like herds of goats that appeared from Gilead.

**Song of Solomon 6:6**

Your teeth like herd of shorn sheep that came up from washing, all bearing twins, and barren one not among them.

**Song of Solomon 6:7**

As scarlet cord your lips, and your speech beautiful; as piece of pomegranate your cheek behind your veil.

**Song of Solomon 6:8**

Sixty queens and eighty concubines and maidens without number.

**Song of Solomon 6:9**

One is my dove, my perfect one; one to her mother, chosen to one who bore her. Daughters saw her and will bless her; queens and concubines, and they will praise her.

**Song of Solomon 6:10**

Who is this looking forth as dawn, beautiful as moon, chosen as sun, awe as battle-lines?

**Song of Solomon 6:11**

Into garden of walnut I went down, to see among produce of torrent, to see whether vine blossomed, pomegranates bloomed. There I will give my breasts to you.

**Song of Solomon 6:12**

My soul did not know; it set me among chariots of Amminadab.

### Chapter 7

**Song of Solomon 7:1**

Return, return, Shulammite; return, return, and we will look on you. What will you see in Shulammite? She comes as dances of camps.

**Song of Solomon 7:2**

How beautiful your steps in sandals, daughter of Nadab. Curves of your thighs like necklaces, work of hands of craftsman.

**Song of Solomon 7:3**

Your navel a carved bowl, not lacking mixed wine; your belly heap of wheat fenced round with lilies.

**Song of Solomon 7:4**

Your two breasts like two twin fawns of gazelle.

**Song of Solomon 7:5**

Your neck as ivory tower. Your eyes as pools in Heshbon at gates of daughter of multitudes. Your nose as tower of Lebanon watching face of Damascus.

**Song of Solomon 7:6**

Your head upon you as Carmel, and braid of your head as purple; king bound in flowing locks.

**Song of Solomon 7:7**

How beautiful you became, and how sweet, love, in your delights.

**Song of Solomon 7:8**

This your stature was likened to palm tree, and your breasts to clusters.

**Song of Solomon 7:9**

I said, I will climb the palm tree, I will seize its heights; and now let your breasts be as clusters of vine, and scent of your nose as apples.

**Song of Solomon 7:10**

And your throat as good wine, going to my beloved in straightness, fitted to my lips and teeth.

**Song of Solomon 7:11**

I to my beloved, and upon me his turning.

**Song of Solomon 7:12**

Come, my beloved, let us go out into field, let us lodge in villages.

**Song of Solomon 7:13**

Let us rise early to vineyards; let us see whether vine blossomed, cypress blossomed, pomegranates bloomed. There I will give my breasts to you.

**Song of Solomon 7:14**

Mandrakes gave scent, and at our doors every choice fruit, new with old, my beloved, I kept for you.

### Chapter 8

**Song of Solomon 8:1**

Who will give you as my beloved, nursing breasts of my mother? Finding you outside I will kiss you, and indeed they will not despise me.

**Song of Solomon 8:2**

I will take you, I will bring you into house of my mother and into chamber of one who conceived me. I will give you drink from perfumed wine, from juice of my pomegranates.

**Song of Solomon 8:3**

His left under my head, and his right will embrace me.

**Song of Solomon 8:4**

I bound you by oath, daughters of Jerusalem, by powers and by strengths of field: why do you rouse and why do you awaken love until it wishes?

**Song of Solomon 8:5**

Who is this coming up whitened, leaning on her beloved? Under apple tree I awakened you; there your mother travailed with you, there she travailed, the one who bore you.

**Song of Solomon 8:6**

Set me as seal on your heart, as seal on your arm, because love strong as death, jealousy hard as Hades; its wings = wings of fire, its flames.

**Song of Solomon 8:7**

Much water will not be able to quench love, and rivers will not flood it. If man gives all his livelihood in love, despising they will despise him.

**Song of Solomon 8:8**

Small sister to us, and she has no breasts. What shall we do for our sister in day when they speak in her?

**Song of Solomon 8:9**

If she is wall, we will build upon her battlements of silver; and if she is door, we will engrave upon her cedar board.

**Song of Solomon 8:10**

I wall, and my breasts as towers. I became in his eyes as one finding peace.

**Song of Solomon 8:11**

Vineyard came to Solomon in Baal-hamon. He gave his vineyard to keepers; each man will bring in its fruit a thousand of silver.

**Song of Solomon 8:12**

My vineyard mine before me. Thousand to you, Solomon, and two hundred to those keeping its fruit.

**Song of Solomon 8:13**

You sitting in gardens, companions attending to your voice, let me hear.

**Song of Solomon 8:14**

Flee, my beloved, and be like gazelle or fawn of deer on mountains of spices.

## Isaiah

### Chapter 1

**Isaiah 1:1**

Vision which Isaiah son of Amoz saw, which he saw against Judah and against Jerusalem in reign of Uzziah and Jotham and Ahaz and Hezekiah, who reigned over Judah.

**Isaiah 1:2**

Hear, heaven, and give ear, earth, because Lord spoke: Sons I begot and raised high, but they rejected me.

**Isaiah 1:3**

Ox knew one acquiring it, and donkey manger of its master; but Israel did not know me, and people did not understand me.

**Isaiah 1:4**

Woe, sinful nation, people full of sins, evil seed, lawless sons. You abandoned Lord and provoked Holy One of Israel.

**Isaiah 1:5**

Why still be struck, adding lawlessness? Every head into pain and every heart into grief.

**Isaiah 1:6**

From feet to head neither wound nor bruise nor burning stripe; there is no salve to apply, nor oil, nor bandages.

**Isaiah 1:7**

Your land desolate, your cities burned with fire; your country before you foreigners devour it, and it has been desolated, overthrown by foreign peoples.

**Isaiah 1:8**

Daughter of Zion will be left as tent in vineyard, and as watch-hut in cucumber patch, as city under siege.

**Isaiah 1:9**

Unless Lord Sabaoth had left us seed, we would have become as Sodom and been made like Gomorrah.

**Isaiah 1:10**

Hear word of Lord, rulers of Sodom; heed law of God, people of Gomorrah.

**Isaiah 1:11**

What to me multitude of your sacrifices, says Lord? I am full of whole burnt offerings of rams and fat of lambs, and blood of bulls and goats I do not want.

**Isaiah 1:12**

Not even when you come to appear to me. For who sought these from your hands, to trample my court?

**Isaiah 1:13**

You will not continue. If you bring fine flour, it is vain; incense = abomination to me. Your new moons and Sabbaths and great day I do not endure, fasting and idleness.

**Isaiah 1:14**

Your new moons and your feasts my soul hates; you became fullness to me; no longer will I pardon your sins.

**Isaiah 1:15**

When you stretch out hands to me, I will turn my eyes from you; and if you multiply supplication, I will not hear you, because your hands full of blood.

**Isaiah 1:16**

Wash, become clean, remove evils from your souls before my eyes; stop from your evils.

**Isaiah 1:17**

Learn to do good, seek judgment, rescue one being wronged, judge for orphan, justify widow.

**Isaiah 1:18**

Come and let us reason together, says Lord. And if your sins are as scarlet, I will whiten as snow; if they are as crimson, I will whiten as wool.

**Isaiah 1:19**

If you are willing and listen to me, good things of land you will eat.

**Isaiah 1:20**

If not willing nor listen to me, sword will devour you, for mouth of Lord spoke these things.

**Isaiah 1:21**

How faithful city Zion became prostitute, full of judgment, in which righteousness slept, but now murderers.

**Isaiah 1:22**

Your silver unapproved, your tavern-keepers mix wine with water.

**Isaiah 1:23**

Your rulers disobey, companions of thieves, loving gifts, pursuing repayment; not judging orphans and not attending to widow's case.

**Isaiah 1:24**

Therefore thus says Master, Lord Sabaoth, Woe to mighty ones of Israel. For my anger will not cease against opponents, and I will execute judgment against my enemies.

**Isaiah 1:25**

I will bring my hand upon you and purge you into purity, but rebellious ones I will destroy; and I will remove all lawless ones from you and humble all proud ones.

**Isaiah 1:26**

I will appoint your judges as before, and your counselors as from beginning; afterward you will be called city of righteousness, faithful mother-city Zion.

**Isaiah 1:27**

For her captivity will be saved with judgment, and with mercy.

**Isaiah 1:28**

Lawless and sinners will be shattered together, and those abandoning Lord will be finished.

**Isaiah 1:29**

Because they will be ashamed over their idols which they wanted, and they were put to shame over their gardens they desired.

**Isaiah 1:30**

For they will be as terebinth that has cast off leaves, and as orchard having no water.

**Isaiah 1:31**

Their strength will be as stalk of tow and their works as sparks of fire, and lawless and sinners will be burned together, and there will not be one to quench.

### Chapter 2

**Isaiah 2:1**

The word that came from Lord to Isaiah son of Amoz concerning Judah and concerning Jerusalem.

**Isaiah 2:2**

Because in last days mountain of Lord and house of God will be manifest on peaks of mountains, and will be lifted above hills, and all nations will come upon it.

**Isaiah 2:3**

Many nations will go and say, Come, let us go up to mountain of Lord and to house of God of Jacob, and he will announce his way to us, and we will walk in it. For from Zion law will come out, and word of Lord from Jerusalem.

**Isaiah 2:4**

He will judge between nations and reprove many people, and they will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into sickles; nation will not take sword against nation anymore, and they will certainly not learn war anymore.

**Isaiah 2:5**

And now, house of Jacob, come, let us walk in light of Lord.

**Isaiah 2:6**

For he let go his people, house of Israel, because their land was filled as from beginning with divinations as land of foreigners, and many foreign sons were born to them.

**Isaiah 2:7**

Their land filled with silver and gold, and there was no number of their treasures, and land filled with horses, and there was no number of their chariots.

**Isaiah 2:8**

Their land filled with abominations, works of their hands, and they bowed to what their fingers made.

**Isaiah 2:9**

Man bent down, and male was humbled, and I will certainly not let them go.

**Isaiah 2:10**

And now enter rocks and hide in earth from face of fear of Lord and from glory of his strength when he rises to shatter earth.

**Isaiah 2:11**

For eyes of Lord high, but man low, and height of men will be humbled, and Lord alone will be exalted in that day.

**Isaiah 2:12**

For day of Lord Sabaoth upon every insolent and proud one, and upon every high and lofty thing, and they will be humbled.

**Isaiah 2:13**

And upon every cedar of Lebanon, high and lofty, and upon every oak tree of Bashan.

**Isaiah 2:14**

And upon every mountain and every high hill.

**Isaiah 2:15**

And upon every high tower and every high wall.

**Isaiah 2:16**

And upon every ship of sea and upon every sight of beauty of ships.

**Isaiah 2:17**

Every man will be humbled and height of men will fall, and Lord alone will be exalted in that day.

**Isaiah 2:18**

All handmade things they will utterly hide.

**Isaiah 2:19**

Carrying them into caves and fissures of rocks and hollows of earth from face of fear of Lord and from glory of his strength when he rises to shatter earth.

**Isaiah 2:20**

For in that day man will throw out his silver and gold abominations, which they made to bow to vanities and night-creatures.

**Isaiah 2:21**

To enter hollows of solid rock and fissures of rocks from face of fear of Lord and from glory of his strength when he rises to shatter earth.

### Chapter 3

**Isaiah 3:1**

Look now, Master Lord Sabaoth will take from Judah and Jerusalem strong man and strong woman, strength of bread and strength of water,

**Isaiah 3:2**

giant and strong man and man of war, and judge and prophet and diviner and elder,

**Isaiah 3:3**

and captain of fifty and wonderful counselor and wise craftsman and understanding listener.

**Isaiah 3:4**

I will appoint youths their rulers, and mockers will lord over them.

**Isaiah 3:5**

People will fall together, man against man and man against his neighbor; child will strike against elder, dishonorable one against honorable.

**Isaiah 3:6**

Because man will seize his brother or one of his father's household, saying, You have clothing, become our leader, and let my food be under you.

**Isaiah 3:7**

He will answer and say in that day, I will not be your leader, for in my house there is neither bread nor clothing; I will not be leader of this people.

**Isaiah 3:8**

Because Jerusalem is abandoned and Judah has fallen, and their tongues with lawlessness speak things against Lord, disobeying, because now their glory was humbled.

**Isaiah 3:9**

Shame of their face stood against them, and their sin they announced as Sodom and made it plain. Woe to their soul, because they planned evil counsel against themselves.

**Isaiah 3:10**

Saying, Let us bind righteous one, because he is inconvenient to us; therefore they will eat produce of their works.

**Isaiah 3:11**

Woe to lawless one; evil will happen to him according to works of his hands.

**Isaiah 3:12**

My people, your exactors glean you, and those collecting dues lord over you. My people, those calling you blessed lead you astray and trouble path of your feet.

**Isaiah 3:13**

But now Lord will stand for judgment and stand to judge his people.

**Isaiah 3:14**

Lord himself will come into judgment with elders of his people and with their rulers: But you, why did you burn my vineyard, and spoil of poor in your houses?

**Isaiah 3:15**

Why do you wrong my people and shame face of poor?

**Isaiah 3:16**

Thus says Lord: Because daughters of Zion were lifted high and walked with high neck and with winks of eyes and in walking of feet dragging tunics together and playing together with feet,

**Isaiah 3:17**

God will humble ruling daughters of Zion, and Lord will uncover their form.

**Isaiah 3:18**

In that day Lord will take away glory of their clothing and their ornaments and braids and hair-nets and crescent-moons,

**Isaiah 3:19**

and the hangings and ornament of their face,

**Isaiah 3:20**

and arrangement of ornament of glory and bracelets and armlets and headdress and wrist-bands and rings and earrings,

**Isaiah 3:21**

and purple garments and garments bordered in purple,

**Isaiah 3:22**

and robes for house and transparent Laconian cloths,

**Isaiah 3:23**

and fine linen and blue and scarlet and linen woven together with gold and blue, and reclining veils.

**Isaiah 3:24**

It will be, instead of sweet smell = dust, and instead of belt you will bind with rope, and instead of golden ornament of head you will have baldness because of your works, and instead of tunic bordered in purple you will gird yourself with sackcloth.

**Isaiah 3:25**

Your most beautiful son whom you love will fall by sword, and your mighty men will fall by sword.

**Isaiah 3:26**

Cases of your ornament will be humbled and mourn, and you will be left alone and dashed to ground.

### Chapter 4

**Isaiah 4:1**

Seven women will seize one man, saying, We will eat our bread and wear our clothes; only let your name be called upon us; take away our reproach.

**Isaiah 4:2**

In that day God will shine forth in counsel with glory upon earth, to lift up and glorify remnant of Israel.

**Isaiah 4:3**

It shall be that one left in Zion and one left in Jerusalem will be called holy, all written for life in Jerusalem.

**Isaiah 4:4**

Because Lord will wash filth of sons and daughters of Zion and cleanse blood from their midst by spirit of judgment and spirit of burning.

**Isaiah 4:5**

He will come and there will be over every place of Mount Zion and all around her a cloud will overshadow by day, like smoke, and like light of burning fire by night. Over all glory it will be covered.

**Isaiah 4:6**

And it will be for shade from heat and for shelter and hiding from harshness and rain.

### Chapter 5

**Isaiah 5:1**

Now I will sing to my beloved song of my beloved concerning my vineyard. Vineyard came to my beloved on hilltop in fertile place.

**Isaiah 5:2**

I put fence around and staked it and planted chosen vine and built tower in midst of it and dug wine-vat in it, and I waited for it to produce grapes, but it produced thorns.

**Isaiah 5:3**

And now, man of Judah and dwellers in Jerusalem, judge between me and my vineyard.

**Isaiah 5:4**

What shall I still do to my vineyard that I did not do to it? Because I waited for it to produce grapes, but it produced thorns.

**Isaiah 5:5**

And now I will announce to you what I will do to my vineyard: I will remove its fence and it will be for plundering, and I will pull down its wall and it will be for trampling.

**Isaiah 5:6**

And I will leave my vineyard, and it shall certainly not be pruned nor dug, and thorns will come up upon it as upon wasteland, and I will command clouds not to rain rain on it.

**Isaiah 5:7**

For vineyard of Lord Sabaoth = house of Israel, and man of Judah beloved new planting. I waited for judgment, but it produced lawlessness, and not righteousness but cry.

**Isaiah 5:8**

Woe those joining house to house and bringing field near to field, to take something from neighbor away; will you not dwell alone on land?

**Isaiah 5:9**

For these things were heard in ears of Lord Sabaoth: if many houses shall become, they will be desolate, great and beautiful, and there will not be ones dwelling in them.

**Isaiah 5:10**

For ten yoke of oxen working will produce one jar, and one sowing six artabas will produce three measures.

**Isaiah 5:11**

Woe those rising early and pursuing strong drink, those remaining till late, for wine will burn them together.

**Isaiah 5:12**

For with lyre and psaltery and drums and flutes they drink wine, but works of Lord they do not look on, and works of his hands they do not understand.

**Isaiah 5:13**

Therefore my people became captive because they did not know Lord, and multitude became dead from famine and thirst of water.

**Isaiah 5:14**

And Hades widened its soul and opened its mouth without ceasing, and her glorious ones and great ones and rich ones and her plague-struck ones will go down.

**Isaiah 5:15**

And man will be humbled and male will be dishonored, and lofty eyes will be humbled.

**Isaiah 5:16**

And the Lord Sabaoth will be exalted in judgment, and the Holy God will be glorified in righteousness.

**Isaiah 5:17**

And plundered ones will be grazed as bulls, and lambs will eat deserted places of those taken away.

**Isaiah 5:18**

Woe those drawing sins with long rope and lawlessness as with strap of heifer's yoke,

**Isaiah 5:19**

those saying, Let what he will do come quickly and draw near, that we may see; and let counsel of Holy One of Israel come, that we may know.

**Isaiah 5:20**

Woe those saying evil good and good evil, those putting darkness light and light darkness, those putting bitter sweet and sweet bitter.

**Isaiah 5:21**

Woe those understanding in themselves and knowledgeable before themselves.

**Isaiah 5:22**

Woe your mighty men, drinkers of wine, and rulers mixing strong drink,

**Isaiah 5:23**

those justifying ungodly for gifts and taking away right of righteous.

**Isaiah 5:24**

Therefore as stubble will be burned under coal of fire and be consumed under loose flame, their root will be as down and their blossom will go up as dust, because they did not want law of Lord Sabaoth but provoked oracle of Holy One of Israel.

**Isaiah 5:25**

And Lord Sabaoth was enraged in anger against his people, and he laid his hand on them and struck them and mountains were provoked, and their corpses became as dung in midst of road. In all these his anger did not turn away, but hand still high.

**Isaiah 5:26**

Therefore he will raise signal among nations far off and whistle to them from end of earth, and look, swiftly lightly they come.

**Isaiah 5:27**

They will neither hunger nor grow weary nor grow drowsy nor sleep, nor loosen their belts from their waist, nor will straps of their sandals break.

**Isaiah 5:28**

Whose arrows are sharp and their bows bent; feet of their horses were reckoned as solid rock, wheels of their chariots as storm.

**Isaiah 5:29**

They will rush as lions and stand by as lion's whelp, and will seize and roar as beast and cast out, and there will not be one rescuing.

**Isaiah 5:30**

And it will roar because of them in that day as sound of surging sea, and they will look to land, and look, hard darkness in their distress.

### Chapter 6

**Isaiah 6:1**

And it happened in year king Uzziah died, I saw Lord sitting on high and lifted throne, and house full of his glory.

**Isaiah 6:2**

And seraphim stood around him; six wings to one and six wings to one; with two they covered face, and with two they covered feet, and with two they flew.

**Isaiah 6:3**

And one cried to another and said, Holy, holy, holy, Lord Sabaoth; whole earth full of his glory.

**Isaiah 6:4**

And lintel was raised from voice with which they cried, and house was filled with smoke.

**Isaiah 6:5**

And I said, O wretched me, because I am pierced to heart, because being man and having unclean lips and dwelling in midst of people having unclean lips, I saw king Lord Sabaoth with my eyes.

**Isaiah 6:6**

And one of seraphim was sent to me, and in hand he had coal which he took with tongs from altar.

**Isaiah 6:7**

And he touched my mouth and said, Behold, this touched your lips, and it will take away your lawlessness and cleanse your sins.

**Isaiah 6:8**

And I heard voice of Lord saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go to this people? And I said, Behold, I am here; send me.

**Isaiah 6:9**

And he said, Go and say to this people: hearing you will hear and certainly not understand, and looking you will look and certainly not see.

**Isaiah 6:10**

For heart of this people grew fat, and with their ears they heard heavily, and their eyes they closed, lest they see with eyes and hear with ears and understand with heart and turn, and I heal them.

**Isaiah 6:11**

And I said, Until when, Lord? And he said, Until cities are made desolate from not being inhabited, and houses from not having men, and land will be left desolate.

**Isaiah 6:12**

And after these things God will send men far away, and those left behind will multiply on earth.

**Isaiah 6:13**

And yet upon it still = the tenth, and again it will be for plundering, like terebinth and like oak whenever it falls from its casing.

### Chapter 7

**Isaiah 7:1**

And it happened in days of Ahaz son of Jotham son of Uzziah king of Judah, Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel went up against Jerusalem to war against it, and they were not able to besiege it.

**Isaiah 7:2**

And it was reported to house of David, saying, Aram agreed with Ephraim, and his soul and soul of his people were stirred as when tree in forest is shaken by wind.

**Isaiah 7:3**

And Lord said to Isaiah, Go out to meet Ahaz, you and Shear-jashub your son, to pool of upper road of fuller's field.

**Isaiah 7:4**

And you will say to him, Take care to be quiet and do not fear, nor let your soul weaken from these two pieces of smoking firebrands, for whenever anger of my wrath comes, again I will heal.

**Isaiah 7:5**

And son of Aram and son of Remaliah, because they counseled evil counsel about you, saying,

**Isaiah 7:6**

**Isaiah 7:21**

**Isaiah 7:22**

**Isaiah 10:1**
